records.script: This robot does almost everything itself. From autonomous mode to swing notes, this machine is extremely intelligent. With human parts added, it would be a cyborg. Team 4256, Cyborg Cats!!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team knows the note would sound best deposited in the amp. They always had a handy thumb on their bot and only one hook in the air. Congratulations to Team 2481, The Roboteers!!

This team built a robust, fast and impressive robot using a custom feedback dashboard that talked back. You can hear this voice say if there an on-field failure. So, listen for Karen, announcing to watch out!
This team has shared the love across the web to exchange ideas and advice to all that join them. They pay homage to those that rolled before them. They leave the competition green with envy!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When Ian Malcom brought up "Chaos Theory" he was talking about them. From custom shopped parts to matching uniforms, this team's "look" made all of eyes pop. When it came to aesthetics, this team went lean, mean and GREEN. Let's give it up for team 931!!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Striking a balance between form, function and aesthetics - this team used simulations to stress the bot. Great vibrations and bright lights is a great way to celebrate Team 5557!

The modular design of this robot helped them climb high to catch the judges' attention and their hooks latched onto the chain to seal the deal. Using the spring loaded hooks, and a large number of LEDs to provide their driver clear feedback on their status. This Tennessee team knows that green means they're good to shoot.

The tank drive steered this team towards success. As they looked at their home country, they realized the young teams needed a way to scout and learn strategy in order to excel. This team developed a little magic and compiled it into a scouting app.

This well-made robot stands out among the others. Using their swerve drive and field-oriented driving, this beautiful robot did easily rise to the top highlands of the competition. They go by their call sign...Sundown.
This team's outreach was more than just robotics. Their global reach not only educates, but lifts up communities in need. This revolutionary group has inspired a buffet of STEM fun.

The music of this team has inspired high school and college acceptance rates of 100%. With 90% of these artists pursuing STEAM fields. Their team harmony was forged and Hacked into a Road where innovation in recruiting via social outreach project forming has drawn over 1000 members from 30+ schools. A roar that reaches 74 zip codes (5 countries) spanning over 90+ event in 3 year time in their communities. This team has a choir that sings to spread their roar of knowledge to areas of personal security, medical therapy as well as water resource and availability. Please help us sing congratulations for this year's Rocket City Regional FIRST Impact Award winner, team 6652 Tigres from Monterrey, Nuevo Leon, Mexico.

This award honors the team which, although young, shows strength in helping students learn about science and technology. It is hard to "fathom" how far one team has come in establishing these partnerships. Please congratulate Team 9787.
They might be new, but they've cinched a sweet victory. We were inspired by their outreach, engagement and their cool hats. Let's give a warm "Oompa Loompa Doompity Doo" for...PURE IMAGINATION

As we soar through the skies of innovation and teamwork, it is time to recognize a group that has truly launched themselves into the stratosphere of camaraderie. They've proven that when it comes to synergy, they're not just reaching for the stars, they are the stars. So, without further ado, lets give a cosmic round of applause to the team that embodies the true spirit of teamwork and sportsmanship, THE ROCKETS!!!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Even though there are rough waters ahead, this team is ready to weather the storm with a commitment to environmental and team sustainability, it's all hands on deck. We know they'll go for a full steam ahead. The "Flagship"!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division

From their series of short stories, to their robotics kits and their in-school partnerships, this team is FIN-tastic. Their eco-focused STEM initiatives are are what really got a huge REACTION from the judges. They won’t be-REFF it but Drift it

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team’s design process was a breath of fresh air. They put the PETAL to the metal with comprehensive planning and rigorous prototyping to design for both game advantage and team strengths. They certainly won’t be pushing up any daisies in this competition.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team has been a beacon for FIRST in their small town community. Their mission was to spread a spectrum of knowledge across the globe for FREE. Their 3-phase program to spread ASD awareness was an AUTO-matic success.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team grabbed our attention with their unified approach. Their children’s book series have really cooked up a storm. The judges couldn’t pasta up this rookie team

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division

records.script: End to end, top to bottom, this team’s robot was well-built and robust. They certainly won’t be having any MELTDOWNS in this competition.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team took control systems feedback and troubleshooting to the next level. Their creative and well-executed use of LED displays for feedback and status monitoring on and off the field really made a BANG with the judges. In particular, their drivetrain monitoring system, which helped FUSE maintenance and functionality, BLEW our minds.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team bonds with books, coding free meals and more. Their knitting and heart of a robot helped families made homeless after the shaking stopped. With a flare, new braille legos will soon be there.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team MARCHES to the beat of a redundant drum. Their robust contingency planning left no part or subsystem behind. And they aren’t TOYing around as they STEALTHILY soldier to the field.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team’s innovative STEAM intiatives, legislative collaboration and incredible branding make them the deserving winner. Like a recently hatched egg, they are just beginning to crack the suface of their potential. With their determination and spirit, they are not just chicks, but full-fledged chickens ready to soar to new heights!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team shines as a beacon of STEAM, blending tech with art through their collaborations with artists. They are dedicated in their classes and when they are volunteering at events. The judges had to highlight these shining junios from the great white north.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: With unparalleled enthusiasm and firey zeal, this team champions safety in their community. Their unicorns bring a touch of magic and free fistbumps to anyone they meet. If you need Pluggy, he’ll be right there, Pronto!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team’s robot is powered by the sun. They created a sustainability toolkit, translated into 5 languages. Their island community thanks their positive carbon contributions.

This team showed right at the start their ability to hit multiple notes during autonomous mode. Their consistency and reliability truly helped them rise above the competition. Even without having the drivers direct the robot, the robot always knew exactly what to do in a new frontier. Congratulations, Team number 7525.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Creativity Award This robot is able to take notes from all sides and score without help. These Cajuns heat up the competition and frustrate their opponents by moving quickly and hitting their target. Congratulations, Team Number 8044.

The design and delegation of every aspect of the build are vital in today’s engineering climate. Designing every aspect of functionality is critical but this team’s design is elegant, efficient and very effective. This team has gone above and beyond with their ability to communicate with their robot as you can see what’s going on with their robot from a mile away. Whether it’s diffusing situations or blowing the competition away, this team has excelled in all aspects of the competition. Congratulations, Team number 16, Bomb Squad.

When other teams asked for help, this team was the queen of the hill. They swarmed the occasion to spread STEM and robotics to their community and beyond. Stand at attention for the winners of the Gracious Professionalism Award. Congratulations, Team number 3792.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The imagery award is in honor of Jack Kamen, Dean’s Father, for his dedication to art, illustration, and his devotion to FIRST. This aware celebrates attractiveness in engineering and outstanding visual aesthetic integration and machine and team appearance. This team took consistent design and attractiveness to a new level. They did more than stand on one foot when it came to their team’s appearance. While KISS might be their engineering philosophy, they Rammed through the competition when it came to outstanding visual integration.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team excels in industrial organization and management. They understand the need to create more than just a great design. This river city team has produced documentation that allows efficient support and maintainability. Congratulations, Team number 1038.

The balance between innovation and functionality struck a chord with this team. From the start of their 3D designed herring bone gears, to their telescoping arm to drop the last note. They melted the competition for the Innovation in Control Award. Congratulations, Team 2357, System Meltdown.

Judges Award “PIT Professionals Award” This team performed exceptionally during the games, making it all the way to the finals. In the pits, this team demonstrated incredible cohesiveness in both spirit and technical knowledge, following the engineering design process to a T, and were able to create a focused and robust robot. Through effective practice and perseverance, turning blue with focus, dropping the anchor on their competition. Congratulations, Team number 2992, USS Prometheus.

This team’s design ensured robustness throughout the entire competition. The workmanship, machining, and overall construction are the epitome of durability and clean design principals. Ironically, nothing on this team’s robot was broken. Congratulations, Team number 3937.

Engineering is art; it inspires minds. This team's diverse vision shines; it blooms. Their gracious professionalism bridges gaps, builds strong bridges and displays Unity in strength. They want to win but they want others to compete at their best - and not just in first. As true engineers they have their notebook. They have become the inspiration for future generations; their inspiration thrives. It’s electric. This team will continue to soar like eagles.

This team demonstrated FIRST core values by developing relationships with teams in 9 different countries. They are GEARED for success, spreading the mission of FIRST and transforming the culture of their community with several STEM opportunities, including a rocket camp, aviation camp, STEM on Wheels, and STEM for Seniors. They’ve also donated over a few thousand LEGO kits to kids in 16 hospitals in 8 different states, including 100 kits given to the Arkansas Children’s Hospital. In addition, this team worked with the local police department to design and build a rack for their police car. Although the competition for this award was very challenging, the FIRST Impact Award has been well earned by the Sprockets!

The Rookie All-Star Award celebrates the rookie team exemplifying a young but strong partnership effort, as well as implementing the mission of first to inspire students to learn more about science and technology. This young team exemplified strong partnerships and inspiration in their first year. They were giants when they doubled the size of their team in the first year. With an infectious energy, these Titans exemplified the future of FIRST.

When the other teams said, “Hey”, this team brought the horsepower. This team came together beginning in January at quite the clip, with 45 minutes a day, to get their robot built. This team should giddy-up on their high horse for the Rookie Inspiration Award. Congratulations Team number 9608.
This team consistently brings the noise. Their enthusiasm is apparent and they stick together. But most importantly, they never say die. Congratulations, Team number 9067.

records.script: This team makes FIRST strong through their extensive community activities, support of numerous STEM events, summer camps and many philanthropic efforts. As their tentacles currently reach out to 11 schools, 10 cities and 3 states, their “OBSIDIAN” is shared with many!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team demonstrated industrial design principles with efficiency and elegance. The seamless handoff between the intake and elevator really stood out, and their multistage climber was outstanding. Congratulations, Team number 4270 the Crusaders!

This team openly acknowledged the realities of system failure, and need for redundancies; They know how to see from their robot’s perspective, and really knows how to FLASH their Innovation in control Congratulations, Team number 9719 ThunderTech Robotics!

This team’s robotics found their way out to a very different world; Their robot spinned and twirled; In the theater of competition, they are the coolest cats…. Congratulations, Team number 1452 The OmniCats!

From Pit to Field, this team demonstrates their robustness in structures, in wiring, and in control systems Their build quality and workmanship can be seen across the matches, while they FORGED a new identity. Congratulations, Team number 4421 FORGE Robotics!

This team has truly made a remarkable impact, inspiring future generations through their outreach and education efforts. Their STEM activities took them outside their community, city and country, beyond the reach of ‘just the robot’. Congratulations, Team number 6902 STRIKE!__

This year’s winner has extended their arms with regular classes as Leader and Mentor, helping many other teams beyond their region in both technical and “non-technical” aspects of FIRST. They have successfully lobbied to get recognition for both STEM and Women across their region, and they LIBERATED robots to new homes with clubs around the world. Their "Clean Web" initiative has established a partnership with a commercial recycler to collect a MILLION pounds of electronic waste

This team exemplifies FIRST values, making a significant IMPACT within their school and community. From supporting a girl’s coding camp, helping Indigenous youth and VEXing their opponents, their passion is visible both on and off the field. The Rookie All-Star Award is presented to: Team 9641 Robotics71 !

This team focused on and emphasized diversity and community. They swarmed in, mentoring other robotics groups and spreading pride at local events. This rookie team ‘s enthusiasm both on and off the field inspired and created a buzz among the judges. Congratulations, Team number 9449 Yellow Jackets!!

This team is willing to jump over obstacles to lend a hand - or a pad. When it comes to spirit, attitude and depth, they “coverall” the bases, and took to team spirit like a frog to water... Congratulations, Team number 7332 The PuddleJumpers

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: When you show up year after year, dependable and faithful For over 20 years of being in the Dawg House You know they have staying power! Congratulations, Team number 244 RoboDawgs 3D!

Se você precisa de autonomia, procure eles para te ajudar. Ensinar a máquina a fazer algo por si próprio não é uma tarefa fácil e eles demonstraram excelência em fazer isso, pode confiar, essa equipe mantém tudo sob controle.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Esta equipe mostrou a importância de desafiar os limites da imaginação e transformar ideias em realidade. A máquina deles não tem apenas um cérebro, possui rodas diferenciadas. Além de estarem levando um grande aprendizado, hoje também estão ganhando um prêmio.

Essa equipe trouxe um robô selvagem, que nada na escuridão das águas. Despertando assim a curiosidade dos juízes que ficaram impressionados com a robustez e experiência dos processos de engenharia. Com mais de 15 anos de experiência, eles abocanharam esse prêmio.

Compreendendo o poder do conhecimento e seu impacto na comunidade, essa equipe colabora de forma graciosa com outros times e com a comunidade para implementar projetos e destacar a acessibilidade como parte fundamental de suas conquistas. Diretamente do fundo do oceano, eles surgem com muita força e garra, contagiando à todos com sua energia inesgotável.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Uma identidade visual integrando equipe, robô e Pit abre as asas para voos mais altos. Com uma estilização arrojada e uma perfeita combinação com laranja, são imediatamente identificados nessa floresta de competidores. Ergam sua guitarra e venham receber seu prêmio.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: A equipe alçou voos, colorindo e encontrando o olhar dos juízes. Este ano eles já saíram do ninho com um design diferenciado, sofisticado e cheio de detalhes. Vestindo as cores e a força de um dos símbolos do Brasil eles voaram na nossa arena.

Com seu sistema de controle bastante inovador, utilizando IA e um feedback tátil, nos fascinaram assim como nos heróis da TV, usaram tecnologia de ponta, se unindo e formando um mega robô. É hora de morfar !
No passado, tecnologia se espalhava como pontos pelo oceano. O mundo evoluiu e as máquinas pare cem pensar. Robôs éticos e conscientes já criam estratégias na Ilha da Magia.

O Robô vencedor não é um R2D2 de Star Wars. Essa equipe trouxe uma qualidade diferenciada em seus processos de fabricação, materiais empregados e montagem. Com notável robustez até parece que esse robô veio das estrelas.

Com diversos projetos de engenharia, essa equipe demonstra um compromisso em disseminar a STEAM e os valores FIRST na comunidade, bem como esforços contínuos na construção da competição a longo prazo. A luz que essa equipe emana é amarela e, como eles mesmos se definem, são como engrenagens que funcionam juntas para um trabalho de excelência.

A equipe teve uma sacada incrível e criou uma ferramenta de ensino criativa, divertida e interativa, nela são explorados diversos temas, como por exemplo aerodinâmica. O alcance foi fantástico pois foi traduzido para cinco línguas, incluindo três nativas do Brasil. Desta forma eles conseguiram abraçar muita gente, com certeza deve ter sido por causa dos seus oito braços.
Uma nova estrela surgiu para impactar sua comunidade. Ciência, tecnologia, artes, engenharia agora são um projeto de lei. Répteis estão em evolução tecnológica.

De espírito esportivo e trabalho em conjunto eles entendem, seja na arena ou no pasto, esse time demonstrou compromisso com STEAM, moldando mentes e construindo futuros, seja mecânico, mitológico ou mini.
Guiados pela sua estrela, com sensibilidade e imaginação esse time trouxe o espírito do nordeste brasileiro para a competição, você já ouviu o seu grito de guerra.

Gracious Professionalism is the core of everything we believe in. This team was very apparent in the pits helping out other teams. They've even taken their robo power into the community making the streets safer with their pine needle bot.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is recognized everywhere. The appearance of team members, robot, pit, and souvenir items are known by all. Always expressing the principles of FIRST through dedication and involvement, they wave their wands spreading the M.A.G.I.C. of FIRST.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's robot shines bright with its robust, general design. This team comes in hot, developing a robot that works well on the field, while giving their driver a good situational awareness throughout the competition. There's no chance for flame out here!

For this team, there is no challenge too tall or too small using vision and sensors to control the field. Using innovative branch concepts to develop roots and share knowledge. Ultimately to ground the center of gravity for Stumpy.

The judges recognize and want to award one team for their total commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging. These big thinkers impressed the judges with their accessible pipeline, looking to normalize female involvement throughout STEM. We see and hear you.

This team's carefully-crafted components were verified more than once and proved their quality and robustness. This robot took big hits in the field and led the herd. When a quality robot is needed, this divine team jumps over the moon.
This team showed measurable year-over-year growth in outreach. Like a bird of prey, they saw all options to engage. Their multi-level training helped attendees soar to new heights!

Creating an effective pipeline is a key element of sustainability throughout FIRST. This team has found effective partnerships to not only extend but enhance the STEM experience of both participants and spectators. Combining and stacking events creates a strong foundation, taking advantage of every opportunity to share STEM folks with FIRST and FIRST folks with STEAM. The blocks just fall into place.
They have improved and problem solved in mastering FIRST Robotics allowing them to "Dream Big."

This small but determined team pushed hard to live up to their school's excellent reputation. Identifying needed skills helped them recruit new members. These knights worked through circuits to achieve a neat appearance to a good defensive robot.
This team's enthusiasm was colossal in both the pits and the stands. In mythology, they may have been banished, but in FRC, the team's energy triumphed!

records.script: This team demonstrated sustainability in the way they recruit as well as they recruit as well as recycled materials. This flock has taken their robot's wings and learned to fly. With a little help from Mike in Jersey, these blackbirds can now sing!

Today, at East Bay Regional, an award we bestow, To a team that refined their autonomous code, like well risen dough. Their method, complex, with finely crafted code, Four cameras, six pieces, scored on the go. Innovation and dedication, they did sow, Congratulations to these well-buttered rolls, whose brilliance did glow.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Levers, rollers, sticks and more, which ideas come to the fore? This robot picks, flips, and spits, cuz' its intake includes a wrist. This team's portfolios most exotic, the creativity awards goes to Galileo Robotics.

This team’s robot showcases their excellent design and engineering a-BELL-ities. From conception to implementation, their elegantly designed and efficient turret led them to a well-documented success. Exhibiting Excellence in Engineering isn’t CHEESY.

Look down from atop the stands, and record what you see. For we are here to tell you about a team, graciously professional and always helping rookies. From competitions to applications, when we tell you of this team make sure you hear it. For they are so GP that we can hardly bear it.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has a treasured style that no one needs a spyglass to see. This team integrated their theme with all aspects of their team and brought booming effects to show their unique presence. All hands on deck to give a hearty congratulations to team number 5430

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This red and black robot does it all, Whether speaker, amp, or trap they don't fall. Highlighting an intake that works in every direction, Their clean and compact design an ELEMENT in their selection.

With advanced vision, this team's intake doesn't miss a note. Not just aiming for the center, a single button will orient this robot to the goal, and their spinning shot is the GUACAMOLE. Using a Lime light and an Orange Pi, this team squeezes the most out of their robot with zest-in-class controls.

This team understands the value of simplicity as an asset, not a hinderance. Their robot consistently excels, and they have a profound grasp of the FIRST mission, anchoring their approach in gracious professionalism. At the end of the day, the judges were impressed at how this team can turn on a dime, they know that changing the world happens one robot at a time.
For an experimental team, they sure iterated to perfection. While other teams were shearing apart, they "weld" it together. With such a robust machine, their robot is far from prototypical.

This team left the judges speechless. The scope and scale of their inspiration is unstoppable. They have started hundreds of teams, taught STEM classes to thousands of students, and reached tens of thousands of people. Galloping through barriers, this team is inspiring everyone regardless of who you are or where you are from.

This team is on a quest to defeat STEAM barriers for all. Starting in their home town, they quickly leveled up to champion diversity and inclusion in STEAM at every school within their district. Setting their sights on the next level, they partnered with other underserved communities outside of their home state. They donated FIRST Lego League kits and followed up with many remote mentoring sessions. They raised the funds necessary for those teams to travel to meet with their mentors in person and to compete, some even winning awards! Keeping the FIRST energy going year round, they’ve started and co-hosted a new off-season FRC event for their region. Not letting a lack of FIRST in other countries get in their way, they’ve used FLL as a platform to make STEAM not just accessible, but a universal language for all. You can’t stop these phantomz from leveling up the world!
This team has proven their reach is far, spanning hundreds of miles. They support economically struggling communities in their country. These cats are not rare or endangered!

This team bootstrapped their way to the spotlight. They conduct themselves well by exhibiting FIRST Core Values, reaching out local FLL teams, and going viral with their message of tenacity. They are the un-DEFEATED winners of the Rookie Inspiration Award. Congratulations, Team 9470 – CTRL-ALT-DEFEAT!
When it comes to spirit this team delivers, they cheer, they chant, they love their drive team. Please celebrate the energy of these red raptors of the sky!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team works with the local clubs and LEGO robotics teams giving young people a chance to develop skills as they grow and move onward in FIRST. Team encourages FIRST values with signed posters and buttons. Working in a carbon-neutral environment, moving their waste to local companies, recycling metal to the metal working classes, this team LIVES the CIRCLE of sustainability.

Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.script: Hide yo' amps, Hide yo' speakers, This robot will track them, All the way from the bleachers. Don't let it see you, Or you'll suffer it's wrath. What has four eyes, And never strays from its path? When it comes to autonomy, This team did the most. This robot don't miss, The competition is TOAST!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: From the creative minds of these mutts, their stubbornness has no bounds. Even if that means jack-hammering the trap at the end of the round!
This team's approach to engineering insures they will not go extinct. They "fossilized" professionalism and design into its process. Don't let the "short" arms fool, they still climb to the top!

This team exemplifies the highest standards of integrity in all they do. They live by core values such as "we not me" and "everybody belongs". They judges would like to recognized the Gracious Professionalism of the the Firebots.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Energized by unique avian inspiration, Soaring on artistic steam with wings spread wide Lishan Magpies fly high!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Enhanced with form and function, intricately entwined, this robot's prowess leaves others far behind. A beacon of innovation, a sight to behold, In the world of robotics, its story is told. With swerve and shooter, and climber's grace, this blue robot claims its place.

Its metal frame adorned with modern grace In the Controls Realm, it finds its place A hang system novel, sleek and bold This robot is crowned, its tale is told Innovation hailed, a robot takes the stage With turret shooter poised, it aims to engage!
United in resourceful skill and might, Their prior triumph a beacon in the night! With students' initiative and driving plans, They eagerly unite, ready to conquer and shine bright!

In colors bold, its victory declared. The quality award, rightfully snared. With neat and robust wiring inside, In excellence, this robot’s secrets reside. In hues of blue, black, and orange, it stays small. A beacon of quality revered by all.

This team stands out for their embrace of all. Empowering kids young and bold, with every circuit and story told. With the breadth of their programs and drive to include, we’re inspired to present this award to you.

Deeply embedded in community and fostering trust throughout, their well-known brand is recognized at home and worldwide. Pre-K to launch, classroom to market they leave a trail for others to follow. In a flock of spectacularly high fliers, these young brains reach for the stars and soar beyond.

For embracing FIRST, it found its call. A shining star, inspiring one and all! Its design, ambitious, a sight to behold! Innovation flourished, its story told. In Bytes and Bagels, its victory clear! So let us hail this Rookie All-Star this year!

In recognition, resplendence, and remarkable resourcefulness, the award awaits, In the realm of robotics, a rookie revelation rises, radiating with the rigor of redwoods. As the googlee eyes rotate, let's render the revered R cubed recognition, a reward for the Redwood Rangers Robotics!
Heard from afar, their crescendo shakes the stands. When they hit the right note, they amped up their fans. It was a clear sign their impact we cannot negate.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is growing in harmony with their community. With help from their alumni network, they are guiding future generations and their community to not only sustain their team but improve the environment around them. These cats will continue to aim for the universe!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.script: This team took on a triple challenge of localization from camera to carpet. They used a distributed system to detect AprilTags and send them to the RoboRio for processing. Latency could be a problem, so they apply a correction algorithm to keep their prediction up to date. Finally, they use a setpoint system to maintain robot traction and complete their autonomous HAT trick.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Material science is an interesting TOPIC Sometimes team choices upset our LOGIC Instead of aluminum or lexan like they SHOULD This team relies on good old PLYWOOD Their use of recyclable, layered green composites, SLING SHOT this winning team ahead of the competition.

This team follows a robust engineering process to make critical decisions. Up against tight constraints, they strategically sacrificed part of their robot to find the perfect CONSTELLATION of features. For a carefully prioritized design, this team follows their STAR SIGN!

With their luminescent jackets, this team dashes around the venue to ensure a smooth and fun experience for everyone. Shielding us from foul forces (rain) they escorted everyone for safe passage. Outside of the venue, this team used their super powers to mentor and support STEAM activites, always with a smile. Robots PLUS Support PLUS a positive attitude is the ULTRA combination for this winning team.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team carries through the team’s image from their buttons, colors, and WINGS. They may not breath fire, but these serpents cannot be missed.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This quick robot turns the whole field on its FACE. Strategic use of aluminum alloys ensures everything stays in PLACE. Don't let its shine make you think it's not ROBUST, every part of this robot was designed to not BUST. If you have to make the whole gear, you've been HAD. But when your cannon slaps, you know you've gone MAD.

This team built an innovative shooter that can lock goal orientation, and will inform the driver when a shot is infeasible. Their robot never gets lost, thanks to some PARTICULAR filters. Without wasting a SLIVER of time, this auto shooter is QUICK!

From summer camps and sharing, this team focuses their outreach and mentoring on coopertition and collaboration. They work hard on diversity and sustainability and it shows in every member of their team. They CYCLE their efforts, making the Judge’s decision as easy as PANCAKES. The Judges TIP OUR HATS to

This team shows how quality is not just about strength, but also about how you handle failure. The judges found them in the middle of their post match checklist, which includes tightening every bolt on their external intake. But the real achievement was that in one match, a shooter motor failed and couldn't spin as hard. Their control system simply calculated new trajectories and let them keep on PRESENTING their notes.

When you are FORGED IN FIRE your impact is long lasting. No matter the age, no matter the audience, this team promotes STEM and FIRST to all. With a Mo-dest do-meaner (modest demeanor) this team has been recognized by leaders of their community both big and small for their passionate advocacy and actions. Constantly on the go with community engagement this team is SUPER SCO-NIC.

The FIRST Impact Award is presented to the team judged to have the most significant measurable impact of its partnerships among its participants and community over a sustained period, not just a single build season. The winner is able to demonstrate progress towards FIRST’s mission of transforming our culture. The recipient team will be invited to a FIRST Championship where it will compete for the FIRST Impact Award against winners from other qualifying events. Like many teams, this team ORGANIZED and DELIVERED SIGNIFICANT outreach to elementary and middle school students. Their reach for FLL teams increased 400-plus percent with 1000 team hours. They taught middle schoolers about STEM, INSPIRING them. Beyond this, this middle-sized team saw a need BEYOND THEIR AREA. Beyond California, beyond the United States, to another country. Helping young people learn English gave those needy young people access to learning STEM in rural areas, supporting a new FRC team there, and more! Their efforts INSPIRED us with its IMPACT. At another level, the members of this team saw the need for government funding and recognition of STEM education. As part of Students Association for STEM Advocacy, three years ago, then as the catalyst and co-founder of California Association for STEM Advocacy, with ANNUAL CONFERENCES and many visits to elected officials, even writing legislation for STEM funding, this team believes “ADVOCACY DOESN’T WORK WITHOUT COMMUNITY”.. Through SCHOOLS OF FISH, this team makes RIPPLES of IMPACT turn into WAVES of CHANGE.

This rookie team dreams of building more teams. Despite their challenges, they are spreading STEAM through their TED Talks, the school carnival, and connecting with teachers and local businesses to support programs. This rookie team has established themselves as the FIRST building block for their community.

This very spirited team can easily be spotted in the stands. Roaming the venue with their distinctive shirts, giveaways, mascots and pompoms you can see their excitement for their game. They barely have enough time for a Cup of Tea.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is not just about graduation or which college to attend; it’s about empowering any career path a member chooses to pursue. Whether through internships or outreach, their community involvement is STELLAR. You don’t have to go very DEEP to find this team.
This nimble robot has eyes on the back of its head and automatic claws. This kitty keeps its shooter on a swivel while MU-ving around the field.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Using surgical concepts and materials, this team demonstrated flavorful strategies and creative execution. Their shooter’s design is a risk they did take, but don’t let the colorful name of their bot fool you. So, here’s to the team that’s always in the loop with their bot Froot Loops.

This team’s process from conception to implementation was ON PORPOISE. Their scissor mechanism is elegantly designed and robustly engineered for PEAK performance. They are the PINNACLE of Excellence in Engineering.

Soaring to great heights, this team ensures other teams are taken well care of. With several teams commending their helpful nature, this team embodies gracious professionalism behind the scenes. They are truly in their element.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: You can hear them from afar as they come over. The sound of a bird that flies over. The sea of blue that lands in the stands. It’s a beautiful blue Falcon that comes to land.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot is packed up clean and compact. Their drivetrain and intake are quick to react. With vision lighting their LED bar, their STINGING shooter is seen from afar.

In a field where innovation shines, one team’s control scheme truly aligns. With a turret shooter guided by light, they’ve mastered the mechanics of a zero-backlash screw. While auto-targeting, pose localization guides what they do. Maroon and black lead the pack, solving problems with trigonometry’s knack.

This team has a green thumb. By successfully replanting the seed of FIRST, their team has grown deep roots, securing themselves to the hillside. For their perseverance in expanding the garden of FIRST despite adverse circumstances, the judges would like to honor this team.

This team’s design factored in Weight And Reliability, leading them to a simpler machine with fewer parts. Their modular subsystems and independent CAN buses helped them stay running no matter how tough the fight. Through the competition, this robot proved that it was built ready for WAR.

This team runs STEM-focused summer programs, hosts FLL tournaments, showcases a high excellence in engineering design, and has established strong connections within its local community and sponsor network. Their presence was felt every corner at this event, helping whoever they could. This ORANGE team has truly cracked the CODE to fulfilling FIRST’s mission.

Tackling community challenges head-on with innovative STEM solutions, this team rallies together from far and wide. They identified community needs-designing, soldering, and changing lives. Using their coding chops to support the FIRST community, they should feel proud to carry the banner of their purple lion mascot.

This team shines brighter than any star with their smiles and skills. Overcoming all their challenges and inspiring us as they climb up the hills. This rookie team really understood what it meant to be in Hollywood.
This team pulls from the past to move forward. Built to solve technical challenges, they will take their team over the wall. Inspired by stars and the Trons, they are in it for the long haul.

LITTLE BY LITTLE, this team is building partnerships to further the objectives of FIRST. This team’s spirit is MAKING STEM MORE FUN in their team, community, and at every competition by crossing different borders. These guys aren’t sheep to follow the herd. Their enthusiasm RAMS through the competition in every way.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: In a world where gears mesh in perfect symmetry, one team stands tall through a commitment to sustainability. From transforming beaches and recycling e-waste, this team has a vision where environmental care and community partnership are essential. Let’s congratulate a team who leaps and bounds in front of competition for a greater cause.

Autonomous operation is extremely valuable in all of FIRST, not just the first fifteen seconds of a match. This team stands out for the custom-designed software that allowed their robot to plan its own actions on the field. The match telemetry they showed us removed all ambiguity about who deserves this award.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s design for grabbing notes from the ground from any direction really impressed the judges. It VACUUMED the notes so fast that they almost became RADIOACTIVE. For addressing all the ELEMENTS of the creativity award, we are glad to give the award for the all-directional intake design of Radium the Roomba.

This team wowed the judges not only with their design, but with their ability to explain their process for evolving it over the course of the season. They clearly presented their plan for reaching 100 percent. Their modular design is plug-and-play, and their engineering notebook was truly a work of art.

Balancing realism and idealism, this team's FORTE is building opportunities for others. Always thinking of their fellow teams, they demonstrate innovative design, coopertition, and true professionalism to other teams by providing practice space and travel to Houston. They are a true renaissance team.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team stands on an island of their own, hopping their way to the top of the group in the imagery award. Aesthetics and visuals clearly are important for them and they truly hit the mark. This team has taken a concentrated effort to coordinate a beary cool image.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team went over and above to make sure that their robots vision cannot be blocked and that their CAD was done in 18 days. From the bottom plates to the 6 foot drop test with the boat hook, this team's robot truly demonstrated form, function and aesthetics. This robot works like a four seasons hotel taking in notes like the true lord of the dance.

Good design not only creates systems for managing a robot when everything is going well, but also for knowing what is broken when the inevitable happens. The team’s comprehensive system for reporting real-time failures to drivers really impressed the judges. We are sure it can help them SWIM through any SEA of troubles as if they were ARMORED IN SHINING METAL.

This team has a robotics program that is in the process of re-creation. Innovatively reaching beyond the bounds of their community and school. By developing robotic workshops, they are making a critical impact on children of homeless shelters.

This team’s robot and pit exemplified clean design in both its form and function. One of the things that really impressed the judges was the innovative use of LED strips not just to show general status, but to show how well the robot was pointed. It is no PARADOX that this robot deserves the quality award!

This team has been able to deliver a big impact all over the world. With their support, teams were able to get all the cogs turning and undertake new problems. This team’s goal is to achieve universal education, and with their curriculum development, training courses, and 3D printer distribution, they are ready for liftoff towards this goal.

Getting enough game play is one of the greatest challenges for FRC teams especially in Title I schools. These troopers took the time to identify the problem space and truly understand the broader operating environment. With sharp fangs using social media platforms addressing spectators and stakeholders alike, our winner secured funding to extend the robotics season statewide.
Young but strong, these students get the FIRST message. Equipped with a growing STEM curriculum and strong community partnerships, they’re ready to go into battle. Bearing down for the long haul,

This team is well-organized, building a simple, robust robot that can ride the ocean. They have made a difference buzzing the stereotype of typical PE programs, elevating technology at their school. This team does their own sting, working to improve their school’s graduation rate and test scores.

Made for the eyes of children, their enthusiasm to spread their love for robotics is catching. This team celebrates their soaring spirit through flight & friendship. Connecting even locally with bandanas, birds, and books, teamwork is a core element to success.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team grabbed the judges’ attention with their work in sustainability. They are not square with their environmental involvement. This group of block heads removed 40 tons of e-waste and grew the FIRST ecosystem.

records.script: This team rises above the Redwoods. From start to finish, these performers leave no note un-hit. Them and their robot are certainly not half-baked.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When it comes to unique design, this team FLIES high above the rest. Its hang mechanism adjusts center-of-gravity so that the robot can perch atop the STAGE with ease. Their outside-the-BOX design allows them to adjust their trajectory faster than you can say "PIZZA TIME."

Inspired by their MUSE, this team produced copious documentation of their design process. Their multiple independent mechanisms are easy to repair and VIBE well together. The judges are sure this team will CRUISE to victory.

This team demonstrated outstanding Gracious Professionalism. Identifying nine examples of GP in their documents, posters and badges, they transmitted the concept with detail and humor. By reaching out to local elementary schools, swapping information with competitor teams, and sharing software via Discord, this team really stood out.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: To this team, branding is a way to bring their community under their WINGS. As the competition WAXES and WANES, this team remains enthusiastic and green. This team has truly shot for THE MOON in two years.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: By elegantly combining practical and efficient design, choosing this team was a snap. This team gives careful consideration to materials, reusability, and a clean and functional aesthetic. They fabricate their future, printing parts that are thought-provoking.

This team strikes the perfect balance between human and machine. By illuminating LEDs automatically, the operator doesn’t need eagle eyes to determine the robot’s status. The effectiveness of their solution is reflected in their performance.

This group is supercharging their community, school and government. Flush with commercial connections, they place certified students directly into advanced manufacturing jobs from high school. The Judge’s Award for going ALL IN on Industry goes to Team 7426 Pair of Dice!
This purple team has been performing with pride. From their iterative design process to their reliable and robust robot, this team consistently delivers quality.

This team stood out for their ability to measure the results of their outreach programs. In addition to mentoring or assisting over 40 FIRST teams, they targeted female representation through SWE Next and girls clubs. As a result their team went from just 2 girls to over 20 in a year. This team really puts their ideas to the test.

This team creates an expanding curriculum for youth STEM education, spearheads engineering programs at their school, and bridges communities across the peninsula and the world. With a robust commitment to supporting Women in STEM, they leverage their position in their community to ensure strong fundamentals in their pond. This team gears up local underserved communities making truly accessible programs for all. Leaving their shallow waters, they're spreading their STEM curriculum across oceans to help alleviate poverty and empower women. These green chompers are unstoppable.

This Team’s strong pedigree gave them a unique setup to recruit and train young team members to build an innovative and independent robot. They have multiplied their efforts throughout their school and community via the FIRST California Rookie Network.

This team’s voice was amplified throughout the competition. Through ups and downs, they roared for their team members through the crowd. They have claws, they wear horns, and they dance in their teal tutus.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is a reel advocate for the FIRST community. By continually evolving and expanding their outreach initiatives, they cast a wide net across the globe. They impact Big Fish and Little Fish, from legislators to toddlers at the Childrens’ Hospital. These documented and environmentally-sustainable efforts lead to a smashing success!

Detecting game pieces, their sensors ENHANCE. They know their location in every CIRCUMSTANCE. Not leaving things to chance, no room for SNAKE-EYES. With Seven-twenty degree rotation their design DEFIES. Their sensors and software make them PRECISE, And all heads turn as they “ROLL THE DICE”!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Making the MOST with what you have AVAILABLE requires creativity. When you’re FISHING for robot music, you have to get a NOTE on the HOOK. Get two effective HOOKS and you have a HIT!

DETERMINED to improve their design process from last year, this team started differently after kickoff. Reading the manual together, they used sub-teams and prototyping, and they showed their WRATH at their last year, strengthening their design process for this year’s robot, demonstrating their EXCELLENCE!
It is often hard to find small parts? Right before your next match starts, we need an app to help report! You better call TECH Support

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: With a consistent image year over year, they used their theme in children’s books reading at libraries. With special sweets and bright RED HATS, this team’s image is known to everyone. Their COOKIE JAR provides PARTS and help to other teams as well!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: In the realm of robotics, where innovation meets functionality, one team has SET THE BAR HIGH with their exceptional approach to design. Embracing the principles of a CLEAN AND MODULAR DESIGN, they have created a reliable robot that is also a BREEZE to maintain and adapt. With a robust intake neatly tucked within the frame perimeter and an inverted control system, they've demonstrated that THOUGHTFUL DESIGN can lead to FORMIDABLE PERFORMANCE. Dressed in striking orange and black, this bot has CLAWED ITS WAY through the competition with elegance and strength.

This team has MASTERED the art of resetting encoder drift. Kind of like a ROBOTIC ERASER for imprecision. Climbing the ranks this team uses a gyro sensor to level out their climb. And if SYMMETRY is your thing, their shooter and intake share a body making their robot the EPITOME OF EFFICIENCY. Their beam breaks and Hall effect sensors not only build a FAILSAFE robot, but also HAUL in the APPLAUSE. This isn’t just any team, they are a SOARING SENSATION, spreading their WINGS in the domain of CONTROL.

In three years, they’ve established a non-profit, gained key local sponsors, and engaged their community with outreach. Working to ensure their team’s success, they impressed the judges with their enthusiasm and energy. This district wide team of MANY HEADS has surpassed expectations with self-organization and robot quality.

This FAST team is a SHINING example of quality, with a robot meticulously ADORNED in 3D printed parts that reflect their team's colors. Their commitment to quality SHINES THROUGH a vision system that constantly reports an internal quality metric, ensuring their POSE ESTIMATION is as accurate as possible. This PRECISION allows them to SCORE WITHOUT STOPPING, seamlessly integrating robustness and functionality.

This team’s outreach is multi-dimensional and INSPIRING. Besides mentoring many FLL and FTC teams, hosting qualifiers, and having an ongoing academy for elementary students. Helping teachers, a new path, raising money and building a MOBILE LAB to help teachers gain experience and confidence with STEM tools and curriculum. Developing and raising money for a FTC hackathon for the islands, their INSPIRING WORK became caused an ERUPTION of eight FTC teams.

This team combines COMPREHENSIVE local outreach with HUGE support to fellow FIRST teams. In their community, ONE IN FIVE of all students participate in their camps or youth leagues. These programs are more than SELF-SUSTAINING, allowing them to EXPAND to new underserved areas and fix up other team’s robots with a signature FLAVOR. Even when they are not competing, this team attends FRC events to provide tools, parts, and EXPERTISE to other teams. They also participate in Women in STEM events, co-host off-season competitions, and help other teams emulate their SUCCESSFUL SYLLABUS.

This rookie team has mastered it all. Starting in the off-season, their ambition stood tall. Out of a garage their students convene 9th grade standouts in the robotics scene. Their performance inspires, their passion so sweet. No reboots here, CTRL-ALT-DEFEAT
Their energy soars as their ties strengthen. In their 19th year, and with 67 teammates, Such fun they have each year. They describe their robot as kind of JANKY.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Engaging students EARLY, with FLL workshops and outreach. Working with local government, an A-PLUS for driving EXTRA miles to support so many teams, taking sustainability to a new level: gathering and melting cans, making ingots. Next step: turning ingots into parts!

Autonomy, when done right, rolls in like waves and is unstoppable. Their autonomous capabilities set a HIGH watermark that really made an impact. Coming in like a cyclone, this team stormed their way through the competition.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team surfs the waves of creativity. On their surfboard, they used an interesting mechanism that could TRAP high and low. ORANGE you glad their surfer bot cracked the code.

“Practice what you know, and it will help to make clear what now you do not know”, said a famous painter. This team exhibited its engineering mastery with the finesse of passionate artists crafting their canvas. The models and overall integrated system are truly impressive.

This team does all sorts of things with the many hats that they wear. Grab a port key and aparate because this team is there to help. They show that they care by delivering MAGIC through owls to these mini muggles.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: At the CORE of this team is a cadence for polish and quality. Going on the road or heading to a show, there is a seat for everyone. Keeping everything under wraps, this team displays their marketing and cohesion for pit to play every day.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This shape-shifting robot can do it all. 4 wheels plus 1 intake plus 1 shooter plus 2 hooks and 1 clean design add up to the complete package. This versatile robot was OCTO-awesome.
This dinosaur will shake any driver’s hand. Their use of AI for notation is terrifyingly innovative. This team's industrial control will save them from extinction.
This team flies in to support their alliances. They designed a solid link to harmonize with other teams. Soaring to great heights through their unique climb,

The judges would not mess with this animal in the arena. This team’s robust robot construction allows it to eat breakfast, lunch and dinner without fail. In every match, EL TORO charges out onto the field with pride.

These birds of prey SOARED to success to include everyone playing a part. This team migrated from a tank drive to a swerve drive this year. Their successful Engineering Expo was inspirational and brought communities together.

This team exhibits steam with creative strategies and art in the mind’s eye. Persistence and passion for others ensures this team’s impact story is a page-turner. Close your eyes and imagine mapping the environment to ability and beyond!

With the heavy luggage and distance this small team traversed sand and sea. Like sugar, with just a little heat, this team will caramelize. The way this team plays the field, receiving penalties from their opponents, is how they strategize.

Introducing a new team is hopping on the challenge. Their teamwork and engineering are certainly bright stars among the seasoned crowd. Cooperation, respect and professionalism define this energizing rookie team.

This team lights up the stands with their enthusiastic ROAR, while cheering for the MANE event! They face their challenges with courage and conviction and still spread joy through the PRIDELANDS. Led by their mascot they bring energy to the CYBER arena to bring the house down!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team successfully herds future generations of FRC teams. They ensure cross-training and problem-solving to shepherd future nerds into the fold through FLL and FTC. All work and lots of play sustain this team for FIRST.

A proficient team adept at field control and maneuvering This team leverages their multitude of autonomous features to ensure consistent and reliable scoring Skilled at selflessly re-PATH-ing their auto to complement alliance partners averaging 5.5 notes in auto.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team prowls the field to make a clean sweep. Their offset style helps them stack the notes. Their broom bristles are as sleek and powerful as their creativity.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This rookie team is leading the way in outreach. Whether supporting an FTC team, giving FLL teams a tour of their shop or bringing their robot to other schools, they’re spreading FIRST values. As an impact team in the making, this team is the STAR of the show.

This team came to the competition ready to showcase their excellence. Through planning, prototyping, and collaboration, they have developed a robot that performed with precision on the field and pushed the boundaries of engineering ingenuity. It’s easy to see why this team is also known as “KING OF THE JUNGLE”.

The word FIRST can sometimes mean a solitary entity, but this team considers FIRST to include anyone and everyone. Being different isn’t SCARY! It’s part of how this team embraces the diversity of our world. Embracing our core values as an LGBTQ+ silver sponsor and advocating for menstrual equity, we see this team BREWING up the future of FIRST.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has a great strategy for incorporating and communicating their brand. Their ability to integrate branding into their pits, robot, and outreach events has set them apart and given them a voice in their community. This may sound CHEESY…. We BRIE-lieve this team belongs at the top.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's compact bot performed without problems on the field due to their thorough design process. Their fast & agile bot was seen blazing orange across the field. They raced through this competition like a TIGER.

This team’s mastery of advanced technologies sets them apart. They utilize their ability to selectively choose notes and targets. Harnessing the power of AI and leveraging their reptilian-like vision system.

This team inspires future roboticists while cheering on future athletes. The team has a new SPARK in their community. The judge’s award for INCLUSIVITY goes to this team for their adaptive equipment to support their ROBOBUDDIES.

This team aimed to excel in every task and executed them with precision. Their innovative arm design facilitates seamless scoring across the competition, while its lightweight construction can be lifted with a single finger. Their robot engineering has been instrumental in their success and allowed them to FLY high in competition.
This team’s outreach statistics were an inspiration to the judges. Their outreach spans both locally and afar. Hopefully, you can all help me in saying that THIS IS A GIRL THING.

Today we celebrate a team that has demonstrated unwavering strength and tenacity through their commitment to inspiring others Like mythical beings, they’ve left an indelible mark on their community by championing diversity, STEAM, and robotics education through both FIRST and outside avenues. It is with great honor that we present this award to a team that truly embodies the spirit of making a difference -

Building well-rounded students by teaching and inspiring students of all backgrounds and experience levels. Hold on to your cookies because they are about to go nuclear This bright, fresh, and EXPLOSIVE team cannot be missed on the field.

This team made a SPLASH with their energy and enthusiasm on and off the field. Their props have made appearances with teams throughout the stands and pits. With a top-to-bottom spirit plan, these FISH have wormed their way into our hearts.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Since the Enlightenment, we have been inspired by great thinkers and builders. Great ideas last the test of time and thrive because of great management and adaptability. This team is all about the science, SQUARED OFF to accomplish great things for a long time to come.

This team reached the summit with their technical prowess and seamless navigation. Their preprogrammed paths and auto targeting lead to near perfect accuracy. They showed up dressed to KILT with consistent performance.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This teams’ unique design allows them to score from anywhere on the field. Their intentional spin and use of computer vision has been instrumental in the competition. Without this creativity, this team would be “Up a Creek”

This dynamite team is in harmony with their machine and each other. They left a giant footprint on the playing field with their matrix management and sprint reviews. “Tacosauras” has a finger on the pulse of their excellence in engineering.
This team graciously approaches collaboration from a different angle. They find creative ways to exalt others. Like the desert sun, they rise from the East, shining their light like angels.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: With printers in 3D and LED patterns, this team put their best face forward. Like the foothills of Colorado, their CAD integration and programming created beautiful form and exceptional function. The orange and teal dragon is a bot that would make Napoleon proud.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team wow’d the judges with their sleek custom swerve modules and interchangeable components. These busy bees speed across the field consistently scoring point after point. Their sturdy design allowed them to be a force on the field.
Under the northern lights, this team played notes accurately. With precision they fly through the northern woods. Their claws have a sharp grasp of innovation in control.

From the ridges of ingenuity, this team used an unconventional design approach. By physically putting themselves in chairs, they got into the mind of their bot to optimize their design. With a saber tooth grin, this team really put their teeth into their work.
These cats are really excited about quality. This team pounced on the challenge to build a robust robot. When it comes to the rigors of competition, they have it wired.

Engineers craft robotic “symphonies” blending innovation and inspiration to “tune” the future. Their efforts “amplify” from classrooms to communities, striking “chords” of progress. From Jackson, their “melody” reaches the Indian reservation, uniting tradition and technology.

This team's presentation blew the judges out of the water. Their engagement with other teams proves that collaboration amplifies impact. Their tentacled outreach approach serves and engages multiple marginalized communities in FIRST. They leverage intelligent design to make their outreach efforts transferrable and accessible for other teams. Their embodiment of diversity, equity, and inclusion ensures that everyone Under the Sea can realize their full potential.
These stars from the East are focused on growth. Their training and documentation is open to all. Don’t be obtuse and confuse them for ANGELS….

On the not-so-green slopes of a hill, a small team fights for respect. This team is working through their difficulties to make an impact on their school. During the off season, expect a battering ram effort to green up their dream of reaching the peak of robotics success.

This bot’s large eyes are always on the lookout to build FIRST values, one brick at a time. This team is cool under pressure and will always warm your heart. This Artic team will cheer you on in their snazzy jackets and alliance shoes.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has exemplified environmental sustainability, tracking carbon emissions and waste disposal. They refused to rest on their laurels, recruiting and keeping sponsors involved. With their professional grade documentation, and innovative use of kindles, we have no doubt these young engineers will be titans of the industry.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.script: This team’s shear strength is evident after one match. With their inventive “breadboard” driver station to their impressive autonomous control system, this team torques tighter than the competition.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's innovative design has helped them hang on throughout this competition. They sought creative solutions just outside of their shop. Their robot screams like a banshee, but this team grunts!

In a league of extraordinary teams, one has risen above with their colorful spirit and unwavering dedication to outreach. From Brazil to Canada and beyond, this team’s impact knows no bounds, embodying the true essence of the Engineering Inspiration Award. This team brings ‘peace’ of mind to the world of FIRST on and off the Field.

In the words of FIRST cofounder Dr Woodie Flowers, ”Never underestimate the power of a dedicated and passionate group of individuals to accomplish the incredible.” BALANCE This team is all about balance. The team members are evenly balanced between the grades in their school. Their outreach is balanced between three distinct concentrations. The number of Lego teams they started, and support doubled this year. TEAM SUPPORT This team maintains an open practice field for any teams that needs the space. New this year is a 12 hour a day support line for any team to get immediate help. OUTREACH Anyone in their community can benefit from their outreach. If you are in middle school, you can learn about the water crisis. If you are an elder, you get to play games to improve your mobility. When asked what their team candy bar was, they refer to themselves as the Sour Patch Kids, but they won us over with their sweetness.

This team can fly high in the numbers with no issue. Their red rollers can be seen hitting notes from across field. With their stellar design and impressive track record. This team continues to ace the competition and soar high up in the leaderboards.

This award goes to a team that embodies the principles of Gracious Professionalism in all aspects of their robotics journey. Their willingness to go the extra mile to assist others, whether it's troubleshooting technical issues or offering encouragement, sets them apart. Sometimes a small push can help set a team in the right direction

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team and their machine truly stands out in the pits and the field. From rollers and LEDs to their team outfits, this team showcased aesthetic synergy and alignment between their members and machine. With their machine leaving a lingering neon green streak on the field,

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This award goes to a team that was not only efficient, but had an innovative design and aesthetic. Their approach integrated components into a sleek, low-profile design, flashing black and red accents as they maneuvered swiftly across the field. They rammed through defenses, relentless to deliver their notes no matter what
This team “soars” above the rest. From their innovative custom interpolation model to their time to frequency domain transfer framework, these hawks fly past their competition

Dean Kamen once said “Every once in awhile, new technology, an old problem, and a big idea turn into an innovation”. This team comes together to have came up with multiple big ideas including the utilization of AI and 3D printing technologies to solve the old problem of making the world more accessible. Shine on.
This team works with quality in mind. With their impressive modular design, they roared with the ferocity of a tigress.

This award recognizes a rookie team that not only excels on the field but also embodies the true spirit of FIRST. This team's quick discovery on how to foster inclusivity and growth within their community, coupled with their impactful social media presence, sets them apart. Their sentimental robot name reflects the close-knit bond they share, like a family united in their pursuit of excellence

This team exemplifies what spirit truly means in FIRST. Their enthusiasm about their team, community, and education in STEM inspires students to be passionate members in their schools, and underserved communities. The spirit of this team is apparent in their efforts working with FLL teams, boys and girl scouts, and even when they're at robo-recess.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: When this team was burnt down, they rose from the ashes. With multiple recycling programs and initiatives to share their knowledge with the next generation, this team truly understands the importance of sustainability. They're like aluminum, the material that’s always up for a can-do attitude towards recycling.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: With their custom AI hungry to capture the note, the driver was still in control. This team filtered out sensors noise that would have sabotaged their localization. Clad in yellow, they always invest in the left most note. “Oh my lordy”…

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team could come in 4 ways but they are leaving one way. This team is carrying the competition. Just don’t mess with Toucan, he will be toting you around.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Partnering with sponsors, politicians and the media, this team advocates for FIRST funding. They demonstrate to girls that they can be engineers and challenges world leaders to improve Women in STEM initiatives worldwide. From airshows to Pentagon visits, we cannot wait to see how these girls soar.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: They have a plan from beginning to end. They lean back as they fling notes during Auto and then make sure they trap every note in their Crescendo. As they light up the field, you will find them at the end of the Spectrum!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This southwest team really knows about helping their fellow peers. They shake up teams near and far helping I pits at competitions, hosting international teams and even bringing parts to worlds for global teams who cannot afford them. Every roll is a 7 with these students.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team hit all the right notes during Crescendo. Having their on melody, their theme can be seen from uniform, to robot, to pit. Watch this team “Shake Their Tail feathers” to accept the Imagery Award.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team led the charge with their sleek black design and modern automotive styling. Their smooth form fitting 3D shells could not cover up their robots consistently fast scoring. Canada would be proud of these rams.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team came together with a creative and innovative design, which resulted in giving the team beautiful harmonics. They came out of hibernation to “swivel” around the field like a “turret”. Say “CHEESE” R2D2 Major!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team creates leaders in the north of their country to make possible the teenage dreams. At the same time, they demonstrate the fun. They have only one color, and that is purple for all.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s pit crew reminded the judges of a Formula-1 crew with their efficient, focused robot checks. Their robot was designed to be both robust and easily repairable, with modularity thoughout. This team’s robot glows with care and quality, but relax----it is not radioactive!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: These rookies are true all stars. They may be wet behind the ears, but are not slowed by the lack of resources. They turn trash into treasure creating a sleek robot design. Their game notes are flawless. Why buy it if you can print it? Let’s go search for buried treasurer as we call all hands on deck for this one-piece team.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Finding sponsors, promoting FIRST -----that is how this team Crescendos. Bi-monthly this team promotes STEM to students who have not previously seen robots. This team shares knowledge with the community, other teams, and exchanges parts to ensure everyone has a great event. Determined to compete this year, the team even shipped their robot pieces in suitcases and rebuilt it before the regional event.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Traveling abroad did not turn their mood azul. Using subteams to spread their enthusiasm of STEM, this team created educational materials and produced them in multiple languages. Creativity, intelligence and collaboration will remind you of their mascot that has 3 hearts and pulls you in with it tentacles.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This crusading team has built a strong army. They not only mentor FLL, and FTC but have written curriculum for FLL to be implemented in the classroom. Sound the trumpets this team is forging the future.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
