records.script: This team could do it all- scoring all the field elements. Beyond that their robust autonomous ability to position and pass notes to alliance partners impressed the judges. They consistently scored multiple notes. Just like Hiccup, this team has definitely trained their dragon.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team blew the judges away with their creativity. Their trap mechanism gave them an advantage on the field. These bird’s robot is soaring high on the winds they blow.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.script: With their community that is like a family, this team connects with their across all ages. They ensure that there are no barriers to STEAM access through their diverse outreach. Much like their theme this year, they can be anything they want to be.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.script: This team’s members gave a golden systems explanation. The judges were spinning their heads trying to follow their elegant multi-directional intake. Left or right, the notes twist into the perfect position for their stage to lift off.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.script: This team exemplifies the FIRST core values. They have empowered themselves to advocate for STEAM. Class is back in session with this team through their work together to bring a winning positive attitude to the field and an unwavering focus on working together that has brought physics, robotics, and AP courses to their school.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team had us tickled pink with how they integrated their unique colors in their attire and on their robot. Their theme creates a fun and exciting atmosphere. They have painted a masterpiece of success with their symphony of teal and pink.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team blew the judges away. Their attention to detail, inspiring integration, and excellent performance is perfectly complimented by their distinct décor. They were completely in the zone and left us green with envy.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.script: This team came onto the scene with a compact but mighty bot. Their innovative systems design allowed them to intake and shoot almost simultaneously while travelling. Talk about cycle time! This team’s unrivaled speed and acceleration has propelled them into orbit.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.script: This team spoke to the judges in so many ways. Across their many initiatives, this team makes sure that their message of STEM is accessible around the world. The judges are proud to recognize this team for their work on communication inclusion.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.script: This team rode in on their horse to deliver a masterpiece. They utilized the field as a part of their consistent intake. Let’s saddle up and take a ride with this outlaw.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.script: This team worked hard to overcome their challenges. They excelled in making partnerships in their community. This team stands out like stars in the sky.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.script: This team’s passion for outreach is inspiring. In a short amount of time they have made connections, created opportunities, and contributed to their community. They make us hungry to see what they will do next.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.script: Empowering their voice has the green light on this team. They have an overflowing enthusiasm and community that unites them to achieve more.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division sponsored by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Inspiring the youth with their multi-year pledge they thrive. Creating leaders as their spirit drives. With ducks at their side, they keep afloat. Sustaining success, on every note they wrote.

Autonomous mode is like a quickly moving water. So, the limelights, encoders, and software have to stick together, even when someone gets sick. If you want the notes together in the river then you have to use the Otter Pilot.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: In a competition where innovation “sparks” success, one team’s ideas were “electrifying”. They “charged” forward with their inventive solutions, “energizing” the entire competition. They are a lightning strike of creativity.

On the forefront of innovation, one team’s creation is as bright as their aspirations. Competent planning, documentation, and execution came together to help them blast off to new heights. Even the flamingos agree, PINK is a color of excellence.

When the competition faced collisions and setbacks, this team navigated a smoother course for all. They offered assistance and cushioned blows, ensuring fair play and cooperation. Proudly padding the way for others, Gracious professionalism is in their ingredients.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Many teams were dressed as a theme, but one shines brighter than the rest. From their robot to their uniforms, they told a unified story. While they may not live on Drury Lane, this team “ate and left no crumbs.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team learned from past seasons and used a detailed process to figure out their wants and needs. The inputs from more than 10 cameras went into weighted algorithms. Using animal instincts and integrated tech, this team really rammed their way to the top.

The advantage of hardware controls is the SPEED. But the POWER of software is in the simulation of the robot, field, and video. Of course, what wins is the MANEUVERABILITY of notes to the bot, aiming, and shooting.

With each sale of their delicious treats this team was able to “Open Doors” to a better future for their community. They were unstoppable in their mission to make the world a better place. These STEAMing alligators invited the world to experience their warlock.

This slick bot’s quality workmanship lurks in every component and play. It unfolds from the murky depths to score consistently from afar. This bottom-feeding, note-eating green monster is born to withstand the elements of the game.

Originating from their vibrant, rhythmic area, this team embodies the spirit of innovation. Together they are making waves in the world of STEM. Their recent publication of a book showcases their dedication to spreading knowledge and inspiring others, solidifying their status as innovators in their community.

This team is an Amplified Advocate for FIRST in their community. With Women in leadership positions they are primed for success. They have started and mentored multiple FIRST program teams in their area and around the globe, hosting many annual competitions. They also have been instrumental in orchestrating a FIRST Alumni Network in their area, and have filled Major Key Volunteer at both their own, and FIRST regional, competitions. They have Harmonious long-standing partnerships with their Sponsors, including NASA, and when a Hurricane struck their state, they opened their workspace to provide assistance to fellow teams. Hosting outreach events at regional airshows and parades, They are always On-The-Go, and have shown true to their Song, that Access to STEM should not have a pricetag, and that anyone can be a Sculp-TOR of Tomorrow.
Despite facing an initial fog for being new, the buzz of excitement sparked by their community work spread their success to competition. This team quickly found clear skies in the yellow haze.

Hailing from the west but not too far west, this purple team is cohesive down to the ones & zeros! This team excels in honoring their mascot designer by naming all their components after him! Definitely not the “B” team, Jeremy would be proud!

This team’s dedication shines through as they mentor young minds, build innovative labs and engineer robots with a knack for finding rings. They truly embody the spirit of FIRST with every circuit and gear, just don’t ask them to break a twenty.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team's eco-quest started with beach cleanup and community recycling, serving up a slice of sustainability! Now, they're topping it off by lighting up lives with solar panels for families without electricity, all while cooking up partnerships with corporations and government to keep the dough rolling in. This team is baking up a cheesy masterpiece!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.script: Ladies and gentlemen, gather round as we celebrate a team that blazed through the competition with the precision of a well-programmed robot. This team not only set the field ablaze with their consistent performance but also added an inferno of value to their alliance as they adapted to unexpected twists truly making them stand out on the field. Let’s give it up for team 4458, Infernobotics.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Most teams thought that the best way to solve this year’s challenge would require building some form of Shooter mechanism. But one team demonstrated Creativity by building a simple, effective solution with a frisbee-holder. The 2024 Creativity Award goes to Team 1744, the Robo-Rays.

In the heart of the wilderness, where nature's creatures roam amidst the whirring of technology, a team has emerged as true pioneers of engineering excellence. Their creation, a beacon shining through the mist of competition, stands as a testament to their professional approach and dedication to the design process, leaving other teams buzzing with admiration. Their solutions, born out of rigorous problem-solving, are not just functional and practical; they are as graceful as a heron's flight and as stealthy as an alligator's glide on the field of play. Like masterful creatures, they have sculpted their robot to perfection, ensuring that every component serves a purpose and contributes to their success. With excitement and admiration, we announce that the winners of the Engineering Excellence Award is: Team 179, Children of the Swamp!

The Florida Regional was graced by the presence of an exceptional team from the big apple. They embody the principles of FIRST core values in action and answered the call to support other teams throughout the event. This team consistently demonstrates a commitment to being a positive pulse… on the field, in the pits, and in their community. It is our honor to present The Gracious Professionalism Award to Team 694 - Stuypulse!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The team shows their team’s identity in their pit, their team outfits, and a well-designed robot. They embrace the theme of Crescendo, promote their sponsors with an iconic sponsor panel on their robot, and decorate their team with memorable accessories. This team’s imagery is out of this world. Presenting the Imagery Award for the 2024 South Florida regional to team 1523, MARS.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot's elegant design not only mesmerizes but is a force to be reckoned with. It's highly effective performance on the field is matched by it's beauty, and is known across all galaxies. Congratulations to Team 5557 bbr8ers for their stellar achievement in industrial design!

Let's give a thunderous applause to our deserving winners of the Innovation in Control Award! This FIRST team has hit the right note in innovation, harmonizing their vision control systems with AI to play their notes as effortlessly, like a symphony orchestra. Their ability to conduct an ensemble of hardware, software, and AI, even amidst a few offbeat attempts in navigation, shows a composition of true genius and teamwork. Bravo, Team 59 Rams!

We'd like to share a story of determination. This team turned challenges into triumphs and showcased tenacity and Grace in the face of adversity. Their knack for cleverness proved that true innovation (and their underpants) know no bounds. Join me in celebrating their True Grit by giving a roaring round of applause for the team that brought a touch of Turkish delight to their hard work during the competition— team 8861, "06 Angora".

In terms of speed, this team was fast and sometimes furious, with power and extreme maneuverability. No matter how much they were challenged, they continued to perform flawlessly, that any Formula 1 driver would envy them. They were in command of Quality Congratulations Team 180

Within the realm of the FIRST kingdom... These young engineers inspire fellow teams as well as mentors, teachers and even their administrators. These brave explorers encounter all manner of animals that roam here... along with their cub ... SCOUTS. When receiving their new workspace, they encountered an error: safety not found. So they took it into their own hands. Good job resolving that 404, and congratulations team 3627

This team has made their mark in STEAM by focusing their efforts on a medley of initiatives that echoes the rhythm of this extremely diverse community. Their priority is identifying specific needs to create achievable goals and then reaching them with harmonious outcome. Their team orchestrates it so that everyone can perform dressed for success. They've taught us that the best way to create a masterpiece is to innovate through iteration. Congratulations, Team 108

This team was founded by a dynamic force of two young ladies. Like their engineering contemporaries, Gates, Bezos, and Jobs, this newly formed team started out of their garage as well. Standing out as a beacon of innovation and inspiration, this community-based team was formed by students representing six different schools forged by their passion for engineering under the heat of Florida. True to these qualities and attributes, please share in our recognition of team 9404 - FORGE, as this year’s Rookie All-Star.

In a very short time and after many long nights, this team was able to assemble their first robot. Like in the Colosseum, their courage in the face of adversity inspired awe and admiration. This team earned the Rookie Inspiration. Congratulations Team 9779 Gladiator Robotics!

The roaring energy of the crowd, fused with the team’s unstoppable determination, created an electrifying atmosphere that fueled their drive to succeed. With the ferocity of their team mascot, they tackled each challenge head on, never backing down in the face of adversity. They showed the best Team Spirit. Congratulations Team 6743 Fusion

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: When we think about engineering quality products, a team needs to consider how an innovation improves the lives of those who use or are affected by that innovation. Bringing our creative juices to those even beyond our robotic domain is an objective we all aspire to achieve. Our Sustainability Award Recipient creates not just a wonderful robot, but it quenches our thirst for helping others and improving lives. This team not only thinks outside the box; they also think about how to fill the box with the key fuel for life itself. We are proud that one Disruptive Innovation coming from FIRST is a mechanism for delivering clean, filtered, water to the people of Kenya. Congratulations to Disruptive Innovation for the 2024 Sustainability Award!

This team started each match off by quickly scoring points while being completely hands off. Contrary to the robot's name, they had a lot of teeth during the competition and really ate up all the notes.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team had numerous iterations of their design to come up with a unique function. They traveled here from Atlanta, Georgia and are NOT Rusty despite what some believe. This team has some of the most hungry students here creating the bagel launcherrrrrrrrr.

This team's outreach and community engagement was extensive and impressive. Through showcases, training labs, and targeted campaigns to special populations, these middle Georgians are inspiring future generations in STEM. If you want to soar, choose this team as your wing man.

This team goes out of their way to assist any team in need. They stand tall in their community on and off the field! Like Johnny Appleseed they have planted the message of FIRST both within and outside their community. Now… count the letters. This team was Confident, Calm, Cool and Collected in front of the judges. When they are out on the field you can hear the coming due to their high frequency!!

This team manufactured their own parts when the odds were stacked against them. Their mini tournaments prepared them for what was to come creating co-opertition. This team is like a bull in a china shop if you aren’t in their alliance.

This team may just be getting started but with their positive attitude they are prepared to run the distance. Their teamwork shines through everything they do. Just like C3PO from Star Wars, they shine like gold.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Danger Danger on the Way We make AI the old school way Flint to Ignite and save the day

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's robot design achieves a remarkable balance of distinctive form, practical function, and breathtaking aesthetics. The sleek, shiny exterior of their robot reflects a dedication to excellence, while its engineered low center of gravity ensures stability and agility on the field. With their fiery determination this team turns up the heat to HOT!
This team has amazing controls and professionally engineered components. They successfully made the journey from Suwannee to join us here today. Emerging as the relentless Michelin champions….

This metro Atlanta team faced challenges on and off the field last season. To overcome those challenges, these hard-working future engineers and programmers recruited a new collection of pirates to help them take a bite out of the competition. The judges would like to award the "More Than Robots Award" to Team 6905.

This mythical creature brought the quality, from the immaculate condition of their pit, to the lean, clean design of their robot. Their fame and acclaim will be legion by the time this competition is over. And, just so we're clear, the name of their robot is CADENCE, not Candice!

This team energized the crowd with an electric spirit, this team sparked a connection that even Odin would admire. Now, let’s raise a cheer that thunders and hammers in honor of the Wild Bots and their mighty Thor.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: In the arena where metal reigns, A team emerges, their vision sustains. With a staff in hand, they chart their course, crafting a legacy with eco-force. Through storms of bolts, their practices shine, their sustainability tale, their story sells.
Left to its own devices, this team’s robot starts each match strong. When it flies out to make quick early scores, you’ll hear it coming. Team 7451 Avengers!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.teamName: Career Blazer Robotics - The Fighting Mongooses
records.script: This team understands what it means to tow the line and make room for your friends. We have all heard of a ball and chain holding you down. This team has taught us that a wheel and chain can lift you up. Instead of lifting by winding up, this team decided to lift by rolling along. The creativity award goes to the team with the little blue wheel that could, Team 5900!

This little team is small but mighty. If you ask them what their middle name is, we suspect they would answer “outreach”. Keep doing what you do to Rocket to success. Congratulations team 4188 Columbus Space Program!

This team is very well organized, like a small corporation with a diverse membership. They have an awesome history but what is most impressive is how they constantly evolve to be more effective in promoting FIRST within their community, Georgia and beyond. On paper, you know the FLAT 2-dimensional stuff we write on, they have a lot of accomplishments. Since their formation years ago, they have established key relationships with their sponsors and are frequently called upon to be ambassadors for GeorgiaFIRST. While they are very competitive on the field, they are the first to assist other teams at competitions. Over the last few years, they have started FTC teams and hosted FLL tournaments in addition to other activities including distribution of STEM kits. Did you know they have also been in a movie? They can CRUSH cans very effectively, but they do not crush their competition instead they build them up on and off the field. You know them as WALT. We all know them for being FIRST SUPERHEROS that represent what FIRST is all about.

From a well organized pit, full of competent and fast moving hands, emerges an engineering marvel. Low by design, to keep the machine on the ground, and keep running even in the fiercest of matches. Two inch shooter wheels, well dressed wiring, and custom fixed gear for sturdy arm angles, reveal radiant engineering hexagon up the competition. Congratulations Team 1414 IHOT!

When other teams needed assistance, this team helped them stand back up again. They were seen aiding others in and out of the pits, showing amazing sportsmanship throughout the competition. They wear the golden crown of Gracious Professionalism, team 5109 Gladiator Robotics.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The gentle giants have set themselves apart in a sea full of gladiators, warriors, and knights. From their mellow pit design to their themed onesies, this team has “lei’d” the foundation for fun on and off the field, and “hula-ed” their way into our hearts. You’ll want to be on their alliance, so you too, can go home with a cuddly new friend.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s name tells you where they are from and what they can do. Top notch documentation describes their journey and their design. Overall solid design included over the bumper intake, chain lock slot, and solid controls for a robot named Fluffy.

This team absolutely nailed it, showing total “control” both on and off the field. With stellar performance on and off the field and after an incredibly engaging and comprehensive walkthrough on their integration process in a vintage garage atmosphere, the Innovation in Control Award was snagged by Robotz Garage, team 4451, from South Carolina!

This team grew 675% over four months. They have a three prong approach for students to learn and grow in the shop and even at home. They collaborated with other school clubs to ensure their FLL teams had consistent mentorship. The Metal Mindset Award goes to 5293 the Metal Crusaders!

This team’s clean wiring and care for their robot aided them well. They overcame their technical issues and danced their way up the rankings. It takes more than a hit to knock this queen off her throne. Congratulations 1648 G3 robotics!

Finding that right starting point and keeping focus is often a challenge for rookie teams, but not for this team. Their professional business plan, collaboration with commercial sponsors, community outreach, and ability to continually adapt their robot has allowed them to align all the axes for developing an FRC team and homing in on success. Congratulations Team 9500 G28 Robotics, our Rookie All-Stars!

It’s hard to find the equation for inspiration, especially for rookie teams. Through the development of their team, outreach into their feeder schools, and dedication to the ideals of FIRST … Eureka! This team found it! Congratulations 9522 Archimedes!
This team can really get into robotics. They come together to celebrate wins big and small. Their excitement for STEM is contagious. 9057 G.I.R.L.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: We got a charge out of this award. They use energy anyone can afford by using batteries that are much larger. The sustainability award is won by Team 4819 Chargers!

Swirling and whirling across the field, this fast robot can aim and score from anywhere within range. This robot picks up notes, positions itself, and scores with simple switch actuations. Like a musical artist hears a note and hits a tune. This Robot sees a robot and makes a turn.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has developed a highly creative and unique feature for their robot, the uniqueness of this creative element lies in its practical application, as it allows their robot to efficiently and effectively use their over the bumper intake. It is worth mentioning that perfecting this unique mechanism took six iterations, demonstrating the team's perseverance and commitment to achieving optimal performance. This team knows how to use their finger (claw)!

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: Navigating the FIRST landscape with fresh eyes, a team embraced the Core Values with open arms, fostering collaborations that transcended their rookie status. Their strategic recruitment from middle schools laid the groundwork for a growing community pipeline. For their initiative and embodiment of FIRST principles.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: Standing together and radiating a determined stare, this rookie team clears through the clouds with a ray of technological determination. Within their rookie year, they showed their dedication through a variety of community activities, leadership, clear vision, and "bear-arrific" spirit!

This award requires defining the problem, researching the rules of the game, brainstorming and developing the best engineering solution. Along the path, there will be roadblocks and hurdles to overcome in order to “rise above the ashes!” This team has shown all of these steps including a notebook with detailed images, code analysis, electrical diagrams, and step by step assembly.

This team has planted the seeds of compassion and cultivated a bountiful harvest of kindness not only in competition, but in their community as well. Through tireless dedication, passion, and teamwork, this remarkable group has used hydroponics to transform a food desert into a flourishing oasis, brimming with vibrant produce that they donate to their local community. From the pits to their gardens, let's celebrate the generosity of this team.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: In a realm where creativity and resourcefulness intersect, a team stitched together a masterpiece from a diverse array of components, each piece telling its own tale of past glories. Their robot, a testament to inventive reassembly, mirrored the classic tale of creation from remnants. Congratulations to these mad scientists!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team turned up the temperature in the judges room with gears that spin and a sleek slim skin this robot was built to win where cool gets hot, WHO IS HOT!!

Operating from the outskirts of Atlanta. This team impressed the judges with remarkable robot automation and even implementing well considered code checks and failsafe's ensuring that robot still stays competitive in the heat of competition. This team is well deserving for this award proving that even the king of the jungle can master coding.

In a land where gears and rhymes intertwine, a team with a mission so fine, they blended art with the craft of design. With tales in tomes and robots that roam, they brought stories to light, in every home. Building libraries small but grand, spreading knowledge across the land. And so, with joy, we celebrate and commend, for their tale of STEAM has found its splendid end.

This FIRST year swerve drive team have implemented redundancy and risk mitigation measures, ensuring that their robot maintains functionality even in the face of unexpected challenges. From the meticulous workmanship, reliable robot sub systems, well organized wiring, flawless paint job, and having their team mustache throughout their robot, the entire machine exudes excellence. Additionally, the oldest "Green" team in the Peachtree District takes pride in their unique feature of driver station feedback through controller vibration which enhances control and precision on the field.

In the heart of Georgia, a high-flying team spreads their wings, not just conquering challenges in the arena but also lifting others to new heights. Their digital prowess extended beyond borders, as they guided peers through the virtual skies, and their ingenuity shone brightly with a pioneering app, breaking down barriers and opening the world of robotics to young minds of all abilities. Congratulations to this beacon of innovation and inclusivity.

In the heart of the rugged countryside, where the tumbleweeds roll and the sun sets low, this remarkable team has been blazing trails and inspiring minds. For them, it's about changing the engineering frontier for their community for generations to come, through educational and community volunteer work, as well as fundraising for a STEM hub that all can enjoy. With lassos in hand, they've shown that engineering knows no bounds, even in the most rural of landscapes.

This team’s essay and presentation showcased their dedication to innovation, community engagement and spreading message of FIRST. Their unwavering commitment to improving the opportunities of all students has empowered a diverse group of young minds, inspiring a new generation of STEM leaders. Their efforts created an unstoppable storm called Marvin, proving that they don’t just navigate the storm of challenges – they redefine the eye of innovation.

This team’s performance propelled them into the spotlight as true leaders in innovative outreach efforts. The use of social media and focus on growing diversity in STEM proved that with determination and teamwork, they can conquer any frontier. These efforts hit all the right notes, demonstrating that with bravery and determination, they can shoot for the stars and achieve out of the world greatness.

With a flare of red, white, and blue this Rookie team is encompassed with fighting purple perseverance. Showing a staunch determination to meet every challenge during their rookie year, they have marched forward while leaving a blazing trail of FIRST core values at every turn.

In a sea of teams, one stood out through the waves as a beacon of camaraderie, positivity, and unwavering spirit. Their commitment to fostering a welcoming and inclusive environment didn't just "light up" the crowd, but it created a tidal wave of enthusiasm that swept through every challenge they faced. Leaving ripples of cheer in their wake, let's hear it for the Manatees!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team, not unlike a league of heroes, crafted a sustainable future through a "Tree of Mentorship," planting the seeds of curiosity and nurturing talent from the ground up. Their journey, marked by acts of kindness and a pioneering academic path, speaks to their commitment to education and supporting their wider community. For ensuring a secure and sustainable future for their team, they are a Marvel in the community!

Their programming may seem BASIC but these coders let their robot take control. This team can rack up points with their hands tied behind their backs. They may be retro, but they are no eight bit hacks.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team did the math and it was not pretty. They realized that two motors are better than one. These docile swimmers took the plunge for skillful scoring.
This team has an un-blockable dedication to inspiring and requiring future members. It is "OTTO" - matic how they keep it stupid simple.

Making an impact takes more than a song; it requires building through a crescendo to have intended impact. Taking FIRST to the community requires the whole team. Sometimes you have to run for President to have an impact. A superhero can impact a large number of people using STEM as their super power at STEM nights but a team of superheroes can really make a difference!

From brainstorming to modelling to prototyping this crew had a thorough design process for their robot. They took flight with their skillful method of development. This team of EAGLE-NEERS is far from winging it.

records.teamName: Career Blazer Robotics - The Fighting Mongooses
records.script: FIRST core values are demonstrated with positive attitude on and off the field whether you need a part, help with building or even inspiration. This hometown team is ferociously ready to help.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's dynamic fusion of creativity and technical ingenuity soared them to victory. The team adorned in shimmering gold hues dazzled the judges. They seamlessly blended the mythical and the technical with a mascot symbolizing renewal and a life sized walking cardboard robot.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team combined rugged design with pristine style. This bot TOWERS over the REST. This MOUNTAIN can't be moved.
This team's control system was designed to utilize autos, beam brakes and april tags to strategically work with their alliances. Make NO FLUFF about it this team could go global by any other name.
This team originates from a city with a "C." They are the team to call when you really need a HAND. Their outreach has E-nabled people around the world.

This team's robot had a compact design that held up to the heat of the competition. Even when a part broke, they had a backup plan so they did not miss a match. This winning team does not need the help of magic spells.

In competition a good coach will focus a team on the fundamentals of the contest. From humility and hard work this team earned respect on and off the field in their first year. Their school and the team really CARE which inspired their team name!

records.teamName: Victory Church of Christ Robo Knights
records.script: The future of robotics is a truly bright inspiring unity with the help of a higher power. These knights do not need a round table, they gather around a programming station instead.
Do not think they are that grouchy! Loud support can be heard in the stands for themselves and others. We've got spirit yes we do, we've got spirit how about you....oi-oi-oi.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has more experience with sustainability than their number suggests. When the previous team dissolved, a new team exploded onto the scene. They turned to defense when their stick went BOOM.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.script: This team has consistently helped their alliances get to 6 or 7 overall autonomous speaker notes. They can consistently take the longer and harder shots. This team’s autonomous functions make them a great alliance partner, not just a lone wildcat!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team impressed the judges with a unique turbine to open a TRAP door without touching it. This robot was a masterpiece with an arm and shooter system folding and unfolding like a transformer. They demonstrated unique creativity by folding such a complicated shooting and climbing system into such a small box.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.script: This team demonstrated a strong commitment to advancing STEM not only in their local community, but also throughout the world. They developed and introduced CAD curriculum to spread STEM throughout their school district. They then spread their message of empowerment of women across 6 different continents. They went above and beyond in their neck of the woods to mentor and teach other teams how to rebel against the status quo.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.script: Using their keen senses, this team seeks precision and excellence to outsmart their opponents. Their relentless pursuit of innovation and automation allows single user control to perform multiple complex tasks. Innovation is their bark and technology is their bite. They fetch solutions with a wag of their tails and a byte of code.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.script: This team strives to be a paragon of gracious professionalism in everything they do. Their catalog of workshops, magazine publications, and hosting solutions for international teams helped many to be prepared. Our judges found in this team a PEAR-fect example of FIRST core values.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s red-eyed robot caught the judge’s attention when visiting their pit. They enjoy bonding with other teams by rocking out in the garage. This team hit their crescendo with its heavy metal theme!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team worked through multiple iterations to achieve their high auto score. This team was able to interweave their use of CAD and wooden prototypes to perfect their design. Even though it was black and sleek, this charging team was no dark horse!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.script: This team created several components that were innovative, resulting in this robot efficiently and effectively operating in the field of play. Implementation of one of their unique components was a major improvement that enabled the robot to score easily – and that’s not just blowing hot air! The judges all know this team will greatly APPRECIATE this award.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.script: Turning pages to find new ways of sharing the message of FIRST has been the practice of this team. By EXPOSING friends to their robot, the have ENGAGED and INSPIRED the joy of participation in FIRST in many places, including shelters. Even beyond their technical achievement, they have turned trouble into opportunity because they BELIEVE that everyone can be a MAKER.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.script: This team built a robust bot able to withstand the rigors of this competition. Features like their custom PCBs, aircraft construction techniques, and 3D printed herringbone gears catapulted them to the top. These warriors have the qualities to achieve anything!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.script: This rookie team demonstrated efforts far outside the standard deviation with their strong robot and outstanding impact in their community. This team improvises, including custom printing 3D gears and developing their strong shooter. They adapt their outreach to meet the diverse needs in their country, reaching over thousands of people with FIRST’s message. This team has helped establish 7 robotics labs in underserved schools across the country helping these students overcome challenges to learn more about robotics and STEM.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.script: With a focus on outreach and advocacy, this rookie team demonstrated they are already off to a fast start. From creating an organization focused on upholding women in STEM to their work creating new FIRST teams, they are focused on the impact that FIRST can have on students. They have demonstrated the success of their LADDER program to help students grow skills through FLL, FTC, and FRC. This team embraced the A in STEAM with their incredible pit display and student-made plush dinosaurs.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.script: This team has brought the spirit of FIRST to their small community in a big way. The energy and excitement they’ve raised shows them to be more than a mere TADPOLE. The growing change they are inspiring is definitely a reason to turn on PARTY MODE.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division sponsored by BAE Systems
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team maintains their team and the TREES through LONG-running sustainable programs. They help ensure their team’s continuity through multiple environmental events. When it comes to sustainable teams, they lead the PACK.
Autonomously, their speed and accuracy was hard to beat. They powered through the opposition with a roar. They lived up to their name of "Kika Mana".

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team deserves the Creativity Award for their innovative use of AI in their robot's autonomous functions, and the clever integration of rollers designed to increase spin of the note for precise launching. These local kids' meticulous risk mitigation strategies, practical applications, and creativity not only set them apart but also greatly contributed to their success on the field.

This team designed its code to be remotely de-bugged as its robot travels from region to region. Team members explained the engineering design and process, sensors and data, modularity and materials. Managing data from many sources like a spider with many legs, this team's Rythm impressed the judges with engineering excellence.

This team showed that it's not how far you travel, but how you get to where you're going that counts... and they traveled a long way. They overwhelmed their peers with help, happiness, joy, ... and stroopwaffles. They soldered so many relationships with other teams that they were a favorite for this award among their peers. The "force" behind this team is about more than just winning.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team came to the competition ready to ROCK! Wise enough to amplify this year's Crescendo theme, they incorporated gold records, flying V guitars, and so much excitement that they had some left to S.P.A.R.E. Their robot swooped onto the field undoubtly showing "HOO" they are!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When it comes to packaging, this team has an Amazon beat. They designed a concise, sleek, and compact robot that outshines the rest. They epitomize the elegance of industrial design.

When it comes to controls, this team emerged large and in charge. This bot used an autonomous aiming system that relayed readiness to fire by a vibrating controller. Match observations revealed the capability of Bothoven to accurately fire into the speaker from various positions.

This team deserves the Judge’s Award for their exceptional resilience in overcoming cultural and continuity challenges. Their charging approach to self-teaching and documentation, coupled with extensive outreach efforts to inspire younger generations, ’amp’lifies their dedication to both their team and the broader robotics community.
This team took a short flight to Oahu to compete. Their design is durable, redundant, and easy to main and repair. This is an excellent example of "Kauai"-lity quality engineering.

This team not only builds certifiable robots for competition, they also build bots to explore under the sea. In addition to creating STEM academies and summer camps, this team invests in professional development, by requiring team members to get certified in safety, manufacturing, and milling, and as a by-product, Ha Ha Lua was born. This team drives hard to reach the Summit, while inspiring, empowering, and building the next generation of community-focused STEM students and professionals.

This team empowers indigenous and underserved communities, weaving technology with heritage to sculpt a future that honors the past. As torchbearers of change, they ignite the flames of innovation, preserving cultural identity while fostering global communities. They blaze a trail of diversity, equity, and inclusion in STEM. The winner of the FIRST Impact Award goes to Team 2438 ‘Iobotics, from ʻIolani School!

Only 6 months old, this team's original inspiration came from Canada; and now they've taken flight, flying high from their national and international roots! As a rookie team, they've proven to be fierce competitors, reaching the Hawaii Regional finals, as an alliance partner. With excellent performance on and off the field, Musashi, the warrior and the team have proven themselves worthy of the Rookie All-Star Award.

This team's outreach efforts have blossomed beyond their countryside hometown to reach thousands of people within their community and beyond. Their robot shines like fireworks whenever they are on the field. They bring a fresh spark to the Rookie Inspiration Award.
This team's spirit cuts through any storm cloud like a bolt of lightning. Their thunderous voices ring out for both their team and their alliance partners. They are a shining example of Team Spirit.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team hails from a hot spot in Honolulu. Their foundation is strong as they continue to evolve and improve. They ignite the spirit of cooperation, community, and culture through their team's activities and successes. As we invoke the spirit of Pele, the Team Sustainability Award goes to Team 3008, Team Magma.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.script: With the use of Choreo (kor-ee-o) and containerized autonomous applications, this team ensures that they maintain the advantage on the field. They provide their simulation replay kit and data visualization scope to help other teams debug their code. When it comes to Crescendo, this team plays Presto!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s front and back intake allows them to pick up notes whether coming or going. Their climbing mechanism has allowed them to SPRING to the top of the stage! This robot’s security mechanism allows them to direct note traffic in a way that will make JoJo proud!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.script: This team is inspiring their community and building bridges between technology and societal needs. With innovative outreach programs they captivate and engage their community in STEM, while also utilizing their engineering skills to solve healthcare and environmental problems in their country. Advancing global goals and local well being, this team’s future is GOLDEN.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.script: Detailed game and data analyses were just the beginning for this team. They then artistically evolved their robot’s modular design to ensure they can just PLUG and PLAY.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.script: This team models collaboration and generosity, and inspire a love of engineering in students. When it comes to supporting FLL, FTC, and FRC teams with practice fields, camps, podcasts and more. This team puts a wrap on Brains, Braids, and Bots.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team took the Art in STEAM to heart and filled something empty with something beautiful. Their team was named as an homage to their founding sponsor, they definitely make Stephen proud.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot was designed to execute maneuvers to score points while not getting damaged. It can hang by itself or hang in harmony with another robot. With drives that can be hot swapped if needed and dressed in teal… It even has a new design element – the flexy joint.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.script: The innovative code, That this team wrote, Lets them cobble a path, From note to note. Their robot speaks, In topics and nodes, So get out of its way, Before ROS loads.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.script: This team reaches out to local, state, and federal representatives to strongly advocate for STEM philosophy change across state lines. They have a focus on improvement of computer science curriculum. They go bananas for grass roots education in computer science. The judges present The Change Agents Award

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.script: This team’s well organized wiring in the belly pan ensures on field robustness. Their automated functional checks enable the team to make sure that the robot is match ready. The judges really loved the show and tell using the 3D printed mini-model.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.script: This young team has a survival plan in place for their sustainability. And they are impacting their community from tots to seniors. Would a dinosaur do robotics? A Dino Might.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.script: This small cohesive team raised money through service to the community. Their local media has recognized them for everything from cleaning ditches to running food drives. They get their strength from LIGHTNING in a bottle.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.script: This team pounces with pride, leading the pack with their roaring spirit and fierce determination. Through initiatives like Hack a Roar, Theraplay, and Seed Camps, they engage their community and sponsors with the might of a tiger’s roar, uniting students from 21 different schools under one spirited banner. Let’s give a big round of A-PAWS to these tigers of technology.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division sponsored by Molex
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: In order to sustain themselves and others, this team has many non-competitive objectives. They represent their country well and have developed themselves both creatively and ecologically. Using collaborative methods, this team rises like a PHOENIX.
This robot scanned its surroundings and locked on its target. With turret ready and Hutz set to stun. This team MEGA-LY understood what it takes to be autonomous.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: In fields of code where circuits gleam They skillfully collect notes with creativity from any direction In yellow and green, their robot "Croppenheimer" harvested with precision.

This team swerved away from the tank steer and traveled to Cedar Falls. Using their design process, they plotted a course to amplify their design and compliment alliance partners. When it comes to Engineering Excellence, they have it all Under Control.

This outstanding team from the middle of Iowa has a great STORY to tell. From leading summer STEAM camps for youth, to sponsoring 11 FLL teams to providing any team in need with parts and tools. Even though their name is microscopic, their Gracious Professionalism is huge.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team shows a primal warmth with futuristic slickness crafted by skillful human hands. They are accompanied by visuals that inform and educate. They are worthy of an Imagery Award in the cyber and grizzly category.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team is wild in their styling design, that aces their weight reduction with elegance and sophistication. But it's not just about the design, on the playing field this team's robot performance is no joke. You can watch them hit the blackjack pot with their design.

You can see this team's innovation through their cameras. They use a specialized controller and AI to eat notes and jettison them out Their robot may be named Phantom, but their innovation in control is very real.
The judges identified a strong, diverse team. Great outreach promotes FIRST and ensures the team's future is bright. Their influence spans from the state legislature to children's literature.
This team "rocked" the state. Their clean design embodies both mechanical and electrical collaboration. They have clearly "honed" their design skills.

This team created sustainability through diversity and education. Members exemplify the FIRST mission by creating programs to change not only their team, but also the world. Who would have thought "cookies" could have helped change diversity in STEM and help recruit the next generation of robotics?

Robot design skills can be used to solve problems in the real world. Working together to strengthen elementary STEM programs. Their shop builds the next generation of doers to solve the world’s problems with confidence.
The Devil has whispered in our ear. This rookie team is a mean green fighting machine. They have truly embodied the spirit of FIRST robotics.
This team said it best - "Its not our place to teach, it's our place to learn." They came into their first competition like a cyclone. Their business plan was truly inspiring.
This team filled the stands like leaves fill a tree. Their energy not only supports their teammates but also fosters a positive team environment. They've taken team spirit to new heights.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team tries it's best not to "PUN"ish their team and our planet. Imagine new uses for broken glass and soda pop. This team is SLUGGUNG toward innovation.

When auto started this team attacked the speaker Consistently scoring more points while operating autonomously As raiders they moved lightning fast and scored for their alliance. Congratulations to TEAM 4698 Raider Robotics

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When teams are encouraged to push beyond the boundaries of convention, this team reached for heights previously unattainable. Their creativity inspires others to reach for the stars without flying too close to the sun. Congratulations to team 4598 Incarus Innovated.

This team understands how a strong design can have a big bearing on game performance. This team really knows how to press the right buttons for an effective match. Mechanical design made with input from electrical and programming to produce a robot that will leave your head spinning. Congratulations to team 6036 Peninsula Robotics.

This team from a small community has a huge impact on their state. They mentor FLL teams AND does NOT mind lending a hand to teams before, during OR after competitions. Graciously share this award with your eight FLL rookie teams. Congratulations to Team 6358 The Buhlean Operators.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is certainly visible from a distance but when they roll by the purple really flies. Orange you glad this award goes to team 399 Eagle Robotics.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s performance on the field showcases their design and build methodology. Starting with a spark, this team used modeling trial and error to create a red hot robot. Flaming on and off the field, congratulations to TEAM 2584, Flame of the West.

When Teleop starts this team mashes their buttons With push button autonomous driving they can move across the field fast This bot is definitely not a couch potato. Congratulations to TEAM 2122 Team Tators

“The Strong Values Award” This team not only built a strong robot but they value building a strong team foundation and have tons of strength to share with their remote neighboring communities. They don’t speed through the team building process and take the time to build a welcoming team atmosphere. Congratulations to TEAM 6364 Ten Ton Robotics

This team keeps it simple and stable. Their robot has layers of redundancy to endure hard impacts without compromising performance. The team’s design protects its components while making updates easy and accessible. This time flies up to 19 feet per second and can shoot into the speaker at a max speed of 95 miles per hour. Congratulations to Team 3245 Ravens.

This team represents a commitment to women and girls in STEM through their measurable success of getting more girls involved. Not only growing their team to 30% girls in one year they have ensured their voices are heard through holding half of the student leadership positions. With the support of Society of Women Engineers we are blown away by the engineering inspiration of this team. Congratulations to Team 2813 Gearheads.

records.teamName: Victorian Engineered Robotic Nation or V.E.R.N.
records.script: Seeing a need for STEAM showcasing in their state, this team took their great exhibition on the road, turning their showings into several FLL, FTC, and FRC new teams and mentorships. Please stand, take off your top hats and googles, and cheer for this year’s impact winner TEAM 5461 VERN

This redneck team is no stranger to finding hidden treasure to use for parts. From duct tapes to zip ties this team impressed us with their ingenuity and creativity. Congratulations to TEAM 9726, The Notus Pirates

In a jungle full of talented rookies, the judges spotted this rookie team for their determination and their willingness to iterate their robot. This team clawed their way to score many points in their first year. Congratulations to TEAM 9438 Leopard Tech.

WHAT team demonstrates enthusiasm through stickers, pins, cheers and props? In the lab and on the field they ratted out the competition. If you’re on the wire about the winner, look for the lab coats and congratulate TEAM 1569 Haywire

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This substantial team shows the love for disco and parties. This well managed team builds for the future with rookie workshops and a girls in hardware initiative. This team doesn’t take any chances with sustaining their troop. Congratulations to TEAM 846 The Funky Monkeys.

With its exceptional field vision, it maintains unmatched consistency during operations. Its ability to scan its surroundings with googling eyes in all directions ensures superb vision even in low light conditions, making it suitable for herding… CATS.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team is colorfully creative. As binary numbers go, they are a solid “seven”. They don’t have to WRESTLE with control of their shooter due to their stunning arm bar move.
This team impressed the judges with their processes in designing their robot. They showed their teeth in their excellent robot design. We look FORWARD to seeing them compete in the future.

This stealthy group helps across the competition; they gather intelligence to provide an arsenal of extra parts to those in need. The moment they sense trouble, this team is there as quick as a NINJA.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When this team searched for an image to show their deep commitment to FIRST values, they found the answer right under their NOSES.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: From top to bottom, this elegant robot lights up the competition. This team can dispose of notes quickly. Using their lights, they can DEFUSE any problems that arise.

This team used vision to their advantage during both their autonomous and tele-operated periods. Their implementation of machine learning algorithms was not convoluted in the slightest. This made their robot great value for the MONEY.

This community team impressed the judges on the battlefield. Their extensive collaborative efforts institutionally, in the community, and with a not-for-profit make other teams GREEN with envy. Let the Colony Rise!

This robot was well constructed, from component labeling to wiring. It was built to a plan from concept and design, tracking parts all the way to assembly. These DOGS are on the hunt for six sigma quality.

This metallic team inspires us through tremendous outreach at the Capital and STEM camps. They make us hungry with events including Burgers and Bots. This “Show me” state team’s brochure really blew the judges away with their green theme.

This team’s Impact at a glance is impressive. The team has strong community roots, with global aspirations. The team recognizes a problem, brainstorms, and manufactures solutions that add to their operating budget. State and top government recognized this team’s effort and has accordingly provided additional funding to “build a roadmap to change”. This team has been around the block and had its ups and downs while traveling. We’re not kidding around,
This team may be new, but they are already one big family. They have set their course for spreading the FIRST message. Watch out hockey, Canada has a new sport – Robotics!
This team built up their confidence along with their bot. No one could throw a WRENCH in their plans. Their passion for STEM is RIVETING.
This team’s unique brand can be recognized up close and from across the arena. Their vitality ADDS extra cheering power to other teams. Daily check-ins have amped up the wellbeing of each ONE.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: As this team has grown, they have switched their recipes. With sponsor support, they are bringing energy and technology to remote areas. One slice at a time, they take a bite of the PIZZA!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.script: This team's ability to interpolate threw their opponents for a loop. The choreography of their robot allows them to hit every note and dance around the competition. The basketball team is not the only PURDUE win this weekend. BOILER UP!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This is a small team working to solve big problems with few resources. When thrown a CURVE, they know to stay within their LIMITS. This team would definitely rather drive a TOYOTA, than a broken down CHEVY.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This team "values teamwork and communicating like engineers to accomplish greatness." No one can ECLIPSE their spirit as they compared the evolution of their robot this season to the evolution of their team. Both are adaptable and are ready to take on whatever challenges may cast a SHADOW on their path.
This team kept their strategy hidden UNDER THE STAGE. From Safety to Compatibility, they overcame their obstacles like a TANK. The judges felt they stuck to their process with PRIDE.

On or off the field, this team's collaboration with other FRC teams has no global bounds. When other teams are seeing RED, this team always steps up to help. It is not ALARMING that this team is Gracious and Professional, always ready to tell everyone "CHALLENGE ACCEPTED".

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has PAINTED a visual cohesion between their robot, pit, and team. They can be seen smiling...while SHUFFLING SIDEWAYS across the field. No need to PINCH yourself awake, sleeping beauty has already left the CASTLE.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's design was FORTISSIMO and hit just the right notes. They planned to crash like a symbol, but with cameras 360, they dodged and weaved, scoring with ease. The only thing they didn't show the judges is their advanced hidden ALIEN technology.

This team can drive with one hand tied behind their back. Their take on logging is refreshing and the use of simulation provides a clear vision to success. With a rapid refresh rate they can beat any HOUND in this robot race.

Though this team is small in size, they stand out for their ability to work in harmony. The many hats they wear prevent them from being KICKED around. No matter what happens, they always perform with a DEVILISH smile. Receiving the OLD BOT NEW TRICKS award.

This team impressed with a harmony of design and color. Chaining notes through an efficient design and a plan for failure, with BLUE and GREEN they are all together. This team exemplifies Quality without compare, don't be deceived by the BOWS in their hair.

With a focus for the inclusion of putting the A in STEM, they are STEAMing up the competition. Attending their summer camps is a BADGE of honor, successfully recruiting students to engineering and paying particular attention to their pipeline, doubling the number of their FLL and FTC teams. Their increasing efforts inspired the judges, so look out for their Next INVASION!

BOYS & GIRLS this team has made a lasting IMPACT on the FIRST COMMUNITY. They have MOBILIZED their outreach efforts with new partnerships in their community. As a PACK, this team has definitely CHANGED LIVES, BUILT ROBOTS.

In the few short months since their founding, this team has made it to the front of their class. They are engineering a high definition future with their downloaded plans. We cannot wait for them to take their ideas out of storage, and continue to transform them into inspiration.

From their strong connections with their school, to their dedication to supporting local business, this team sings with a passion. Their bright colors, ingenuity, and infectious enthusiasm has allowed them to grow from a small flame to a roaring BLAZE!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team ensures their longevity through strong recruitment and reuse of material. With a sound understanding that recycling, especially their batteries, is instrumental, they are leaping into the future with PRECISION.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: This robot can compete on air, land, and sea. Their ability to track and follow notes helps them stay in the LIMELIGHT, and blend in with CORAL. Their adaptable autonomous modes THRUST them to early leads. Congratulations 1501 - Team THRUST

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team geared up for a risky ADVENTURE. They explored a new path, picking up notes from three sides with a unique and simple intake. In their crusade, they founded their small robotics family! Congratulations 3947 - The Last Crusaders

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: Sharing their passion for robotics with younger kids around the world, has this team reaching for the stars. They're definitely GROOVIN' through the universe. Congratulations 4926, Galec Tech

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: With a focus on growth of FIRST in southern Indiana, this team lets everyone know they are MAKING AN IMPACT. Support of many teams from kickoff, mentoring young FRC teams navigate the challenges of the season, and even including them in trip planning and booking their hotels. This team will never raise their drawbridge, they welcome all to their CASTLE. Congratulations 6498 - Castle Robotics

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: When it comes to building robots, you have to have your EYE on the prize. A design process to ACCURATELY meet your needs might just do the trick. In fact, this team was PRECISELY on point. Congratulations 3176, Purple Precision!

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: Other teams will always be welcome at this team's house. They are GRANTING access to a large block of land to make a machine shop and practice facility. We can't believe a PHYXT team could be so flexible! Congratulations 1720, Phyxt Gears

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team rises up the challenge of FIRST. They impressed the judges by their IMAGINATIVE integration of their theme not only in their robot, also in the heart and soul of their team. Whenever the judges saw this team, they gave us PANDA-MANIA!! Congratulations 1747 - Harrison Boiler Robotics!

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's BREAKAWAY design impressed the judges. With LAYERS of protection, they created a strong BASE of success. KA-CHOW!! to team 3452 - GreengineerZ

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: This team innovated by first building their robot within a virtual simulation. They have done the math and physics to optimize their controls to drive with only four buttons. They love to HOUND the competition. Congratulations 868 - TechHOUNDS!

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: This young, scrappy team is hungry for opportunities to grow. Their cowboy mentality may look chaotic but their focus is FUN. They made the impossible possible when they gave new life to TEDDY. Congratulations 4008, Theodore Roosevelt's Disco Haircut!

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: Don't let the GREEN disguise this robust robot. If their modular intake breaks, it can simply fly off into SPACE. ...OOPS! Sorry... I guess this information is no longer CLASSIFIED. Congratulations 5188, Classified Robotics!

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: This team has started with the RIGHT FOOT FORWARD, engaging and demonstrating all values of FIRST. Their robot is designed effectively and efficiently for this season, with limited resources and some unique partnerships. Like a Python, this team has the potential to GROW LARGE and GET POWERFUL enough to SQUEEZE the competition. Congratulations Team 9554 – Portage Pythons.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: This small but mighty team is composed of fiercely dedicated students who are using AI to make their team stronger. They're ON FIRE with amazing support from their school administration, and supportive alumni funding. Congratulations 9491, Crypto Creek

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: This team extends the spirit of FIRST beyond their pack. They are changing lives through their extensive outreach. It was their energy that had the judges ready to sing along: ARE YA READY, KIDS? Congratulations 5484 - Wolf Pack!

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team earns their reputation by being INNOVATIVE in helping their students operate in HARMONY. Their readiness to deal with adversity is demonstrated by their continuous acquisition of new skills to pursue LARGER COMPETITION. They engage the NEXT GENERATION early by conducting camps and involve the community to draw their INTEREST. Don’t worry if you collapse, this team has an AED to rescue you. Congratulations to Team 2197, Las Pumas!
This team has been making noise all weekend. Its been impossible for us not to take NOTE of their four piece auto. Was that the sound of THUNDER or a sonic boom?

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team used game aspects to streamline their strategy to intentionally master specific game elements. They were dialed in on success to create a fierce competition. Their creative approach to the game really had our GEARS turning.
For this team, organization sets the standard. Sharing inspires their imagination. This small DOG has a mighty bite.

This team impressed the judges with their expanding circle of efforts and impact. Delivering STEM and the Future to those in their community. Regardless of background they're not just throwing rocks, they are changing lives. Asking RV there yet?
With engineering design guidelines in place, this team built their frameworks from requirements and stretch goals. There is no GUESSING at this team's PRECISION design objectives.

THis season and beyond, one team outshined others with generosity and passion. They feel more like a family when they gush about other teams, students, and the greater community. With their new rebrand, they are BLAZING the TRAIL of success.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's theme can catch a judges' eye in the middle of a snowstorm. Their team image runs through their robot details, uniforms, and overall branding. Their passion PULSES throughout their team.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team used thoughtful form and iterative design to AMP up the competition. They adapted their bot to prioritize form and function while maintaining a KILLER aesthetic.

You won't catch this team asking for directions. Using their camera, sensors, and automation ensures they are always pointed precisely the right way. They will even tell you their vision is to put their divers out of a job.

The judges love this team for their positivity. They overcame challenges with smiles on their faces while learning the rules are written in BLACK and WHITE. For this, the judges are handing out The Resilience Award.
For this team, Engineering quality in all things is job one. Through a focus on robust subsystems to fulfill their Mission, It’s a simple KNIGHTS move.
With their eyes on the future, we are expecting great things from this team. Their energy and ambition is infections. They are constantly putting their best PAW forward.
This team wowed the judges with what they learned this season. They had strong GRIP on cooperation and all this while SLITHERING into a new home.
When it comes to spirit this team is fierce with pride. Playful in the pits, Ferocious on the field. This old cat will always have new tricks!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team's business plan stood out among the rest, exemplifying their sustainability. They may not be green their their processes sure are. Their continual amendments to their constitution and robot definitely insure they'll be INVADING the future.

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.script: When this robot enters the field, you don't need to fret. Their automated features allow them to quickly align, seek out notes, and adapts to the challenge at hand. Let's just say they left us THUNDERSTRUCK.

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Not getting STRUNG out, this ROBOT GASSED up to find the right pitch. Looking back to RE-CYCLE something from DEEP SPACE. This robot’s creativity BLUE the judges away.

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
