records.script: This team inspires each of their members to make outreach a constant priority. From providing international assistance to local education efforts, the enthusiasm for their community is a BADGE this team wears proudly. When talking to this team, they BOILS over with excitement!

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.script: This team really touched the judges hearts. The work they have done creating future career paths, encouraging entrepreneurship, expanding school curriculum and their stand-up position in their community would make even the Madame smile. They are truly the real mccoy. Congratulations to 6721 the Tindley Trailblazers!

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.script: This Team’s robot was built above SATISFACTION. their Design process is so simple, you won’t get RED in the face. Their elegant and advantageous robot is ready to QUAKE… I mean SHAKE.. the competition.

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.script: This team gets a gold metal for their gracious professionalism. Their teamwork and camaraderie Crescendos both on the playing field, in the pit, and especially in the stands. Starting with 5 and growing to 36, this team gives off the spirit of 300 Spartans.

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team stood out on top of the mountain. They made some B.I.G. moves with their consistently bright and bold mascot and theme. They are NOTE-orious for their imagery.

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s unique design will make you green with envy. Their innovating climbing mechanism will make you TREK MOUNTAINS to see. Don’t be BAMBOOZLED by their design, this team is no EMBARASSMENT.

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.script: This Team’s impressive efforts towards controls lead the judges to embark on an epic journey of discovery. From chasing down bugs in supplier libraries, to racing across the field with the help of enterprise tools. These hounds really have software & controls all locked down.

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.script: The Golden Fiddle Award This team went down to Plainfield looking for a banner to STEAL. . .With a robot of RED. . . and a medal ahead, they were ready to take the field. Sorry Johnny, the DEVIL. . . wins The Golden Fiddle today.

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.script: This team checks all the boxes when building a quality robot. Their focus of getting NOTES IN ALL THE RIGHT PLACES helped CHAIN together ranking points. They really FLEXED high quality at all ANGLES.

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.script: Following the footsteps of their famously feuding Founding Father, a clash of personalities required building a team before building a robot. WE FOUND THIS TEAM TO BE A STAR.

records.eventName: FIN District Plainfield Event presented by Carrier
records.script: This Rookie’s got a great catt-tiude, and their first year has been ins-PURRR-ational. OOPS! We’ve let the Panther out of the bag.

records.script: Its once in a BLUE MOON. When you follow the RAINBOW, to a team that ROCKS this much.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: In finding their way through the woods, this team was enterprising in preparing for contingencies. Electronic fences protect them from harm while almost as many eyes as a spider see the path to victory. Using their customized systems, they can scan their universe at warp speed.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Swooping across the field, this team’s robot is no featherweight. A unique solid nest of blue and red protects this team’s robot from predators. This team’s creativity will shine brighter than the Montauk lighthouse.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: ARRRRRGH! This team has traveled the seven seas to inspire future engineers. From cardboard bots to go-carts, and a voyage that ensures that girls are really into STEM, these pirates have earned their booty.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: Instead of being trapped, this machine flew through crescendo. The robust machine snaked notes everywhere. Rommie did not short circuit.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: This team gracious professionalism is like lightning in a bottle lighting up a quiet room. Their compass points to innovation, improvement, and inspiration all around the world. This award is going down under.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Like little critters, this team infiltrates their environment as they roll across the stage. By boldly interfering with local enterprises, they improve humanity and advance civilization. This team will continue to live long and prosper.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Taking inspiration from a feline’s tongue, this team designed their machine to latch onto the notes. The modular design of this robot created a hole in the atmosphere that allowed it to rise to the top. This brave little toaster warmed the Judges’ heart.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: This robot enters the scene and blows its competitors off the field. Even in low visibility, this machine is able to navigate fully. The judges found this ability dreamy.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: This international team has a strong humanitarianism presence. After the earth stopped shaking, this team jumped into action by bringing in units to provide 10,000 liters of clean water per day and enough electricity to charge hundreds of cell phones. The spark from this team cannot be contained, even in one of their superboxes.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: The climber on this robot helped them lift their way to the top and into the atmosphere. Serious-ly, this machine’s quality doesn’t get lost among the clouds. Their custom manufactured parts and vision lead to a robust reliable robot. Nothing but blue skies for this team

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: Planting the seeds of FIRST values throughout their community, this team really Cares about Education and Growth. In addition to supporting all levels of FIRST, this team helps others through summer camps, developing prosthetics, and using drones to plant seeds. There is no stopping this team once they get going.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: This team is a true international inspiration. They spread STEM all throughout their country reaching ten thousand people directly with their STEM projects and over two hundred and fifty thousand through their social media. I’m sure their “ears” have perked up…

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: This younger team is centrally located within their country in between mountains. Using various tools from pick-axes to umbrellas, the spirit of this team is impossible to miss. Like natural mummies, the minerals in this team are here to stay.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division sponsored by Gene Haas Foundation
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: There’s no hidden magic here, just a bunch of blocks fitting together, inspiring change through many sustainability and recycling efforts. Just drive through one of their events and experience all levels of FIRST in the process, and have forty tons of fun.
This team consistently achieves a 4 note auto with the best on the field. They plan their pathway so they can go the distance. Don’t let the robot’s green color get your “goat”.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team generated a lot of buzz. With their outside the box design, they widely distinguished themselves from the competition. It’s a trap! …ezoid.

This team flew in with a robust and attractive robot. Inspired by the sun and moon, they built two robots so they could improve day and night. These Ravens put on their Flight Suits to carry Adonis through his journey.

records.teamName: The FBI - FIRST Bots of Independence
records.script: These students wear positivity on their sleeves. This team of OURS is inclusive to everyone. Their investigation has found that programming and coding has no gender.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team takes a refreshing approach, orchestrating a cohesive theme. We TIP OUR HATS to these creative students. These CATS work in symphony.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot’s quick pace set the tempo for competition. Its bright colors complement its dazzling display. We were truly “inspired” by this team’s brilliant symphonies of scoring.

In a game where music is the theme, this team shocked us with their Good Vibrations. Their usage of pies while aiming at tags effectively served up notes to teammates, speakers, and amps. As they galloped across the field, they were always in control.

records.teamName: Blue Valley CAPS Metal Mustang Robotics
records.script: This team is taking home the Judges’ BLUE ribbon. Through their stage theatrics they strive for the GOLD. Their performances for Scout banquets make this PONY best in show.
This team’s quality shines as bright as their color. Through element analysis and logging, the plan for the future by replaying the past. You can count on their crimps to pull your sled.

This team is training for a Bright Future with multiple inventive outreach and education initiatives. Education in their school, city, and around the world is CORE to their team. When the judges spoke to this team, the spark triggered a meltdown.

If you’re looking for a conductor, here’s a team you want to keep time. Playing to the community, they trumpet the FIRST mission to all who will listen. Including new voices, ideas, and identities strengthens their ROAD to excellence. They compose their robotic symphonies through mentorships, summer camps, and international outreach. This team donates parts during competitions, programs light shows, and hosts an iconic off-season throwdown. Small in number, they are driven to succeed, while paving new roads for the next leaders in FIRST.
This rookie team is small but mighty. They secured funding for basic needs and developed a plan for the future. Next up: To boldly share their success with the school board.
This team’s community won’t be blue today. Rising from the basement, these students really showcase their team at school. This team takes liberty with Dean’s quote, proclaiming “The Robot Builds Me!”

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team’s leaders have assembled more than one approach to sustainability. With a focus on women in STEM, they have built a pipeline for their future in FLL, FTC, and FRC. But where they really SHRED the competition is in their plastic recycling for housing program.

This team was determined to not let a lack of parts tank their season. Their determination led them to rewrite the popular programming to match their robot’s system. Their wayfinding autonomous routines were able to respond based on the input they were getting and allowed the robot to independently course correct making for smooth sailing. They have set their sights on a “rising green tide” for sharing what they have developed with future teams.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The clean simple design of this team’s robot allowed them to creatively tackle this year’s challenge. The robot’s dual purpose systems helped the team blow all the right notes and get a “hook up” on the competition. This team has sealed the Creativity award with a KISS!

This team’s passion for engineering design shines through in their winning bot. Their all-inclusive point capture system enables them to handle every aspect of the game. They strategically hooked and trapped to sting their competition.

This team is focused on much more than just winning. To them, building and maintaining relationships and helping others to succeed is their top priority. Their structured organization helps them to not only succeed technically, but also helps them to focus on sustainability and community outreach goals to help spread the principles of FIRST. Actively reaching out to rookie teams pre-season and helping anyone in need year round, even in the heat of battle, this team exemplifies the very meaning of Gracious Professionalism. As they say, “Victory goes beyond winning!”

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has consistently maintained their visual aesthetic since it’s inception. Team members are easily recognized on the field, in the stands, and it’s easy to see which pit they call their own. The students have created an image of comradery, professionalism, and fun through every aspect of this competition. There is nothing CHEESY or PUNK about this team.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Flying under the radar, this team handled the pressure to show off their simple and compact shooting arm. This well thought out and designed machine snuck up and clawed the field. Prowling the competition, they emerged victorious from the jungle to show us their elegant design.

This team’s robot gained an edge over the competition by shooting automatically without having to move its “feet”. Like pinball wizards, the team’s use of paddles to aim the notes helped to create beautiful music. Being able to survive a nuclear bast has put this team in control.

This team set out to up their game this year. They optimized their design and build process for their creating this year’s bot. They also developed a system to track and improve their robot based on match performance. From a bear crawl to a run, this team is taking off.

Building from the ground up with rigor and maintenance in mind, this team thoughtfully designed a truly robust machine that clawed its way successfully through the competition. This robot is far from prehistoric. Don’t tread on the quality of this bot. This team rings green, gold, and true

This team celebrates the FIRST mission across the ages from K through grey. This year alone they have inspired over 1500 students, collaborated with 21 teams including FLL, FTC, and FRC rookies, and volunteered at over 50 FIRST events. If you are looking for inspiration, you could not find a better copilot.

This team truly exemplifies what FIRST is all about. During the off season they impacted their surrounding communities by providing TONS of valuable commodities to those in need. Beyond the walls of their own school, these students have not only brought younger students to STEM, but they have gathered FRC teams from the region together to build, learn, and practice. Their efforts to GROW the community extends from the practice field into the GARDENS that flourish thanks to their contributions. The judges were impressed with the way they identified and responded to a nationwide barrier making a big impact less than 3-DAYS after the FRC kick-off! The students on this small team are inspiring their entire country to use FIRST as a BRIDGE to careers in STEM.

In their inaugural year in FIRST, this youthful team has had success in many areas combining their enthusiasm for STEM with their passion for their schools’ history. They have established partnerships with multiple schools and have created ambitious plans to continue to grow their team and others into the future. As they tackled real life challenges, mentored FLL teams and motivated others to learn more and do more in their own communities, the “News’’ of this powerhouse team’s passion quickly spread. Although these “KIPP’s” may be new on the block they are certainly working together to kick some BOT!

This rookie team has taken to flight quickly in their inaugural year. They have embedded themselves in their school and community, building awareness of STEM and FIRST allowing them to build several partnerships. Distributing science packs and demonstrating their commitment to science and technology, they are not content to “roost” on their laurels. They egg on younger generations taking them under wing. This is not a team to “bawk” at!

This team’s spirit reaches out far beyond the competition arena. From hosting activities at their school to adopting special projects, to participating and partnering with many community events, they bring a whirlwind of enthusiasm, energy, colorful spirit, and a true love of FIRST into everything they do. They are “collaborators, integrators, and sculptors of tomorrow.” You may have bumped into their purple clad mascot.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team blew the judges away with their extensive programs that not only excel at sustaining their own team, but in sustaining the broader FIRST community and beyond. Empowering women in STEM, creating solutions to support an organic fertilizer production process, paying it forward for financial stability of other teams, and utilizing technologies to improve education and living conditions in remote communities, this team if figuratively and literally seeding the world. They created a SPARC which built STEAM into a global force of good.

This team not only has multi-note autos, but they also utilize their autonomous functions throughout the teleop period of the match. With a single button push they can acquire a note, with another they find the speaker and score. For this team, autonomous is a fundamental particle of their success. The Autonomous Award goes to Team 125, the NUTRONs!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team selected their materials with an eye toward success. Their design allows them to soar high above the rest! This team that is AMONG US loves their googly eyes! The creativity award goes to 6201, The Highlanders!

This team made their presence known in some unconventional ways. They were inventive with inclusivity within and beyond their team. They have stormed their way to this prestigious award by accommodating their team members, educating their classmates, and advocating for engineering in their town. The Engineering Inspiration Award goes to team 509, Red Storm.

The judges were blown away by the sheer number of outreach events this team organizes every year to serve their community. When sponsorship trouble hit, this team didn’t back down. They clawed their way through it and found a solution. The team brings people from around the world together to hack their way through a weekend of STEM games and exploration. And they even taught their robot how to wish kids a Happy Birthday! When adversity STRIKES, this team, like their rare mascot, does not let their enthusiasm get caged in. It explodes like a ROAR. Congratulations to Team 2877, The LigerBots

A team that has mastered the math and physics in engineering. Their process includes redundancies, lessons learned, and documentation on par with professionals. As always in engineering and design, the devil is in the details. This team has burned their way to excellence in engineering with their robot inferno! This award goes to team 2876, the DevilBotz!

This team exemplifies Gracious Professionalism on and off the field. They help others by donating pieces, parts, and even an entire drive train. According to this team: "we want our opponents to be the best they can be, then we want to win". This award goes to team 3467, Windham Windup!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: With their team color and hats, they can be seen all throughout the competition. Whenever their metal beast entered the field they were instantly recognized. Best of all, this team was able to form an a cappella of tigers. The Imagery Award goes to team 4176, Iron Tigers!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team doesn't let an engineering challenge take the wind out of their sails. Their elegant design and use of unconventional components allowed them to iterate quickly. Some teams solve every problem with a hammer, but this team solves them with a chainsaw. Congratulations to team 8626, Cyber Sailors.

This team's design combined human and machine to allow anyone to strike with precision. They can score from almost anywhere on the field with the physics they derived themselves. Don't let this munchkin fool you, they may seem small but their reach is mighty. The Innovation in Control Award goes to team 78, Air Strike!

This team is so well rounded you'd think they're on a roll. In the last few years they've made a "splash" in terms of branding, recognition, and robot design. Their robot may be small, but they're mighty in a pinch. The Judges Award goes to team 246, The Lobstahbots!

This team had the hits keep coming but the bot kept ticking. They used prototypes to double and triple test their designs, learning to produce a rugged and durable bot. They brought physics equations to create a quick and decisive design that brings a lively spark to the competition. Winning the quality award, the Conductor’s of Calamity in a double time beat, Team 131, CHAOS!

As a team of hardworking and enthusiastic individuals, this team's smiles are as big as the robot they had to cut in half. These KNIGHTS are here and ready to inspire! The Rookie Inspiration Award goes to 9729, the Knights!

There’s a spectrum of things that can show off team spirit. This team’s ultra impactful work transcended their own team and involved others along with their community. This team has been recognized for excellent inclusivity through the community with their parades, polls, photos, and with their un-named unicorn companion and more. Congratulations to team 8567, Team Ultraviolet.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is a peach when it comes to sustainability and recycling. They have a cherry of a process in rebuilding and donating bikes to their community. They have a pumpkin of a plan with their strong FLL pipeline. Although they are a peach, and a cherry, and a pumpkin, this team is the APPLE of the judges eyes! The team sustainability award goes to 2067, Apple Pi.

Although misleading by they're name, there’s only one of this team. When under evaluation, this teams robot was reliable to be let off leash, fully automated to climb and trap at the finish line. But not only did this teams robot dominate with fast and accurate autos, they overwhelmingly secured the Autonomous Award.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Making beautiful music in the field requires creativity. How this team kept their gears aligned was no fish tail. Their unique design had them soaring above the rest.

This team's commitment to advancing science and technology is evident in their schools, community, and beyond. With their perfect blend of numerous outreach and recruitment activities, and their many science and technology educational opportunities, these COOL CATS do it all.

This team has been around for a few years. They have started many FLL and FTC teams over their lifespan, and continue to expand and start new teams including 11 new teams this past year. They are fundamental to supporting FIRST in their local community; and expand their outreach globally. This team is not satisfied resting on their laurels. They introduced our now popular Quiet Rooms to FRC in 2018, pushed to make them mandatory at all FRC events, and are now working to expand them to FTC and FLL.

This team would make most professionals GREEN with envy. Program management is challenging for industry partners but these Bionic Baddies prove that agile processes lead to success. This team's excellence in engineering is truly inspiring and we can't wait to see what comes next.

Robotics within a school always has one fighting for space and time to build. During competition, teams can get worked up into a frenzy, but this team managed to find a way to help others. Though there is always bait in the water, this team swam their way to the top of the Gracious Professionalism Award.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When you move left or right and sight, this team is red and notable in appearance from heads to their tails. Your imagery is clear.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s robot required a multi-school effort They failed fast and iterated to a mechanically elegant design They incorporated machine learning to STRIKE the right note.

This team glides across the field at an alarming speed. From avoiding collisions to scoring fast, this team can easily run ahead of the pack. For navigating the forest that is the competition field, let's hear it for them.

A wise competitor once told us that, "life is more than school", this team demonstrated diverse skills that set them apart. Like Neo, the the judges were faced with an impossible decision; which award? Let's hear it for this dream team.

Beneath this robots hard exo-skeleton is a machine of exquisite elegance and intentional design. Like a fine lobster dinner, each element was expertly curated for the teams purpose on the field. The quality of their build sets these artists of engineering apart from the rest.

This team is a true beacon to what it means to be a FRC Team and to embody the spirit of FIRST. From studying past competitions to getting a space and much more, an outside eye would believe they were VETERANS! This team truly deserves the Rookie All-Star award

This team showed up strong with an outstanding team spirit that wow-ed us all. Their strong community outreach clearly furthers the objectives of FIRST. This team has members from 11 different towns, but they have one unified vibe.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Atop of Rattlesnake Mountain sits a team with an exceptional talent for sustainability. They blaze trails for accessibility and maintaining their team.

This team owns the night. This reliable, high performance robot senses its environment using odometry, PathPlanner and auto aim to consistently score during autonomous. Fusing multiple sensors and encoders enables them to quickly intake and accurately shoot - even on the move.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team defied convention by thinking outside the bumper. They took a hands-on approach when designing their intake. This team clawed at the notes on their way to victory.

This team excels in empowering others through engineering and personal growth. Finding unique ways to engage with the community to support education and development, they are working to unlock the land of STEM. They strive to promote the ideals of FIRST all year round and all cross the highlands.

Like the teeth on a gear, this team has made their impact through connections with the world around them. They expanded beyond their team to reach local, state, and regional communities. At the local level, they are the primary source for STEAM education in their community. Over the past 3 years, they have supported multiple STEAM camps, serving hundreds of K-8 students free of charge to all attendees. In addition, this team mentors many FLL teams within their community and hosted the first FLL qualifying event in their state. At the state level, they pioneered the FIRST experience at all levels - hosting the first statewide kickoff event, purchasing the state's first FRC practice field, and partnering with a local maker space to open a robotics hub to all FIRST teams in their state. Through mentoring rookie FRC teams last season, they increased the number of Vermont based teams by 50%. With the provision of gears in motion, this team's members are working together as a mighty machine to propel progress, innovation, and mutual growth.

This team grabbed our attention in ways that are hard to convey and broke new ground with your innovative approach. Their attention to detail with your intake's material selection and unique conveyor mechanism were out of this world.

This team's mission is to inspire the next generation of STEAM leaders. During the off season, this team mentored students from their school, held community events, and promoted FIRST values with their local TV channel. They went above and beyond to help out their fellow teams. We would like to commend their genuine attitude and behavior.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From pits to the stands, this team's integral theme stood out. Their unique logo and ferocious mascot commanded attention on and off the field. This team's imagery, from head to bot, demonstrated that they are iron clad predators.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With good design and documentation, this team made their pneumatics efficient. At lightspeed, their elegant indicator lights communicate to their drivers across the field. Their lights could practically help them observe a needle in a haystack.
In order to drive the wheels of innovation, a team must leave no gear unturned. This team used their innovative mechanism and control design to climb to the highest heights.

Judges award for Great Promise All great teams start with a plan and a promise to perform. Taking the ball from a sister team and pushing it along the playing field with purpose and pride, they came together to pack a powerful punch. This pup is all grown up.

Their robust, sharp-shooting machine spins its quality notes across the field. They're one of the few teams with a hardware selection criteria. They generously open their parts pool to spread quality to all.
This team became an all-star this year. They showed perseverance and resolve with their short time frames and long robot frames. By now, they've been sworn in as knights of FIRST.

Even though this team is a rookie, they have a concrete, or one may say, riveting, plan for the future. Their outreach efforts and community service projects guarantee they will build a pride that dominates the forests for years to come. There's no foiling this inspiring rookie team.

A team, like a robot, strives to be more than a bunch of parts. Whether chugging up a mountain or spinning around the floor under the sparkle of a shiny disco ball, team spirit grows from shared experiences that keep things focused while making it fun. As they plan their next party with lightsabers and stormtroopers, we congratulate the champions of team spirit.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team devised a battle plan to protect their kingdom. They're constantly forging their legacy by restoring their armor and building their cavalry. In their quest, this noble team has achieved lasting sustainability.
Most teams pick up notes from the ground. Many teams shoot notes high into the speaker. Only a few teams have a 4 and a half note autonomous that takes them to the skies. Guess who’s back.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When it comes to creativity this team commands the topic. This team has a custom button board, a novel climb mechanism and unique method to put a note into the speaker. They rule the robotic cyberspace and are the Colonels of crescendo.

The returning team members of this winning team mentor new team members ensuring knowledge transfer and skill development. They conduct mental health check-ins to ensure that team members are not overwhelmed. They work during the summers to help get new students AHEAD using RoboRecess. The motto of this team is What Would Woody Want? The winners of the Engineering Inspiration award are 558 Elm City Robot Squad.

This team ensures that information flows from senior team members to newer team members by helping the newer members and keeping excellent documentation. They support FLL teams and work with Scouts. This team has FUN together, they are LEARNING together, and they seek out OPPORTUNITIES with ENGINEERING and ROBOTICS. Finding sponsors has led to new passions in optical engineering and aerospace engineering. The team members have been recognized by many outside organizations.Their motto is WORK HARD AND PLAY HARD.

From their super fast note pickup to their quick and agile swerve drive, their strong accurate shooting and scoring ; the big dogs in this competition need to watch out because this high performance cat can really bring home the bacon on the field. The excellence in engineering award goes to team 1699 the robocats.

This team exemplifies the principles of working together with their willingness to share their practice field with others. They prioritize mentoring, strong STEAM outreach and collaboration. They share their knowledge by manning a phone support line, the knightline!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has striking visuals on all fronts. From their music themed pit to their powder coated robot, their branding soars above the rest. You can see their lightning and they'll bring the thunder.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team demonstrated the ability to tackle the problem of power transmission. Their system of belts connected their their tucked away motors to the head of the beast providing a low center of gravity. These features and their symmetrical electronics and wire management is a balance between form, function, and aesthetics.
This team’s shots go in every time. Their control on the field is beauty in motion. They “hunt, aim, shoot”! Congratulations, Team 177 Bobcat Robotics

This team works with senior citizens in their area to help improve their lives. They listen and internalize Feedback. They quickly and effectively respond to feedback including reconnecting with Center for Applied Behavioral Instruction. The judges award goes to team 61 the Intidators.

This team's robust and well documented design process has resulted in an even more robust machine. Their build quality is a snout ahead of the rest of the band. It's most just a robot, it's Perry the robot! Congratulations to team 7407, Choate robotics!

Our winner of the rookie inspiration award has arisen where no team was before. They came together at their school to create a team with big dreams and more importantly plans! Our winner has experienced the highs and lows of competition, have had to modify their robot based on the rigors of competition, and most importantly persevered and successfully competed this season. They have plans to expand their reach beyond their school by adding FLL teams and opening the team to the community. We look forward to seeing team 9710 Discovery Polybotz for many years to come.
They have grown their team, community impact, and passion. From 4H to 4 bar, they are forging future STEAM leaders. Like the muses, they harmonize and their totally owl-some!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team lights up with enthusiasm when asked about the off-season and the future of their team. They impressed the judges with their business plan, organizational breakdown and continuous outreach. This team can "enforce" Team Sustainability like no other; congratulations to Team 178, "The 2nd Enforcers".

From the robot's mouth: With my intelligent and dynamic planning, I don't get stuck. With my dual vision, I don't get confused. My team is pushing the boundaries north and south. The Autonomous Award goes to Team 1100, Inverse Polarity.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team used creativity to make waves in the competition. Smiling all the way, they nailed it with their innovative designs. They're bringing their best poker face when they score in the trap. The Creativity Award goes to Team 5000, The Hammerheads!

This team is committed to bringing the FIRST mission to their community regardless of age, skill, or interest. Their fire burns brightest when they are advocating, supporting, and advancing technology through their work with their younger peers. This team has a card catalog of skills that are sure to impress. Then the Providence River is on fire, sound the alarm! The Engineering Inspiration Award goes to Team 2079, 4H Alarm Robotics!

This team’s howl is making their community’s interest in FIRST shoot upward. Their cool library of courses interests the fledglings of their colony in science and engineering. The work they are doing to educate and empower is just the tip of the iceberg . The First Impact Award goes to Team 1757,Wolverines!

This team worked until they were "crimson and gray" to adhere to industry standards. Their thorough documentation, committed agile approach, and attention to detail really "snapped" them "back" to the realities of engineering. These "GOATs" of Engineering Excellence deserve a place at the "top of the hill.” Give it up for Team 190, Gompei’s HERD!

This team exemplifies Gracious Professionalism in all they do! They never shift away from helping other teams achieve new heights. With their handcrafted professional look, they sang their way to this award. The Gracious Professionalism Award goes to team 4048, Redshift!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Other teams may be GREEN with envy over this team’s impressive Public Relations and Social Media presence; Who knew engineers needed a social media class? They are all GEARED up and ready to welcome new students to their amazing community. Through their outreach they have touched the hearts of many and give exemplary support to their peers. The Imagery Award goes to team 2370, IBOTS!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team thought about the hard hits and not only designed a robust robot but is ready with redundancy. Taking notes below the bumper doesn’t stop them from soundly sending them to the target. When you hear the engines start to roar watch for this robot to score the rafter ranking point! Congratulations to team 1768, Nashoba Robotics.

This team’s robot philosophy includes automatic adjustments in both the autonomous and teleop periods. With two electric eyes, they successfully chart their flight through the field. When they descend from the mountains of Vermont, they always look both ways before landing on a note. The Innovation in Control Award goes to team 6933, Archytas!

This team really popped up on a snowy slope with an impressive plan for expansion. They BUTTERED up the robotics scene with a crisp vision of the future for their state. Everyone please raise your glass and TOAST Team 9101: Green Mountain Robotics!

This team really flipped the script on Quality Design with their robust workmanship and dynamic design. Like a fine French confection, their robot is a mouthwatering slice of engineering that enticed the judges technological appetite. They came in like a lion and showed the competition that they are indeed the Kings and Queens of the crepery. Let's hear it for team 8013, Boston Lions!

This small but mighty team has certainly impressed the community with their prowess and resolve. We look forward to what they offer in the future as their team grows and develops. Their foundation is strong, and their sights are limitless. Let’s hear it for team 9644, NEIA Robotics.

A team that sticks together no matter what displaying excellent resilience. They amplify the voices of women in STEM and called upon prestigious industry professionals for guidance and inspiration. Like a photon in the dark, their priority is to eliminate barriers and keep their team spirit moving forward The Team Spirit Award goes to Team 5962, perSEVERE!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team soars above the competition when it comes to sustainability. From recycling parts to build their pit to creating a structure to pass down knowledge to younger students, they embody all meanings of the word. Rising from the ashes, this team attracted a whole new flock of students and mentors. The Team Sustainability Award goes to 2168, Aluminum Falcons.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.script: This team’s autonomous was harmonious. Their shooter puts their opponents out to pasture. Their five note autonomous left the judges playing “Moos-art.”

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team didn’t hang around in their shop; they spent their time making their robot hang. Though their hang was uneven, everything evened out. This team bolts themselves to the chain and it takes a storm to break them off.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.script: This team is awe-inspiring in their community and draws curiosity to STEM. Their trajectory for the moon is on target. Like their phoenix, Bob the Third, this team is not only resilient, but true engineering leaders in their community.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.script: This team has delivered a powerful message to carry the first mission forward. They took other teams under their wing, showing how STEM initiates can be diverse and inclusive, taking the high ground and waving the FLAG. They also thought outside the nest, reaching out with the FIRST ethos to support projects that range from the world of music, arts and crafts, and even under water. They are the embodiment of co-opertition and helping others to soar.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.script: This team’s CADing covered all aspects of the bot. The judges were hanging on to every word of this team’s hanging mechanism’s iterations. Ringo gets a Starr for their design approach.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.script: This team farmed out its members to help others enter the field of play. They lent their tools, their parts, and their expertise to every pocket of the pit. Overalls, this team is an awesome example of gracious professionalism.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: In the land of FRC, this team made rings for the ears of all. But only one team’s theme can rule them all. And in darkness, their Eye of Sauron watches us all.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team cleaned up on the field and in their robot too. The apple doesn’t fall far from this team’s design, with a sleek, powder coated bot. This team is reaching for their Zenith.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.script: This team keeps themselves in check and has done the math to back it up. With physics based modeling, this team modeled excellence on the field. This capability left the judges bewitched.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.script: The judges were impressed with these students’ calm fortitude in the face of multiple challenges. The students took fate into their own claws by coordinating all team functions. Through adversity these cool cats wowed the judges and competition.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.script: The judges loved the sleek look of this bot, with every wire and bolt in place. This black robot swooped through the arena and into the judges hearts. The quality sings through the Night.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.script: The stands were filled with many spirited and colorful spectators, but this team’s passionate students exemplified the spirit of FIRST. While their unifying theme and cohesive design reflected their team’s appreciation for local history and iconography, their actions show they really take gracious professionalism to heart. This chivalrous team’s chants echoed throughout the arena, showing their Maryland and FIRST pride.

records.eventName: CHS District Owings Mills MD Event
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has achieved sustainability by adopting the 3Rs ethos as a core aspect in everything they do. From reducing consumption to maintaining team sustainability through movie and game nights, they prioritize renewing their team. Just like their robot, McQueen, they have sped ahead of the competition.

This team from out west set their sights on consistent autonomous functions. They leverage vision processing and machine learning to help chase down notes. Driving their robot is so easy even a gecko/GaCo could do it.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: In terms of creativity, one team made the difference. Everything snapped into place for this team with their unique climbing mechanism. This design is truly worthy of Knight Industries.

This team not only builds robots but builds up the robotics community. From hosting off-season events to advocating for FIRST on the national, state and local stage, they fearlessly challenge the status quo to inspire others. Their quest is not for glory but for the betterment of all teams.

This team has spread the love of robotics throughout their community. After returning from a big cat-nap, they went on to start and sustain a number of robotics programs at local schools, and they have also played host to multiple FRC related events. Within their own den, it’s a student-led effort to train their new members, from cubs to future leaders. As kings of the jungle, they have nurtured their pride across Baltimore County.

This team was RED-y when build season started. Their engineering process they used was as detailed as the blueprints for the Chesapeake Bay bridge. Dedicated to SMART requirements and their internally developed SCAPI (scap-ee) approach, this team is cool, calm, and collected in competition.

This team embodies the noble spirit, always quick to assist others with unmatched humility. They capture the essence, always seeking opportunities to support and uplift others. A true cavalier doesn’t wait for a plea for help; they anticipate the need.

Every aspect of the robot's design coordinated cohesiveness not only the team's visual presence but also reinforces their identity and values. Their fusion of orange brilliance and the piercing green eye symbolizes their keen insight and unwavering focus on visual excellence.

Despite many battles, this team’s superpower is unifying spirit and sustainability. Their enthusiasm for igniting young minds and inspiring STEM skills makes them too unique for just one award category. They truly show the compassion and humility needed to wield Mjolnir.

The wingspan of this robot makes its presence known. But the MasterCAD of this robot is the real hero: It commanded the competition from beginning to end. The quality of this robot is worth more than bitcoin.

This team fostered their winged frenzy by flocking together when the chips were down. This bird got recharged by the enthusiasm displayed by their team and fans. Their vigor and vitality exemplified their team and FIRST spirit.

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Autokiniton
records.script: From an AIR-TIGHT robot design to student-led initiatives, this team left the judges “FERRY impressed.” The students were particularly EGGcited to share their team sustaining pipelines and foolproof robot motor redundancy system. They also engage local teams with a county-wide Discord server. This team does not DREAD the bright future ahead of them. Congratulations team 3656, the Dexter Dreadbots!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Autokiniton
records.script: This team has tested the waters in many facets of representing FIRST and STEAM within their community. They have hosted a number of FTC and FLL events with over 100 teams participating and reached out to other organizations to teach coding, CAD and electrical circuitry. This team has created a FRENZY of political activity within their community. They’ve partnered with local politicians to promote more funding for robotics in all schools. They HAMMERED out 50 new teams within their community, helped advocate for a bond resolution with local government that will allow the construction of a shared space for the local teams, and collaborated with their school district to add Mechatronics to their curriculum. They promote diversity to a wide spectrum of students by participating in three girl competitions, hosting an International Day of the Girl event and releasing Women in Science videos. Their MakerSpace4All targets students with learning disabilities. They SUNK THEIR TEETH into the community by pulling together a donation drive for the Midland flood victims, participated in clean-up initiatives at Lake St. Clair Metropark and Adopt a Road in Troy. It’s SHARK WEEK folks…The First Impact Award goes to Team 226- The Hammerheads

Their innovative dual intake system ensures fast, precise collection of game pieces from multiple angles. Beware of their 3D printed gator teeth which enhance gripping ability, making it a stand out contender for this award. Congratulations to Team 1250, the Gator-Bots!

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.script: This team is unstoppable, destroying all barriers in their path. This strong herd of ELECTRIC individuals advance the principles of FIRST from the classroom to the state Congress and beyond. They have broken through the STORMY Mediterranean Sea, creating a slew of FLL and FTC teams in their wake. Despite their powerful nature, they prove there is no CHARGE to be inclusive.

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.script: Hey you guys... This team epitomizes the core values of FIRST through their extensive community engagement efforts. Known for their unique brand of innovation and teamwork, this CREW'S impact extends far beyond the competition arena, as they forge strong connections with companies, universities, and the broader community. Not content with the rigors of the FRC build season, they also organize a simultaneous seven-week FTC camp, demonstrating their commitment to nurturing future robotics talent. Leveraging their sponsor connections, they pave the way for teams across Michigan, leaving a lasting impression on the robotics community. Their dedication, camaraderie, and inventive spirit distinguish them as an unstoppable SQUAD within the FIRST ecosystem. They may not truffle shuffle, but they GOON it out all day.

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.script: This team embodies elegance. Leveraging rapid prototyping, spin calculation, and a methodical trial and error process, this team is truly REVOLUTIONARY. Their unique elevator climber is worth its weight in GOLD.

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.script: This team demonstrated the spirit of Gracious Professionalism by hosting OUT-OF-THIS-WORLD expos and competitions. They POUNCED on opportunities to assist their community, including building PURR-FECT robots with their local preschool. Their CLAWS came out as they PROWLED through the streets to eliminate hunger.

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team NAVIGATED their look and UNFURLED THE SAILS of creativity for a cohesive theme. Their NAUTICAL novelty showcases their teamwork, dedication, and strength as a team. Their custom sponsor panel shines like a LIGHTHOUSE, regardless of which alliance they’re on.

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team built a reliable robot that allowed them to BATTLE it out on the field. They amassed points by specializing in very accurate speaker shots, incorporating a limit switch for intake confirmation, and designing hooks able to take the stage from either side.

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.script: When this team isn’t busy making music, they are out COMPILING DATA to improve their design. With their innovative approach to their shooter angle compensation and positioning routine, they are able to TEAR-A-BITE out of the competition.

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.script: Today, the judges have defined it as “The Diversity Award." This team comes from a small town, where their HEARTS beat as one. They work hard, changing gears and circuits, all while dressing their best, paving the way for the rest. This team is full of girl power, creating athletes and scholars everywhere they go. They are full of pride for their diversity, beaming with inclusivity of multiple cultures as one MEDICAL CORPS.

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.script: This team CHARGED to the top of the judges' charts with their unique and robust machine functionality. With intakes for days and vision without haze, they reached the peak. These WARRIORS rode into battle and emerged victorious!

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.script: This team came together, even though their schools are rivals. Using just one motor, teamwork, and dedication, they have been able to shine bright on and off the field. They may be PUPPIES who bite, but they prefer their robot to fight. In the arena, dressed in the color of royalty, they’ve shown us their might!

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.script: This rookie team destroyed their competition with sweet nature and endless patience. Overcoming the odds with a limited crew, they MIXED their enthusiasm for engineering with determination and FORMULATED a RECIPE for success. These two adorable CUPCAKES spring truth to their team slogan “Bring change” with their endless positive attitude.

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their enthusiasm in all they said and did. Through the troubles this small but mighty team encountered, they never lost their optimistic attitude. These three girls are no BOTS. They have the motivation that will propel them through robotics and life.

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Altair
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team will cross any BRIDGE to reduce their carbon footprint. By nurturing young students, they are planting the future for their community. Don’t let their HORNS fool you, these DEVILS are really angels at heart.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: You may think this team should be extinct, but they are living large. They are already holding girl scout workshops, food drives, and helping FLL teams. They also have extensive sponsor recruitment and engagement. For being a new team, their impressive outreach programs really blew the judges away, just like T-N-T. Congratulations, Team number _9455 _______ The DinoMights from Livingston County

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: Every member of this Pride embodies the spirit of FIRST, inspiring generations to come, leading by example. From clawing their way into a build space, to teaching younger students about Gracious Professionalism, this team doesn’t just meow, they ROAR! Congratulations, Team number _9758 _______ The Pantron-X_from Watervliet_

This team’s multiple STEAM nights enable all levels of students to go FULL AHEAD. Their passion sparks the boilers that drive their STEAM pipeline to growth and success. The team’s vision and engineering development website makes others green with envy. You might even find a Raspberry pie recipe on their discord server. Congratulations, Team number _3656_________ _The Dreadbots from Dexter

From hosting FTC and FLL events to starting and mentoring 78 FIRST teams, this SQUAD is committed to excellence in service of their local community. This team’s impact is both DOMESTIC AND FOREIGN with their international mentor seminar and H.E.A.R. initiative. The judges loved their detailed DETECTIVE work through their sponsor scouting system. They know how to PROTECT AND SERVE the FIRST community. Qualifying for the Houston Championship is: Team 201 The Feds from Rochester

This team has a new playlist, adding fresh tracks across the local, state, national and international landscape. Their impact is HERD among Boy and Girl Scout troops, across FLL-D, FLL-E, FLL-C, and FTC teams, and within their workshops for elementary and high school students. This team is UNITED with those with neuro-diversities, while they round up FOALS for their Pipeline. They GALLOP from place to place to encourage all to get involved in STEAM. Qualifying for the Houston Championship is: Team 548 The Robostangs from Northville

This decision was FREE for the judges. This team has a THUNDEROUS sustainability program mentoring the next HERD of students for 7 weeks at a time. With this team’s ability to mentor teams across FRC, FTC, and FLL they WOOD be a HAVEN to anyone needing assistance. Even their sponsorship efforts are far and above Bronze Tier. They have helped provide software resources for all FIRST in Michigan teams. Their hands-on hallway lets this SQUAD stand above the rest, facilitating student interactions with sponsors and universities. This team GOONS out all year! Qualifying for the Houston Championship is: Team 3604 The Goon Squad from Brownstown

Through sponsor connections, fundraising efforts, and community outreach, this team made the competition look FREE. This team knows that spreading FIRST values is not AUTOMATIC. By taking their successful programs and training others to deliver them, their impact grows exponentially. With a full flock of FIRST events and over 4000 volunteer hours, they soared above the competition. This team is all in on Impact. They may be a small-town team, but they take a global view as they FABRICATE the future. Qualifying for the Houston Championship is: Team 5166 The Fabricators from Freeland

This team’s dedication to electrifying their community to embrace STEAM struck the judges with awe. From their Family STEM Night to their 1500+ hours of volunteering with other FIRST teams, this SQUAD leaves a lasting impact on everyone they meet. Their ability to forge personal relationships with sponsors attracts support like HORSES TO WATER. From summer camps to festivals to using Bunny Helicopters to teach physics, these FABRICATORS of innovation bring STEAM to their community in ways that roar louder than THUNDER!
