This team reflected inward to rebuild. Focusing on diversity and inclusion, the inward strength of these bunnies lets them powerfully impact and reach their community.
These cats hit a high note with their quality. From lighting up city hall to grooming your grounds, having high quality is their drive to success.

This team excelled at communicating the importance of FIRST in their community, and beyond. This maverick of a team is working to create lasting change in measurable and innovative ways. Making hearts dance with gears and circuits galore, this team our judges just couldn’t ignore.

This team’s commitment to the FIRST Core Values impressed the judges. Their advocacy and willingness to engage with local politicians and expand FIRST in their community and state is inspiring. This team followed their "yellow brick road" to impact award victory.

This rookie team has set themselves up for success through strategic community partnerships. They impress the judges with the community outreach they have already achieved and the outreach they have planned to come. This energetic team has built a home in FRC.

This team impressed the judges by their determination to take on the challenge of FRC. Keeping lessons learned in mind, this team is already making plans for the future. Their cat like reflexes have inspired the judges.

This team really brought the energy to the 2024 Greater Kansas City Regional. Maintaining their tempo throughout the robotics season was no trivial matter for this team with a noteworthy mascot. Their enthusiasm in the stands was matched only by their magnetic personalities, which pulsed all the way to the judge's room!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Sparking interest in STEM is only one page in this team’s playbook. Their efforts in environmental and team sustainability make us want to sing like a canary. This team radiates a positive influence by leading recycling efforts and implementing systems to pass on knowledge to those in their community.

This team’s Autonomous is ready for Anything. Their excellent comprehension and attention to potential risk factors Draws no comparison. Being able to design new Autonomous pathing on the fly means this team is playing with A Full Deck of Cards.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: We expect some really jacked happy students due to their note manipulation. They can shield notes from the competition with their hybrid intake system. This red team really raided their competition.
This team’s 2-sided intake was well laid out. They used the rockin’ current to elegantly move notes around and keep them indexed. This team in Blue hit all the right notes!
When you need a helping hand this team gives both paws. Knowledge and resources are open source from this team. They never let their chains wound around the axel.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Their visual imagery stands tallest in their field. It may sound corny but this team will never be de-tassled. Their puns will butter you up.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This blue team had a big impact on us. We were impressed by their use of AI-assisted vision, quality parts, in-house CAD and fabrication. This elegant robot truly INSPIRED the judges.

This team’s control system made them ready to rumble. Using multiple cameras and co-processors this robot tracked both their own and other note locations. The notes they played sent a shockwave through the competition.
Wheels on the bus go round and round and round. This team is truly for all the people. We loved engaging with our new ‘Familia’.

This team’s robot is so good it’s TSA Approved. Their modular design allowed them to travel more than 7,500 miles with a FIRST robot in their luggage. These hawks aren’t silver, but rather good as gold.

This experienced team continues to expand the FIRST universe through their STEM outreach. This team has impactful community outreach through mentoring, sponsoring events, maker fairies, and cooling bike riders. Not to be confused with the animated Jimmy Neutron, this team of subatomic particles are the real deal.

To collaborate and compete, this team racks up its share of travel miles. Where tourism and agriculture are a greater priority, they push to get STEM into the BIGGER PICTURE. They are RAPIDLY moving to “Fit to Lift” their state to a new level in Science and Engineering.
This team is ready to take out the competition. They may be rookies but are not at the bottom of the pecking order. They had all the judges going nuts.
This team is straight from paradise city. Junior in name but not in spirit. They slashed through their competition with enthusiasm.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team came out of nowhere. We were impressed by how they recycled parts back into their team. We were not stuck on a wall making this decision.

Autonomous operations begins with planning the path to success. Then, it is creatively implemented with the optimum combination of April tag and swerve odometry sensors that AMP UP the arena. After witnessing this team's performance, we were surprised the team still needs a driver. The phenomenal performance, the multi-note 15 second RIFS, and the blue hair really rocked the house. Congratulations to Team 1706, Ratchet Rockers!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When a NOTE is off key, autotune can bring it back into PITCH. This team used a series of BELTS, PULLEYS, and ROLLERS so they could pick up a NOTE from the entire length of their frame rail and perfectly CENTER it. Which lets this team PITCH the NOTE into the SPEAKER even from the top of the HILL. Congratulations to Team 1732, Hilltoppers Robotics.

This team excels at data driven engineering, following the process from strategy through design and test. Despite their grouchy robot, the team's blue glow shines a light on the importance of how. In fact, their disciplined approach to engineering is practically PURRRRR-fect. Congratulations to Team 4256, Cyborg Cats.

In a world painted in uncertainty, this team shines in undeniable clarity of black and white. This team's actions in the pit demonstrates the purest of intentions in helping others succeed. There is no grey area in our appreciation for this team. Congratulations to Team 4931, Edwardsville Technologies!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Robotic ingenuity has reached new heights with one team's creations standing out among the stars. They achieved thematic greatness with both their robot and booth design using visuals that were out of this world. The force is indeed strong with none other than team R2 Jesu Robotics. Congratulations to Team 7472, R2 Jesu Robotics!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Some teams GREEN light industrial design from day 1. This team turned GREEN into a strategic, cohesive, and multi-tech approach. This team looks to PERPETUALLY perform at a high design level. Congratulations to Team 931, Perpetual Chaos!

Amidst a whirl of gears and circuits, one team's brilliance shines the brightest. Their control system, inspired by a vigilant yellow guard dog, commands attention with it's precision. With exterior LEDS gleaming like watchful eyes and a shooting mechanism nimble as the canine itself, Argos emerges victorious in innovation in control. Congratulations to Team 1756, Argos!

Embracing their shared identity, symbolized by their mascot, they excelled in their own performance and exemplified the true spirit of co-operation and unity. They spread orange theory of team building throughout a wild geographical area. This expanding team brings their infectious spirit all the way from Mars. Congratulations team 6237, Martin Motion!
This team started with a solid foundation. Their machining is robust as well as artistic. They BREAK AWAY from the pack with performance. Congratulations to Team 3937, Breakaway!

This team rises to the challenge of promoting STEM in their community and beyond. They run over 30 events every year, supporting youth programs, FLL teams, and fellow FRC teams through a variety of initiatives. LETS TIP OUR HATS to these inspiring leaders. Congratulations to Team 4329, Lutheran Roboteers!

Recently, this team has expanded their outreach to capture several other schools in their district, engaging in a quest to make the message of FIRST resonate throughout their community. This team walks the talk. (pause) They give back to their community through an array of outreach and service programs. This team has started, mentored, and assisted teams in an extensive and global network within FIRST. They also support impaired children, victims of domestic violence, and other worthy local organizations. Using its local flowers, forests and lakes, this team has established paths of connectivity across its region and state. Their message is clear, concise, and understandable. Through FIRST, they are making a difference across our world. (announcer please read this slowly) Let us take you on a journey. Just imagine, if you will, you wake up one morning to discover the whole world recognizes, appreciates, and is practicing gracious professionalism and coopertition. That is the laser focus of this team. Please join us in congratulating team 3284, Camdenton LASER!

This team clearly has the favor of the Greek Gods. With 16 sponsors, a youth engineering camp, open house showcase, and an eco friendly focus, they are clearly on the right path. The judges believe everything this team touches will turn into GOLD. Congratulations to Team 9401, Midas' Mayhem!

This team knows the values of FIRST, as it sprang forth from a strong FLL to FTC to FRC pipeline. Their engineering process handles the breadth of the game, and they have great outreach across the field. This nutty fowl has stepped up in a big way to the next level of co-operation. Congratulations to Team 9428, The Cashew Chickens!

Once you hear and feel this team's passion for FIRST, it will make you green with envy. Their excitement and dedication for FIRST led them to secure funding for their ENTIRE state. Their infinite energy and enthusiasm elevates their spirit above and beyond and makes them sweet as pie. Congratulations to Team 3814, PiBotics!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This small team has a mighty reach in their community. They fly the distance inspiring adventures in STEAM to all ages. Maneuvering through all weather to insure team sustainability, give it up for the Bionic Bombers! Congratulations to Team 7417, Bionic Bombers!

This team’s robot can perform a myriad of tasks with precision and efficiency, using custom code to train and enhance its speed and performance. Like the pony express, this robot gallops through challenging terrain to pick up, deposit and trap notes.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team trained their cat-like reflexes in the virtual world They have taken the integration of hardware, software and simulation to a whole new galaxy. The creativity of these cats is out of this world!

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: As a rookie team they have formed a bond with their community that will last many years. Their outreach is already growing their team and making FIRST known in their school. They don’t work undercover, so we’ll see a lot more of them in the future.
Green is the thing. This team has stepped up to the MIKE in Crescendo… These Cat’s modular design process is well-documented and spread to all points of the Compass.

Many teams assist with GP, but this team shines brighter than other. Their new commitment is putting GP within everyone’s reach. With their colors of black and yellow boldly displayed, this team exemplify the core values of FIRST.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team seems to be crawling everywhere on and off the field. Pinch us, we need to shell-abrate these crustations. They are real lob-STARS.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This Team’s robot stuck to the chain like Velcro, and their button box left the judges sparkling. Their sisterhood had ‘Ri-Ri” singing like Rihanna.

This team’s control system keeps them from flying too close to the sun. They navigate the “vastness” of the field without losing sight of their target. This planet may not have rings, but this orange team can find them quick as lightning.
This team’s robot just keeps on trucking, effectively and simply delivering notes as they go. They are Devilishly good at amping it up.
There’s no “Bad Blood” in this team’s commitment to quality. Their modular design is a true “love story” An Ability to Maintain their Bot ushers in a “New Era”

This team has their hands across many different communities locally and globally. Working with student groups that often don’t have the opportunity to participate in FIRST, this team is able to bring STEM to them and make it fun. This team must work day and night to accomplish what they do.

This team has quickly taken their community by storm with their outreach programs. They connect with schools in their county and with the public through non-profits, museums and social media using STEM kits and bots. There is no question that this team is an inspiration to other FIRST teams.

This team STEAMrolled past the competition by hitting all the right notes. They’ve ‘geared up’ a sustainable STEM program in their community that involves students of all ages, schools and colleges. This team’s fins propel them to the top.

This team thrives on the adventure of spreading FIRST far and wide. The team is always ‘ready’ to help, they are ‘set’ for the competition and ‘speak’ with passion. They take pride in sharing a slice of the pie.
This team caught the attention of not only the judges but the whole venue. Their mix tape pins and colorful capes ensure everyone can their party. These owls are a real hoot.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has big plans to grow for the future. With in-reach and outreach, they are spreading many seeds. There is no doubt that we’ll see their stems sprout.
While their competition buzzed around, this robot injected the most notes with its speed and accuracy without lifting a finger.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Strap in and get ready to climb, if it doesn't workout, try, try again. This team took the engineering design, process to heart using multiple arrangements of climbing hooks without adding too much weight to the bot.

Utilizing the engineering design process, this team kept it short and simple to avoid an early end. They engineered their bot to last through the rigorous game while leaving behind a trail of magenta.
This team has an unmatched Global reach. It's alumni are famous for giving back to grow the team. And this team takes responsibility for the expansion of STEM programs in its country.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Extra small but mighty, this team shined all season. From the beginning to the end, they demonstrated team work, a commitment to safety, and gracious professionalism. Their unique pink style sparkled on virtually everyone in the building.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team released the CRACKENS to not build a bot but a TANK. Their radical design strikes a balance between form, function, and style.
Stalking the jungle of competition, with their custom code... This team found their own path to greatness. Be sure to look out because this Tigers ready to pounce.

This team brought their "A" game in everything that they do. They advocate for DE & I and make sure anyone in their community has access to STEM without barriers. They CAUGHT the judges attention " in their web" with their teamwork, community service, and sustainability. Congratulations Team 1622, Team spyder.
Just as the correct notes make a quality song, the correct parts make a quality robot And with their modular systems, they'll weather any Siege.

Like Vikings, this team traveled the country to experience our Southern Hospitality. Back home they embrace their community with countless student engineering events and also work year-round providing wheelchair modifications for children. GO BABY GO! Congratulations on your truly inspiring engineering outreach Team 2987.

This legacy team exemplifies the principles of FIRST in all they do. Unwilling to stay grounded in their school and local community, this Team has launched out around the world to boost more than just robotics wherever they go. Whether advocating for STEM curriculum, mentoring students at all levels, running/hosting/and supporting FIRST events throughout the year, exciting over 60,000 members of the general public each year, finding ways to raise awareness and funds for cancer and for the needs of economically distressed communities and regions or providing the thrust needed to empower and improve the quality of life for a community in Africa, this Team truly is inspiring generations of global citizens and helping them realize their power to build a better future. FIRST, you have a go to recognize this amazing team with the FIRST Impact Award. Copy That. Congratulations Team 34, the Rockets from Athens, Georgia

Despite being in its FIRST year, this team did not forget the younger kids. Its rural location meant rounding up students from several district schools. The result...A Rookie team that wasn't CHICKEN to take on the veteran teams.

This Rookie team impressed the judges with their grasp of Gracious Professionalism. They shared their STEEL resolve to include team members with many various skills. They're even cookin' with a culinary arts member. "dun dun, dun dun...there are sharks in the water in Pascagoula!

The spirit of this team is TOP HAT in all they do. They haven't lost any TIME in supporting robotics and STEM with camps, international exchanges, and teamwork. TICK, TICK, TICK-don't waste TIME looking for a more spirited team.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This Team is on FIRE spreading their love of robotics in their community through STEM events and other community service projects. They Keep the FLAME BURNING by being intentional about developing under classmen and allowing them to take the lead. They ensure longevity of the team by documenting every step of the process. Their Flame has been burning since 2005, and we're sure it will continue to BLAZE far into the future.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen

records.script: Este equipo cazó notas como cazafantasmas de manera autónoma mediante el uso de tecnología y controles avanzados obteniendo un alto rendimiento y puntaje. Se otorga el presente premio a equipo 4635 BOTBUSTERS

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Nuestras mentes funcionan tal cual una sombrilla, No funciona hasta que se abre. Y estar abiertos a buscar soluciones con creatividad llevaron a este equipo a ganar este premio, donde la naturaleza y las abejas los inspiraron para fortalecer a este robot mediante sus particulares hexágonos. Los materiales no fueron una limitante para llevar al éxito al equipo 6170 de Vitronik porque su creatividad fue ilimitada!
Este equipo llegó volando para mostrarnos que con sus poderes se puede aplicar una excelente ingeniería. Trabajando en equipo hoy logran una misión. Felicidades al equipo 4603 FORZA ONE

En un esfuerzo por fusionar en armonía la tecnología, el arte y la cultura con una perspectiva sostenible y consciente del medio ambiente, colaborando activamente en forma congruente con los valores de First, demostrando siempre empatía, y calidad humana preservando sus raíces Logrado inspirar a las generaciones futuras y, Un ejemplo de cómo la tecnología y la expresión artística pueden coexistir para construir un futuro más brillante y creativo. Se reconoce el equipo 7018 Eolotics

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Por su dedicación al integrar toda la imagen de su equipo y robot, este año se inspiraron en la NASA para difundir la ciencia y tecnología.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Este equipo pintó de rosa el desierto y nos demostró que se puede lograr un equilibrio entre la elegancia y el funcionamiento del robot. Felicidades al equipo 4403 ROULT

En este equipo imaginaron un robot y construyeron un sistema de control innovador como traído del futuro, destacando en la competencia quedando en lo más alto del ranking. Se otorga el presente premio a equipo 4400 CERBOTIES

Es un honor estar aquí hoy para reconocer el increíble trabajo y dedicación de uno de los equipos participantes en esta competencia de FIRST. Durante todo el evento, los jueces han estado observando de cerca a todos los equipos, buscando no solo habilidades técnicas sobresalientes, sino también valores como el trabajo en equipo, la innovación y la perseverancia. Este equipo en particular ha demostrado un compromiso excepcional con estos valores. Han superado desafíos, han mostrado creatividad en el diseño y ejecución de sus proyectos, y lo más importante, han inspirado a la niñez a ser ingenieros por un día. Por todas estas razones, es un placer otorgar el premio de los Jueces a 6200 X-rams.

La calidad no se encuentra únicamente en los materiales, ensambles y diseño de estos robots, ya que para que este equipo haya logrado ganar el premio y permanecer en esta competencia fue necesario que todos y cada uno de sus integrantes fueran personas de calidad mediante sus valores y aptitudes ejemplares. Felicidades para el equipo 5705 Desert Eagles

El premio de Engineering Inspiration reconoce a aquellos equipos que no solo demuestran excelencia en ingeniería, sino que también inspiran y empoderan a otros dentro y fuera de la comunidad de FIRST. Este premio no solo celebra la innovación técnica, sino también el impacto positivo que los equipos tienen en sus comunidades. En el camino hacia esta competencia, han experimentado desafíos, han superado obstáculos y han crecido como individuos y como equipo. Pero lo más importante, han compartido su pasión por la ciencia, la tecnología, la ingeniería y las matemáticas con aquellos que los rodean. Desde programas de divulgación en escuelas locales hasta eventos comunitarios han trabajado incansablemente para inspirar a la próxima generación de líderes en STEM. 4Her, 4us, 4them and 4All. Felicidades a Tech Droid

Este año reconocemos un grupo de jóvenes creativo y competitivo, que genera oportunidades y obtiene resultados contundentes en sus comunidades de influencia, con una misión clara, se da a conocer como equipo competitivo! de un estado reconocido por su minería y nombre forjado en metales preciosos, han transformado sus ideas en realidades y al paso de una Momia bailando el waka waka celebremos al equipo el impact award para Laguna 2024 silverbots 9120

Es un equipo en la sierra de chihuahua que es patrocinado por peñoles y ellos han buscado otros patrocinios de pequeños comercios y escuelas de su comunidad ha impactado mucho a la comunidad con cursos entrenamientos platicas corrección de fugas de agua del pueblo trabajaron mucho en su imagen y su stand y han tenido una excelente competencia por ser su primer año. Equipo 9499 Kamaritech

ROOKIE INSPIRATION Ellos llegaron iluminando cada rincón de esta regional, han tenido un extraordinario éxito en la formación de su equipo durante un año, inspiran y promueve la ciencia y tecnología : “Somos rookies y decidimos no dejar nadie atrás”, 9513 CIRCUIT CREW

Desde un inicio demostraron un entusiasmo que se trasmitió y brilló en toda la competencia, su comunidad y escuela. Un equipo que demostró el trabajo constante, actitud y unión: cómo hormigas disciplinadas y obreras. Una felicitación para MineZ 7546

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Mantener un equipo sostenible no es tarea fácil, por lo que FIRST reconoce este valor. Al igual que un arcoíris, este equipo conforme se desarrolla va cambiando de color. Preservando e impulsando todos sus estándares. Muchas felicidades al equipo 9134 “DEVOLT”.
This team’s bot is famous for belting out notes. On it’s own, it mastered the first 15 seconds of each match.They come from a place that is orange, but they wear the blues.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: While other teams may have been lost on their design, this team’s creativity helped elevate them above the rest. Their intake and launch mechanism took few unexpected turns. Their unique robot has no problem navigating the maze of competition.
This heavyweight thunders across the field. They charge into students’ living rooms to spread enthusiasm for engineering. They attract the ground and repel all collisions.

Amid tremendous competition for first chair selection of this award, this team stood out among several worthy players. As we listened to their performance presentation, we were mesmerized by the well-orchestrated opus of accomplishments. These included hosting over 40 events this season, countless hours of outreach, and innovative programs like RISE and Doyenne Inspiration. They have notably provided advocacy at the national level by meeting with members of Congress. This team raised the bar for this award to the next level, and is well-deserving of a standing ovation for the FIRST Impact Award.
Whose design had a clear orientation? And could spot a note from any direction? They must have been focused on the sunrise.

From broken belts, needed tools, fidget toys, and a practice field, no matter the succession, this team was there to fill the need. They document well that the sum of teams is better than the one that came before. The are the conductors of the gracious professionalism train.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has colorfully augmented the appearance of their machine and the team’s members. They the full spectrum from chartreuse to purple with accent notes in orange. You’ll go ape for their aesthetic choices.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s prickly beast has a rotating arm focused on both speaker and amp scoring. Their spikey bot has no “treble” scooping up notes. They have an industrial design focus that goes well beyond 24/7.
This team has shown it’s stripes throughout the competition. They always know where to find the notes and what to do with them for success. They can proudly blow their horn.
Through the fog in the mountains, this team found their budding neighbors. They generously axed many barriers for rookie teams. The judges would like to recognize these brainiac student mentors.
This team let their wheelie awesome concept drive their design. They rolled out a hot bot with modular construction and skillful workmanship. The are truly riding high and taking a “BOW”.

This team shows a desire to serve as a contagious force for positive change. They are clearly connected with high future potential. The are a rookie team of all-star calibre, chained to a corny dad jokes.

Whether it’s sonics hovering bots, or the discs of a circus, you’ll know “Charlie” and his factory of animal friends by they scrappy prep, dedication to evangelize FIRST with family nights, robotics day, and a fundraising breakfast. This premium rookie team has inspired us with their grit and enthusiasm.
Ghosts, goblins, and witches don’t scare this team. Their glowing excitement no matter the obstacle was contagious for all. This team’s mischievous spirit brought them through thick and thin.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team’s code will last for the ages. They’re mean, really green, and have an impressive machine. When their members move on their ghosts will live on.

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: This robot leaves a vortex in its wake. Their autonomous mode make quite the splash. They can shoot notes like a geyser!

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: With so much creativity at this event, our choices was not very black and white. But in this case, the team’s idea and execution blew us away This team successfully earned their creativity stripes.

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This young team is certainly “up” to the challenge of building an impactful FRC team. Their connections to the community are strong and keep this rookie this rookie team grounded. It’s obvious their “Y” includes fostering STEM with local neighborhoods, schools, and organizations.

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: When they saw their first BOT in the Wild, this team was Amped. They ran free with teamwork and conducted inspiration. These cats are electrifying as Rookie All-Stars.

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: This team swooped in an elegant solution. They were able to slide in place to transform an approach in the design process. They are the Grim that locks in place.

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: We heard many great things about this team from a lot of other teams. They achieved the trifecta of being supportive, helpful, and collaborative. This team is no stranger to the values of FIRST.

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This spicy team is everywhere dazzling the arena with their flare. This team cannot be missed, their brand is rocking. The hottest pepper on the field… Team Hotbotz!

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team sank its talons into the design of their robot. They brought engineering principles to create a design that is both elegant and efficient. As a team, their design soared above the competition!

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: We were wild about how this team used many sensors to achieve their scoring goals. They kept their vision on every note. Their precision set the game on fire!

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: This high flying team is a Beacon in their community. Their large wing span spreads their passion for STEM and FIRST to all schools in their county. This award is a well earned feather in their cap!

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: These lucky Robotiers from the east presented a robust machine. This high profile team built a low profile BOT that allowed them to roam freely across the field. We are happy to report this prehistoric 3D printed BOT has the highest quality of all.

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: Like a ghost on the wind they came from the East. Their landships are treasures for others to plunder. They are the swash buckling heroes of those in need.

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: When power was needed to keep other teams aloft, this team provided acceleration. They were at the controls taking teams to new destinations. They are command pilots of Engineering Inspiration.

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: This team’s 14 year legacy of IMPACT has been well established, YET continues with a magical spirit. This year’s team sustains that tradition with new STEM initiatives for young and old. Their local, national and global leadership shows that even with their successful history, they are a team on the RISE. YETI or not, Houston, this team is going to Worlds!

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: The beauty of this team is naturally seen. It’s spirit can be heard from the mountains to the sea. Jump on this STEAM train and you will find a dragon that will blow your mind.

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Both on and off the field this team has gone green. Their efforts to fix all the bugs have ensured many home appliances haven’t become ghosts. This team proves that sustainability is no error.

This connected team mastered the art of automation. During competition, their bot knew hot to hit all the right notes. These technical virtuosos, aptly named after the connection they forge, elevate the game with their robot’s flawless autonomous performance.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team decided to think outside the box when building their bot. Their unusual scoring mechanism elevated them during the competition, When they are part of your trio, things will get quite bizarre!

This team cruises around the community, looking for ways to spread the message of STEM and FIRST. When they roll out, they leave a trail of inspired future innovators. Their outreach efforts even caused new mentors to pull up and join their team.

When spreading the message of FIRST, this team should never be underestimated. Having established a strong message in their community, there are not FLL and FTC teams where few to none existed previously. Consistently using their team to engage their community through partnerships, and leveraging their brains to achieve success, the judges thought it would be DUMB to not pick this team!
This team took a stab at combining process, tooling, documentation, and equipment into a single useful utensil. This helped them scoop up a high score!

In a field where graciousness and collaboration shine as brightly as the most intricate circuits, one team has seamlessly blended competition with compassion. Their sportsmanship radiates, reach far beyond their own workspace, embodying the true spirit of teamwork. They’ve created a legacy, infusing every interaction with respect and unity. They’ve INFUZED gracious professionalism in FIRST!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Taking the current season theme and looking back at their prehistoric origin, this team directed their creative flex, Leaving an imprint as they alternated, weaving their imagery between their robot and team, congratulations to Team 4935, T-REX!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: During the competition, this team knew how to keep their cool. Both on and off the field, they have what it takes to keep you energized. Their well-designed robot will never need a pick-me-up!

When it comes to replacing people with sensors and automation, this team isn’t monkeying around, notifying their driver with tingles and vibration, with howls and beating chests, it’s time for celebration!

In a competition where innovation and spirit shine as bright as polished metal, one team has roared above the rest. Their enthusiasm is unmatched and their commitment to sharing unparalleled. They’ve roared into action, spreading STEM like wildfire. When it comes to their culture of sharing, this team is the “mane” event!

This team is rock solid in their robot’s recipe and preparation. Strong ingredients, selected with care, seasoned for flavor, and peppered for flare, Heated slightly above room temperature, this robot is chili pepper hot!

This rookie team is off to a smoking hot start. They have created the basis for a strong team that will last through the ages. When you meet this team, you may feel the fire and brimstone radiating from them!

This scrappy team from out west took on the Crescendo challenge and inspired their community with the FIRST message and a strong first-year performance. FIRST definitely has a bright future in the high country!

This team is small but mighty, and sparkles bright, like a majestic symbol of strength and courage. Their spirit and enthusiasm soars high as they take on all challenges with grace and deep pride in their community.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This legend of a team knows that FLL and FTC is a strength to bond. They stomp through their county’s schools, sharing stories of STEM so students grow fond. It’s no myth that a focus of education and learning carries their members to build a team, Year over year, they will continue to be seen.
When a charm in needed to play all the notes, This team casts a magic spell to play the melody, The have conjured a bot in harmony with Crescendo.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: It's frustrating when your brain plays beautiful music, And the notes get stuck in your throat, This teams' creative note, however, just blows your mind!

They defy gravity with their outreach in the STEAM universe and the government orbit. They answer the question, "...to be or not to be" with, to be an engineer. Girl power propels this team and their community to heights unseen.

This team is out front, the leader of the flock. They have used their talents and talons to spread the FIRST and STEAM story throughout their community over a sustained period of time. This team ensures FIRST and STEAM fly across the land.

This is team who has taken 3-D printing to a new level that provides flexibility in design They have created connect/disconnect capabilities to quickly change out components and developed drive train components to go both fast and slow. They have utilized 3-D printing to that makes their robot stand out and excel in engineering.

In the scary world of competition, where supporting others can be a daunting task, and every bit of help counts there's a team celebrated for their extraordinary support to fellow teams, epitomizing the true spirit of Gracious Professionalism. Their HELP STICKERS set them apart in the world of coopertition.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: With a crew that sails under the seas... ...this team garners recognition for their outstanding portrayal of imagery, scary at times, weaving into every design. Ahoy, they seize the prize award of Great Imagery!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: From drawing board to final product, great design leads to a more flavorful life. Just like the perfect pie, some creations standout, combining ingredients in just the right way. And speaking of slices, one team has really delivered the the pie we've all been craving.

This team is focused on always having a nest to come back to whether through the innovation and design of their robot or having a support group to be there for them. They have been a design leader innovative design, use optometry to control navigation, layout of their control systems, to leading in scouting analytics through Eagle Eye. They have soared in controlling Innovation.

With outreach efforts as towering as the animal they are named for, This team earns the Judges' Award for their impactful initiatives, educating elders in technology and bringing joy to the disabled community. Let's salute these champions of compassion and innovation, leaving their mark as mighty as their namesake!
Every team has a burning desire to build a quality 'bot. But this teams' quality control checklists and digital planning has led to explosive performance. And theirs is a sizzling hot 'bot!

Amidst the buzz of fresh talent, this electric team surged into the competition with open minds and paws. Their journey as newcomers produced a river of ideas, milling their ideas down to a competitive robot, revamping their design based on their competitive experiences. Let's hail the cats of rookie inspiration as they charge forward in their first year.

With a name that's a fusion of function and versatility. This team embodies the essence of camaraderie, earning the Team Spirit Award for their infectious enthusiasm, gracious acknowledgment of sponsors, and warm, friendly demeanor. Let's raise our utensils in applause for these lively participants.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: With each team member eagerly grasping new tasks, Through diverse hands and inquiring minds, they tackled challenges with sponsored sustainability for their green works. Their 2.0 team champions a greener path for all.
When faced with the task at hand, their team found the solution. They saw the effects of their hard work on the playing field. They calculated and solved their way into autonomous function.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: While notes flew everywhere, this fruity team did a best fit analysis and launched notes with great precision. They are the Monet’s of robotics winning the creativity award!

Despite their name, several teams often seek them for help. Through extreme outreach with scholarships and elected officials, this team brought inspiration to new levels. Their inspiration for engineering is terrifying.
This team is proof that no storm can stop them. Their outreach is extensive and their mascot even helps clean up a mess. There’s nothing magical about the way this team is wired.
When needing to optimize their robot, this team found their prime path. They used their engineering process to soar to new heights. Their engineering excellence is only rivaled by optimus prime.

This team was gracious and willing to accept the needs of others. When many teams were trapped in a tunnel looking for parts, Light was required to get it out. Most of the shining came from the Darc Side.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Their theme was clear, consistent in image and cheer. Plunging from the depths, you see this theme in all that they do. Treble trouble appeared in all its might to claim its prize.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When it comes to withstanding the heat of the competition, this team’s entire design process stands out. Their distributed leadership, CAN innovations, and documented strategies lead us to a consensus on this award. Their tech skills burn bright, illuminating their passion for industrial design.
These cogs will make their Robot purr. They trained their robot to see sound. These cats are innovative and stay in control.

This team emphasized leadership succession, helping others to come out of their shell. Although in a rural area, they inspired many to join the team. Slow and steady, they persevered with constant enthusiasm, despite many challenges.

When it comes to quality, this team was unmatched – no kitten! They turned wiring conventions upside down, maintaining modularity, and flexibility. The high quality of this bot kept them purring along.
This team only had a couple of months to build a complete robot. We found them to be extremely adaptive and exemplifiers of coopertition. These cool CATS are truly All Stars.

This team showed they are not just another member of the flock. Despite not yet receiving an arm for their robot, this team played excellent defense this weekend. The future looks RAM-tastic for this rookie team.
Small and mighty, this team rallied around their vision. They supported each other in everything they did. Starting as a team of one, they mastered the team spirit award.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has a clear schedule of how their future years should look. With an integral plan that encompasses healthy finances, steady recruitment, and environmental action, they will continue to promote engineering for a long time. Their claws extend from Local FLL teams, to female empowerment, to their green mentors

Though they are not into hanging around, this team consistently hit multiple notes in 15 seconds. The intentionally simple design is reliable, and sings in perfect pitch each time it reaches for a new note. If they were a Formula One car, their carbs would be clean.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This innovative idea turned an elevator on its side. It transformed the movement of notes from one bar to the next. Their creativity glides on rails.

With a course charted to uncover gems and jewels in the community. This team’s travels reach far and wide to navigate seas of innovation. Ahoy, with this team, you are sure to get hooked on Engineering.
When this group came together, they dazzled the community. Their innovative ways and impacts shine through. They are a true blessing for the future of STEM.
This team started with grounded priorities. Leveraging tools and processes from focused groups to fridges. Static electrifies with their Excellence in Engineering.

Embarking on a journey through the STEM universe, This team has been stellar blazing a gracious trail, sharing resources far and wide. Strap on your space boots and hitch a ride on the collaborative comet.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: A skulk of robot gadgeteers slyly perched on the field. They trotted proudly with their hats, coats, and robotic decor. They outfoxed the rest of the field with their clever and functional costumes.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The sleek color coordinated design amazes by zipping across the field. From wiring to materials, to construction, their design was red hot. They successfully navigated the maze of Industrial Design.
Where the sun rises, this team commands and controls. Their robot always knows where it is and where it is going. No matter where these cats are, they always land on their feet.

This team has a passion for equal access to STEM education. Through their camps and support systems, they feed the minds and the bellies of their flock. Their big picture impact is an inspiration from East to West.
This strong robot was built to weather any storm. Facing this heavyweight would put fear into any semi traveling down I95. This big storm has hit North of the Border.

We see numbers everywhere in this robotics competition. Their inspirational artwork has attracted onlookers to their local mall storefront. This team broke the Fibonacci Code with their amazing team spirit.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: In a short time, this team finds itself in an orbit of its own. Their structure, policies and practice sustain their highest energy levels and attract others to their elemental bonds. Their outreach is continuous, and not just a periodic table of grants, sponsors and standards.

Their robot is like an automatic soldier-shoot, reload, shoot, reload, shoot, and reload. Their robot automatically determines the angle and velocity for the turret to make the perfect shot. Zero’s and one’s drive the battalion to victory.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: With their simple and creative design, they laid all the cards on the table They found a way of grabbing the chain that was off the hook They are the Jack of All Trades for the Creativity Award
This team’s engineering process saves every minute As they race against the hourglass and hit every note just in time.
Aiming to help others. With spirit of respect and cooperation. Their arrow hits the target of gracious professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Bundle up, this team brings a cold sting to your face, You can feel this team's brand blow through everything they do, There chilly brand blows away the imagery award

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team used their tools to create an effective and elegant design. Their shooter arm orchestrated the notes to perfect harmony. These cats have a yellow and black bot that embodied Industrial Design.

This team went above and beyond controlling their notes. They created a shooter to produce a variety of consistent and stable shots. They showed us they are more than just a hockey town team wearing flannel shirts.
You can’t get this team out of your head like a catchy song Their style may be street, but their robot can compete We thank them for making Great Northern a stop on their world tour
When this robot gets hit, it does not turn Black & Blue. Combine-ing: Gears, Belts and CNC’d Panels, this team harvested victories When Thunder roars this team’s bot does not shake

When multiple schools needed assistance, they ensured everyone felt included. They are a motivating force for engineering inspiration. This team didn’t let the raging river stop them from advancing respect and appreciation for engineering.

This team is on FIRE – fueled by the spirit of spreading the FIRST mission, impacting the local and national community, and inspiring the STEM future. They are STORYTELLERS who hit the air waves, spoke at live events, blasted the message of FIRST through multiple mediums across the country. They are MASTER BUILDERS who ensured robotics teams have a special place to call their own, secured a huge grant supporting robotics, and supported programs like Unified Robotics. They are ROLE MODELS, who empower inclusivity and diversity, and partner with community leaders, tribal councils, including universities to create a college course about STEM. Their teamwork, encouragement, determination, and diversity were featured in a film that won the Independent Spirit Award at a regional film festival. Here they are in the spotlight again – at full speed ahead.

Like a flash in the sky this team is a star. A true partner on the field with a competitive robot while also collecting a ton of food for their community. Through all the Thunder you hear, they prove its Lightning that does the work.

“This rookie inspiration, a beacon of creation, Their journey a testament to partnerships true, In robotics they thrive, Inspiring me and you. So let’s cheer in jubilation, for this rookie sensation …from the land of the maple leaf’s, too!”
This team is focused on bringing mental health out of the fire swamp. At this event they showed us how much fun they had storming the castle. Their name is not Inigo Montoya – it is Inconceivable.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: When their ranks got thin, they had to regroup. They built back a fleet that’s hard to beat. Their sustainable plan will keep them afloat.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: These All Stars impressed the judges with their commitment to the FIRST core values. While three students had to fight for their existence by advocating for themselves to their sponsors and their school, they are now fully integrated and are innovating their community. Their excitement for the future is palpable in everything they do. This team shows, and I quote, “There is nothing quite like FIRST.”

Colored in Red and Black, this team is getting individuals interested and involved in STEM in various of ways. From getting featured in a local newspaper, speaking about FIRST on a local television network, and attending various school events and board meetings, they are constantly talking about STEM opportunities in the community. Outside of talking about STEM, this team teaches about the engineering process and various engineering principles through working the local Invention Convention and their Girl Power Programming event. With their motto, Accommodate, Advocate, and Educate, there is no better storm to weather than a Red Storm.

One of the biggest ways to get someone involved in STEM is through showcasing STEM opportunities and developing your own, which this team does. Keeping their community up to date about opportunities to get involved in STEM, they share about various STEM events in the local area through their STEM Newsletter, and team website. With their team principle being “Engineering in a Nutshell”, they run a wide range of STEM-related events including a Scratch Hackathon and Robo Race that gets elementary and middle schools students working hands-on to learn about engineering and robotics. No need to sound an alarm,

The breadth and depth of this team’s impact is unparalleled. They participate actively in many FIRST events around New England, and host a wide variety of STEM based initiatives in their hometown. They partner with nonprofits, Scouts, and even their local church to bring STEM to every corner of their community. But their influence doesn’t stop at the coastline; their efforts to teach STEM abroad have led to a mutually beneficial relationship with their international peers. In conjunction with their sponsors and a nonprofit, they were able to donate a school’s worth of supplies to a community that had no previous exposure to STEM education. They pride themselves on being the only team in New England to host official events at every level of FIRST. Their impact is not just surface level, and they will continue to make waves far into the future.

This team is a driving force in their home state. They build strong connections between themselves, their sponsors, and the community they represent. They are dedicated to expanding FIRST through the many FLL teams they have started and mentored, and the FRC teams who use their full size practice field. In the off season they host camps geared toward encouraging young girls to pursue STEM careers and trades. Their focus on the mental health and wellbeing of their members allows them to mesh well with the teams they host at FRC Kickoff. Their efforts led to doubling the number of FLL teams in their home state, showing a commitment to inspiring future STEM leaders. They saw the opportunity to make an impact by expanding FIRST in Vermont and built the connections necessary to make it happen.

This team has a fierce commitment not only to FIRST, but to each other, and their community. They make themselves known around town with their local Scouts, their chamber of commerce, and other area groups. Their dedication to each other has improved not only their team members, but their entire school. Their thousands of hours spent volunteering to help FRC and FLL teams shows their passion for spreading FIRST’s mission; they inspired the creation of dozens of STEAM classes in their school. But where they really shine is in their advocacy for improved diversity and inclusion, not just at their school but globally. They emphasize universal safety, from the safety of their workshop to the mental and physical wellbeing of girls and women worldwide. When they speak about hosting menstrual drives, or showing girls in the Philippines that there are girls in STEAM careers, they BEAM with pride.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.script: This team is very effective during the autonomous mode and continues to integrate autonomous functions throughout teleop. The driver works with the robot, which autonomously collects and scores notes. With advanced algorithms, this team consistently predicts the near future, allowing the robot to reliably score while on the move.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: For the creativity award, the judges chose a team that thinks big. This team was able to utilize a gear in their shooter system which doesn’t even move. It took just 18 hours to print this monster fixed gear for their differential speed shooter.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.script: This team has a well-documented engineering process that is well-understood by all team members. This team can trace their components from idea, through prototype, all the way to final product. According to this team, putting in a lot of effort early and having focused aim allowed them to slingshot their final design, assembly, wiring, and programming.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.script: Spreading the wealth is a concept celebrated throughout the FIRST organization. This team’s commitment to a greener and brighter future is as awe-inspiring as a mountain range at dawn. Please join us as we TOAST to this team.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The judges really had to tip their hats to this team's very loud nod to this year’s musical inspiration. This team showed up with 24-karat magic and the determination to be first in show. Let’s end this awards speech with some fortissimo applause!

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team produced a robot that is compact, fast, effective, and elegant. They stroke the perfect balance between form and function. There’s no negative charge with this team.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.script: There is no trap in this team’s approach. With a flexible brain, and the logic to meld different sensors, this team’s innovative control system integrates its strategy between machine, human, and crustacean.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.script: This team's strong commitment to breaking barriers really sets it apart. They have dedicated themselves to making STEM affordable and accessible to everyone. The judges want to recognize the determination and perseverance of this small but mighty team.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.script: This team focused on robustness and not breaking down. Their belts secured their way to victory. Their redundancy protected them even when they RAMed their robot on the field.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.script: The Judges feel this team is already well on their way to being a core member of the FIRST community. They already have collaborated with several other teams, including volunteering at an FLL event. This team has started their career off with a roar.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.script: This team’s spirit shines through their t-shirts, buttons, stickers, and robot. It’s impossible not to smile when you see them. We’ve no doubt that their positive, inclusive attitude will take them to inifinty and beyond.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Ganson Division
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Team sustainability is on the forefront of this team's mind. They have a strong relationship with their number one sponsor, allowing them to build 95% of their robot out of scrap metal. With their sustainable practices, we are sure this team will be bringing PEACE to FRC for many years to come.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.script: With 360 degree April tag view, and a stereoscopic camera for accurate depth tracking of notes, this team always knows where they are. Cementing themselves as a forerunner of innovation, they also designed a custom, automatic, shifting swerve drive. As always, they are an outlier.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team really blew the judges away, with a ferocious redesign of a common component, this team utilized rapid prototyping based on ironclad research including air flow data from NASA and a grid design to ensure strong laminar flow, this team was able to reliably trap from the ground using a fully custom fan.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.script: One robot, two robot, three robot, four! Most teams build just one, but this team built more! This team sprinted to complete five robots during the season, Their efficient prioritization, rapid decision making, and agile development process were music to our ears.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.script: As recent rookies, this team supports others as they once were supported themselves. Turning a kit into climber, they uplift rookies to share their passion and love for robotics with others. The future is bright, and they’ve found their path.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Riddle me this Batman: How do you “Hush” an FRC crowd? Build a robot whose musical design elements, black, yellow, and neon color palette, and brand standards turn heads and make everyone say, “wow!”

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's robot has a clean design. Their project management system made sure of that! Not bad for 9 days.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.script: This team blew the judges away by their understanding of complex controls theory. Foregoing the standard PID control, they designed their own framework that they utilized through every, robot, function. Snatching notes, like a hawk.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.script: This team won the judges hearts, not only have they created impressive engineering and simulation tools resulting in an advantageous robot, but they're happy to share their whole kit with the full scope of the community. Their impact is felt far and wide.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.script: This team roared onto the field with their robust redesigns and built in redundancies including 3 separate CAN loops, extra motors and rollers, and they even brought an extra wrist, swappable with 4 bolts and quick disconnect electronics but it's so robust they haven't needed to use it!

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.script: This rookie team managed to triple the size of their team in the 6 months since their inception. Even though they were off to a late start they’ve already set the stage for a pipeline of future students from their affiliate middle school. In their premier season, in the spirit of coopertition, they’ve placed a priority on being able to support their alliance partners by performing consistently on the field. This team learned many valuable lessons this season including “measure twice, cut once” and how to troubleshoot and problem solve in real time after having to completely resize their bot at their first event.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.script: The words 'knowledgeable', 'new', and 'optimistic' exemplify the members of this year's spirited-team. New Name, New Ground Work, Enthusiasm, and a nice, neat PVC-PIT bring them all together.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Richardson Division
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team sponsors many FLL and FTC teams and has a great recruitment and sponsor sustainability plan. While this team's color is red, they are going green by recycling and reusing all parts of the robot. And this team is working to remove the invasive species from their pond.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.script: When this team sends their robot out on its own, it sees clearly and knows where it’s going. They get to know their partners, and their opponents even better. It is valuable to be able to update their plan right up to the last minute. With their custom vision calibration software and multiple onboard programs to select from, this team is all about autonomous.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Not all approaches deal with GEARS and SOCKETS. Like a SOFT BREEZE, this bot is gentle on the trap. No doubt about it, the answer is BLOWIN’ in the wind.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.script: This team blew the judges away with their astronomical outreach efforts. From their advocacy for a state-wide day of robotics recognition to creating a scholarship which increased STEM accessibility, this was just another day’s work for these BOTS. They also took STEM activities to a girls’ shelter, impacted over 5,000 local students, and even contacted almost every single FRC rookie team to offer help! This LAMborghini-like team is driving appreciation of engineering faster than their namesake!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.script: With an easy to fix robot, this team turns problems around faster than a speeding bullet. With a deceptively simple design, they swerve circles around the competition. A combination of precision engineering and creativity makes this CHEESY looking design GRATE.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.script: The excitement from this team is palpable. When they noticed a lack of programming skills in their area, they engaged with other FRC teams to equip and empower them with the skills to make it to the championship. This team is emblematic of gracious professionalism!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When it comes to aesthetics, this team doesn’t just MAKE DO. They change and shift their look throughout the competition. Color us impressed!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team created a sleek, mean, scoring machine and treats it with white glove service. From aluminum and plastics to carbon fiber and more, this team has it all, purposefully designed from the start. This team’s design and attention to detail help drive their competition MAD.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.script: This team was spinning and swerving around while keeping their eye on the target. Notes were flying with perfect harmony. It is no surprise that this team is a JACK of all trades.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.script: For this team, their homeland values competition over gracious professionalism. It is hard to be humble when you start an FRC team that outshines you, but this team shows that their ego is not their KRYPTONITE. The judges were impressed with this team’s authenticity and dedication to FIRST’s Core Values.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.script: With a clean design and excellent fabrication, this team built a quality robot. Their use of subassemblies, precision machined parts, and modular coding really takes the COOKIE. Their superb quality is a NIGHTMARE for the competition.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.script: This team never stops reaching out to anyone who will listen. They put a dent in the universe with their WEBBED FTC efforts. They WADDLED their way all the way to Houston.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.script: This not so ANCIENT team has become a surprise blessing to their community. From STEM education to prom preparation, children of all ages are the focus of this organization.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.script: This team is soaring high and captured the hearts of millions with their beautiful spirit. They founded and spread the love of robotics in their home country by hosting kickoff events and starting numerous FTC and FLL teams. The overwhelming spirit of this team has reached the highest levels in their country including the President.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Newton Division sponsored by Medtronic
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has a sustainable structure, mentoring many FLL and FTC teams to ensure a strong pipeline. One third of this team’s sponsors have been around for more than a decade! They bolster these sponsor relationships with everything from newsletters and shop tours to executing projects for them! These PURPLE environmentalists have also collected and recycled hundreds of pounds of batteries from local neighborhoods!
This team can’t help to impress launching 3, 4, 5 notes with finesse. They are innovative to the core with this team, less is definitely not MORE.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team used creative thinking to elevate their robot above the competition. Many teams struggled with tackling the stage, however this team went out-of-the-box to progress traditional design. They wound their minds round the challenge and cast their hook for the stage.
This team “projects” their impact on their community. They use humor to come together, but if it’s not a joke for everyone, it’s not a joke for anyone. Mount your steeds and cheer for this team!

Through this team's hard work and dedication, their dream of creating a STEM education pipeline from kindergarten to 12th grade and beyond is becoming a reality. They are breaking down barriers and expanding in all directions. This year they have revived FLL teams to help spread the word of FIRST. The state-wide, shared innovation hub that they created includes an event arena, fabrication lab, machine shop, and experimental labs and has inspired their entire area. In their spare time, the team also started a Women in STEM bookclub and is developing a robotics program for students with varied abilities. This team's impact resonates across their community and beyond.

This team impressed the judges with their design process that included a progression between an alpha, beta, and competition robot including lifecycle planning, and an organized task list. This team’s robot was designed for modularity and efficient troubleshooting, with isolated quick disconnect electronics and all mechanisms swappable in 6 bolts or less. This devil took care of all of the details!

A team that helps far beyond the bounds of the arena, taking time to train new leads, and also focus on everyone’s personal needs, their embrace of gracious professionalism made everyone a little bit calmer.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team made a splash all over the arena. They designed for the game everything from their buttons, vests, robot, and pit frame. They were loud, proud, and soared above the rest in their imagery.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s robot is built like a tank but doesn’t drive like one. Contrary to their team’s identity, this design is clean and simple. This team and their robot is more than just okay, this team blew us away!
This team swims against the current. They swerved around all their obstacles. Be ready to get hit by a tidal wave! Cheer for this team for their innovative custom swerve drive.

This team did amazing work when it came to team growth. Being able to acknowledge significant mistakes and improve in any every aspect from team dynamics to “just making sure it works,” was remarkable. So clutch your horns and give a round of applause for this team's outstanding improvement!

This team developed and met requirements for a small nimble robot that repels notes. Its revision for competition included clean wiring through a 3D printed wire tray. No despair as their pit of repair remained under-utilized, due to their quality design.
This team experienced an FRC event and that inspired a rainbow of opportunity! Sending out flyers to grow their team. They made there way out of the junk yard to the coliseum to learn.

During both days of competition, this team could be heard cheering all throughout the event. These furious predators could be seen jamming out every day. This team is certainly not a fish out of water but IS a fish.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: To train the next generation of champions. Together, their team organized, and they kicked it into overdrive.
This shipshape team has performed exceptionally well throughout. The treasure of autonomy has consistently and reliably been executed in matches. Acting autonomously to make the notes walk the plank.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team recognized the need for speed this year. Their robot’s exceptional speed and agility makes them an Outlier on the field.
This team was open to creating distant alliances. They stormed the Massachusetts State House to support others to pass and make awareness for bill H 577.

This team’s enthusiasm sparkled from the start – they dedicated countless hours to community outreach and made diversity a huge team focus. Their support to others spreads near and far; from lobbying state legislation to helping other countries across the globe. The judges were impressed by the outstanding fundraising these purple leaders achieved resulting in their Panther Innovation Lab.
This team impressed us with their technical communication and documentation. Tying their data driven solutions back to their objectives and requirements, this team hopped to the top of our list.

Winning the Gracious Professionalism award, this team not only shared their field but had many instances of extending a helping hand to others. They also go beyond robotics and support the community by hosting comedy nights and crafting donation boxes from scrap wood.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Our winners of the Imagery Award truly turned their team into a blockbuster. With the team members dressed as movie characters, they themed everything from their banners to robot color schemes with their cinematic graphics. Calling the characters from the Wizard of Oz on the stage.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team pivoted through five different prototypes. With their simple and effective robot you will find them scoring consistently. Everyone can see this purple robot raging across the field.
Swerve drives, climbers, and small fast robots are hard to control. From brainstorming to week Zero, CAD designs, software, and prototypes appeared. Yet somehow, they managed to trap chaos.
Best all-around machine This robot met the bar for this competition. Their compact and agile robot is sprinting down the field. Their green double-jointed limb is the best all-around.
This team built a robot demonstrating both quality of process and quality of construction. The resulting robot effectively moves, dodges, and shoots, while having a finished, professional appearance.
This team has made a promising start with outreach, a robot performs on the field and significant help from their school. With ambitious goals for the future, this team embodies FIRST goals.

This team was electrifying with their vibrant orange energy. We recognize their unwavering support for fellow teams and the FIRST program. Their enthusiasm and dedication to lifting others make them the perfect recipients of this well-deserved award

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: We appreciate the efforts this team has given to ensure they continue to build a team that operates as a cohesive unit. Their commitment to sustainable practices is commendable, and helps to ensure as little impact to their environment as possible.
This team’s robot really is off the leash in Autonomous mode. Their auto mode may look like spaghetti but the “planned path” snatched the bone. Now is not the time to mess with these dogs.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team conquered the challenges of limited speed and overcame the risk of failure. Despite being heavy, they made the machine practical. This team truly demonstrates the concepts of uniqueness and ingenuity by gliding to score.

This team really asks the tough questions. The answers to these questions are evident in their community outreach efforts. Their outreach program has created a robot that “Oscar the Grouch” would be happy to call home.

This team's work spans from their local schools to around the world. Partnering with organizations to make a tangible difference in the community providing STEM KITS workshops and courses including for special needs. Their leadership cycle is providing a smooth handover of knowledge and resources. Just. Like Clockwork.
This high flying team consistently demonstrated their engineering excellence this weekend. From front to back, they always hit the right notes. Roses are red and these birds are too!!!

This team almost spent more time in other teams pits than their own. From parts to manufacturing, they were always lending a helping hand and fixing robots. Their wings were cultivating GP from beak to talons.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
