records.script: This team can be heard from far and wide. With buttons and boomboxes, they bring music to the pits. Their undersea friends helped ead them to a “sweet victory”

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s clean design helped construct an excellent bot. They were able to deflect many notes to score. On and off the field, they are Hard Hat Ready.
This team make everyone a worker during their design process. Using their vision to keep up with the notes at every angle, you can hear them “buzzing” across the field during every match.

The judges took note of this small team and its desire to contribute in a more significant way. As we all know, the FIRST community is always eager to provide an assist to put a smile on a team’s face. Congratulations Mr. Smiley Face…er…Team 8628

This team drives their robust bot across the field with great speed. They swerved into one of the highest seeds of the competition. No matter where you are, you will be able to hear this teams Cybersonic boom.
The judges loved the sense of excitement generated by this team. Great things come from small garages. Word Hard. Play Hard.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Their three year plan, outlining their goals for community, marketing, robot and business motivated them to get new and strengthen old sponsor connections. This team was agile and driven by pizza to maintain their mentor base, even virtually. They are a true model FIRST team where students are driven, kind and collaborative.
This team had it’s share of the BLUES during competition. Their iterative design process made an impact on the judges. A crescendo of four notes clearly impresses.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: ***Optional rap*** The front, the back, the left, and the lift. This robot lost a beak at risk. Center feeder, always eager, 8117 the creative critter.

This is an ideal team who’s main focus is to excel in every field of engineering. Their enthusiasm doesn’t stop at innovation and winning games, but also giving back to the community. These Raiders are making a huge impact, recruiting elementary and middle school kids for their FLL and FTC programs.

It takes discipline and effort to adhere to the values of FIRST, but a lot more to go above and beyond to spread these values. This team has spread STEAM and FIRST values via community fairs, building public facing websites, mentoring multiple FLL, FTC and FRC teams. Their partnership with other foundations has helped underprivileged communities access to various STEAM programs. Acting as a role model, they are promoting FIRST not only in their community, but also across multiple continents. Hosting international teams and letting their members be a part of the build process, to going out and doing multiple community service events, is just equally important to this team. Every member of this team is proud to be a part of this pie.

This team designed a robot with a full width intake bumper and they really know how to get it to Wor-Wor-Wor-Wor-Wor-Work! They put so much effort into making their robot, pits, and controls “Shine Bright Like A Diamond.” You’re the ones that should “Take a Bow.”

Conducting themselves well throughout the competition to ensure everything is pitch perfect. On stage and off they worked to amplify everyone’s performance. This team is making bumpers and keeping everyone charged up at their event!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has really “Come Together” to show off their theme. They didn’t need any “Help!” while working “A Hard Day’s Night” on their pit decorations. This team is really hoping for a water game with their “Yellow Submarine.”

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Ferocious competitors who are busy on and off the field like the tigers they are. This team shortened their wheelbase, auto centered notes, reinforced their actuators, and took the spotlight in industrial design. With Yogi, their robot, by their side, there’s no stopping this team!
This team’s swerve drive covers up well while giving them a bird’s eye view of the field. They showed the judges a significant use of pies. There’s no doubt these Vulcans are on fire!
This team came prepared to compete. They knew repairs under pressure would be no easy feat. And so, they practiced so they wouldn’t miss a beat.
The judges have a joke for you: Why don’t goats argue over quality? Because there is no BAAAAAA-D wiring around here! Every wire labeled, every part drawn, proving quality is job one.

This team has been guided well throughout the competition. It’s clear to see they understand the mission of FIRST. From the North they will lead, spreading STEM into their district. These new stars will shine bright into the future.

This team jumped to the challenge to show what a rookie team can do. They can’t wait to get back to school and get their paws on their robot. Watch out, these curious cats are on the prowl for FIRST knowledge!
This team came a long way to be here today, and challenges have been crashing into them like waves. But throughout these storms, they remained calm and collected like a relaxing day on the beach.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team committed fully to their goal of sustainability. With their plans for the future you can be sure this team isn’t going anywhere. From the pit to the lobby, being eco-friendly is their hobby.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.script: This team’s autonomous capabilities helped them navigate their way to a top spot. With automatic pickup and shooting, this robot had victory within their claw. This team didn’t have to lance their competition to dominate the field.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team and their robot had a vision to process game elements with ease. Their intake and shooter assemblies danced to the tunes in harmony. With an excellent note transfer process and chain driven climber they crusaded their way to victory.

This team came out of their shells when they told the judges about their outreach. There was nothing sluggish about their passion to spread FIRST’s mission in their community. It was out of this world hearing those escargot tell us how their hydro gas cars go.

This team impressed the judges with a spectrum of outreach events, sustaining existing ones and building new ones. Not only do they work with alot of FLL and FTC teams, they also secured internships for their students from several sponsors and supported programs for adults and children with disabilities. The judges were SINGING FOR JOY from their well rounded outreach programs.
This team’s use of a decision matrix helped separate them from the competition. Their optimized gear ratio powered them to the top. Their team is CHARGED up for the competition.
This team ensured no one is marooned. They tenaciously scouted their way through the field. With professional grace that only good dogs know, shaking hands and fetching when others would go.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team knows it can build a robot but wanted their brand to represent them. They added all the hits to their playlist including a mural and themed swag. Their guitar arms really Roxx.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team had a bot that was slick, clean and robust. Their design met the game challenge with multi-faceted solutions. With dual intake and dynamic elevator slides they can withstand any level of seismic activity.

The way this team BLEW away their competition was something to YELLOW about. They were able to use machine learning to quickly and effectively navigate the field. Their control system accurately de-“CYPHERS” all of their sensor inputs to propel them to the top.

This team made us swerve our head when they started talking business. Doubling their sponsors this season made them a force to be reckoned with. We have to agree their creative fundraising idea is awesome sauce.

The judges were impressed with this team’s modular design that allowed for quick prototype and assembly changes. The DON’T NEED TO SPIN their story to perfect their design. Their amazing OVERTURE is music to our ears.
This team made spirit a high priority. You don’t have to scavenge to hear their enthusiasm in the stands. Their fidgets were fan favorites, proving every little byte counts.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has always been rushing to recycle. Making sure their team numbers never go into the red. Always in the black with their bottles for filament. Soup - it’s what sustainable
These dogs can hunt and cook. Targeting the speaker is a specialty of the house. Tchaikovsky makes beautiful music and spaghetti.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The orange colored features are eye-catching and functional. With six eyes on the field and intake from two sides, this robot is very effective. Goose is more than just a side-kick in this competition.

This team is pushing full STEAM ahead with mentoring FTC and FLL teams. In addition, they are “building bridges” and hosting multiple events. Is it a sea of green, or a shade of blue? This “teal” team is spreading science within their school and community.

This veteran FRC team has been in the game for quite some time, but in recent years they have made some special modifications. They are known by their team members as more of a family that gives individual students a voice and is a thriving after-school activity that blends a diverse gathering of people on a mission. The ‘STEM Spreading Mission’ they began in 2022 has now grown in both overall community reach as well as expanding their collaboration with six other FRC teams working together to produce ROBOCON NJ. Congratulations to FRC TEAM 56 as you STEAM ahead with your efforts to raise awareness of Co-opertition a la FIRST

This team took a systematic approach to analyzing the challenge and designed a solution. They applied swerve drive, Google AI, sensors, coding and creative design in a way that would make Isaac Newton proud. They can intake notes from above or below and deposit them in the aperture.

This team can be seen in other team’s pits more than their own. Not only do they have a drive team for their robot, they also have food drives and clothing drives in the community. Once week zero comes, they can be seen working with other FRC teams practicing and sharing on their field.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This “bright” team can easily be seen in the pits and in the stands. P.S. the judges loved you (Yeah, Yeah, Yeah). They decided to be “day trippers” and rode their yellow submarine.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This compact robot is sleek and hits all the right notes. They learned not to trifle with the power of the beard. They are a ‘ray of sunshine’ and the ‘sweet sound of music’ with which Apollo would be pleased.

This team went to the top of the “Bot Charts” with their unique “mix” of control functions. Their control system is a one of a kind composition of machine, driver and strategy. They drag & drop notes on their tablet, and adjustable robot functions with mixer board volume & fader components resulted in an harmonious symphony.

Eight weeks is a short time to build a fully functional robot. Mentoring and helping other teams, along with meeting their own team’s competition goals, takes extra effort. This team leaps above and beyond in displaying the value of Co-opertition by sharing their knowledge, time and resources with multiple teams in their surrounding area. The Judges’ Award for Co-opertition goes to Team 714.
This roaring team fabricated a robust and quality wiring system that withstands the rigors of competition. These Tigers managed their jungle of wires well and produced a quality robot.
This team is reaching for the stars. Starting as a summer project, they evolved into a full year robotics team. These knights help defend their alliance.
Their robot may seem like just a “Brick In The Wall”, but do not fret, these Demon Ducks have enthusiasm and smiles to span the globe.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Having weathered the storm, with the help of WD-40, this team has found the solution to sustainablity. With the focus on recycling, this group has managed to salvage the resources that others have abandoned. You can really hear the gears turning for this crew.

With four autonomous modes that worked reliably, this team caught the judges' attention. What had judges really hopping with excitement was scoring a note on the rebound while in auto. You'll want this robot DOWN UNDER the speaker!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: It is possible the high altitude led to the creative design of this robot. The judges love their three-camera vision, robust elevator, and an intake that extended. We wish we had built it. Help us go nuts for Euclid because the geometry came together.

Starting with a solid foundation, this team deliberately raised the threat level. Their dead-eye shooting alone is most impressive. Add to that their lift and score strategy, and other teams cry "It's a trap."

This team soared to new heights while helping others. Their talons have grasped and have a firm hold on performance on and off the field. They now perch on the pinnacle of FIRST gracious professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's focus on imagery is obvious in their attire, their robot, and their promotional material. They have a history of recognizing a disease that affects all of us. In memory of their grandmother, they wear pink bowties in the pits, in the stands, and decorate their robot with them.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: We love the fluid design of robot and cart. "Shore," it is good-lucking, but it performs amazingly as well. Of course this vivid team is happy to win, but will be content to be "tide."

This team's control propels with accuracy and overcomes resistance with PFE. The control may put a spin on a note, making music come alive. The driver observes a green light, telling the team the hopper is ready to forge a new chapter.

The deer and the antelope may play here, but there's a new kid in the village. This lynx has discovered FIRST Robotics and is changing the playing field. Judges want to recognize this team with the More Than Robots Award.

Keep this under your hat, but we found a reliable and robust robot, and the lights mean something other than simply being pretty. Admire their pneumatic actuator? So do we! Their autonomous goes in three positions. That robust elevator climber makes us weep purple tears of joy into our food.

This team has impacted the community with clothing and food drives while balancing off-season workshops. They have expanded the number of team members by over 50 percent in the past three years and added more than 20 technical certifications. These students chose to TAKE A CHANCE on their future with FIRST and encourage others to CHIP IN. Stay tuned for the roll out of their children's book.
Bear with us as we describe this golden team. You're not seeing double when you arrive at their pit. Give this team "credit" for their world wide view.

This rookie team embraced FIRST's outreach mission beyond their school. Their effort was expansive and incorporated the engineering design process, emphasizing the iteration process. they satisfied their team's hunger for fulfilling mental health.

This team dispels the myth that lightning never strikes twice. Their thunderous spirit can be felt throughout the halls of Valhalla. These Nordic warriors know how to raise the roof with their enthusiasm.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: From an engineering perspective, this team fully appreciates the concept of garbage in/garbage out. You may be green with envy when learning they scavenged discarded parts throughout their community. You will likely experience a wave of emotions when considering how effectively this team operates in harmony with the environment.

This team’s autonomous code attempts to score four notes. Their programmers impressed the judges with their knowledge learned in Science and Robotics class. This team travelled from their home island to Long Island.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team took creativity to a whole new planet. They poured their hearts into designing unique moving parts, taking a different angle to make their robot roar. Without a doubt, this team’s creation is “magnifique!” (last word pronounced in French)

They demonstrated a thorough engineering process completely documented with measurements and metrics from Cradle to Grave. The Team could clearly speak to all of the disciplines required. They showed us their training logs, their engineering notebook, and had a presentation board that clearly showed the design lifecycle process They could trace all element of the design and showed the analysis and the decision process.

This combined team truly embodies the spirit of Gracious Professionalism. They share resources, reuse parts, and foster new connections better than the ferry between Long Island and Connecticut. We're sure this award is just the start of their path to many crowning achievements.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team transported us with their visuals and imagery, their unique branding helped to define where they’re from. We are off to see the Gecko in France.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s elegant industrial design fuels the power of their robot. Their note conveyance system reflects the efficient and practical designs of professional machines. Like a bodybuilder lifting weights at a gym, their integrated design lifts their robot above the competition.

This team’s programmers developed very sophisticated coding to control their robot, having some software make many decisions during the game play. The team flew to the top of the judge’s list, but they are no turkeys.

This team knows what FIRST is all about: It’s not about winning; it’s about trying. It’s not about size; it’s about spirit. And if “at FIRST” we don’t succeed, we don’t give up. We keep on trying, because that’s how we learn.

In a league where engineering marvels clash and compete, one team’s machine has proven to be as tough and reliable as their namesake. This team didn’t deflate under pressure; instead, they built a robot that could go the distance, play after play. With a nod to their namesake’s legacy, but with a unique flair for innovation and quality, the Quality Award is spirited away by none other than team 6423, the Ward Melville Iron Patriots!

Reaching out, near and far, they work “TOGETHER” with many teams, as they “soar” both internationally and in all “50 states”. Whether it’s summer camp classes, their podcast, or mini-grants, they spread the values and lessons of FIRST as they SPREAD THEIR MIGHTY WINGS.

This year’s teams took us on a ride. They brought us to Canes, showed us how to get our head in the game and even took us on a world tour. Our teams showed us the importance of global outreach, giving back to our local communities and teaching the next generation the importance of STEM. This team looks toward the future, ensuring that the next decade of leaders are set up for success. They met with elected officials and school leaders to implement programs that will help their FIRST team for years to come. This team showed us the importance of laying a good foundation. It was a WILD ride but we found our way back home.

While this is the first year we are meeting this innovative Rookie team, we believe this will be the beginning of a long, successful history in the making. Their diverse and inclusive team impressed us with their teamwork and commitment to the core values of FIRST. With incredible guidance and mentoring, they are ready to stand on their own. We know this team will inspire and amaze us in the years to come.

This team is not stealthy in their pursuit of the FRIST Core Values. They are often seen on the prowl for new members and promoting FIRST in their community. Their panther claw marks show their belief in their mission.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: They were well prepared with their documentation, training, record keeping, to sustain their team into the future. They have dedicated a lot of their heart into recruiting through helping and growing their FLL and FRC teams. They have a SWOT analysis to make improvements. In lieu of bake sales, they championed a drink fund raiser. The were featured in Newsday for their SHE initiative to increase women in STEAM.
They zip and zoom around the field with ease 3...5...7... notes stand no chance against thee Limelights shine and guide the way In green they are seen; in autonomous they are the ultimate dream.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their robot's compact slides reflect a keen eye for engineering. Creativity shines through in every aspect, from the strategic placement to the seamless operation. But it's the trolley mechanism that sets them apart, a stroke of genius in functionality. For this display of ingenuity, we give the award for creativity

Their thought process demonstrates excellence. Their robot displays simplicity and elegance. Their shooter can't pivot, but that's ok, they designed it that way! All season long they've been busy, with changes to little Izzy, planning, CADing, and building evermore Congratulations Team 6-9-4!

Despite being a bird of prey, These raptors supported their fellow flocks in play. Helping fledgling teams in their nests, by volunteering 4500 hours and being their best. They’re spreading the wings of teamwork and STEAM Providing tools, expertise, and inspiration to dream. Swooping in to donate 6o+LEGO kits to empower FLL teams.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Repping their community, this team's branding is fire They use their energy to explore and inspire Across robots and banners, sweatshirts and hair ties Local art imagery makes everyone unified On their robot, they tagged all their friends Their graffiti theme will Inspire New Trends

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This large team was able to amp it up, with a clean and flexible design they climbed to the top This team is in shape to shoot for the sky, where beautiful birds tend to fly. Making a big robot sturdy is no simple ordeal, but they pulled it off because they're birds made of steel!

Everyone took note when they created music in the field, Human and machine, reliably scoring points when other teams wouldn’t yield Their redundant approach in their design Made sure their notes were always aligned They knew right away their design robustness' role This is why the Sciborgs win Innovation and control

In a competition fierce and tight, where skills and spirits soar and ignite. One team rose, heart pure, and bright, aiding others in their flight The judge's took note, and thus they wrote, a commendation that felt just right For spreading FIRST's creed without any greed, let's celebrate Team #1880 tonight.

What makes a quality bot is its ability to mitigate risk, through easy access to vital components and an abundance of redundancy. This team prioritizes durability, so when they get hit in the field, they don't sweat it; and if they do, you wont smell it! When it comes to their checklist, they can mark this one down. If you see them around town, they'll be wearing their quality crown!

Their word carries far and wide not just winning competitions but building community is their pride The transition to Java which increased their reach, for which they traveled far and wide to teach O-boy, did they inspire in English and in Spanish, their pizza all-nighters got them to the finish.

This team has made the most of FIRST, and FIRST has made the most of them. Notably, 100% of the team seniors are pursuing STEAM majors. They are expanding the FIRST footprint by assisting, mentoring, and supporting numerous teams at all levels, in New York, the USA and overseas, including India, Australia, Mexico and Columbia… They have partnered with various organizations and corporations, including Optimum and Develop Africa, to donate STEAM kits and provide mini-grants to numerous FIRST teams around the world. Their outreach is both extensive and effective. They exemplify FIRST, including in social media, and at events they run and attend. The team has run an annual competition in March and invites other regional FRC teams to participate. The team provides a suitable game field, entirely constructed of wood, from their carpentry team. They have established and supported “FIRST Together” as a great stepping-stone for uniting the FIRST community and gaining greater outreach and impact around the world. This team is well orchestrated where the clinks of gears and the hum of motors compose a symphony of innovation!

This rookie team started with just Lego bricks, getting inspired at a young age with all their tricks. In high school they found their space to start a team; their scrappy approach has brought passion to STEAM

With enthusiasm, their ambition flies, aiming high with excitement in their eyes. They've carved their way to competition Fueled by pie and boundless passion Witness the beginning of an inspiring journey, with Team #9509

As a team member said, "Life is boring without challenges" They are a small but mighty team, for whom, setbacks don't matter They are here to learn, make friends and get better Spreading positivity, resiliency, and STEM enthusiasm

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: In green pursuits, they clearly lead, with STEM kits sown from recycled seed. They've taught with care, both near and far, STEAM tools in hand, they raise the bar. With every lesson, tool, and kit they weave the future, bit by bit. In teaching, giving, they unfurl, a tapestry for a sustainable world. In deed that spark, both act and thought, the change is made by binary bots.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.script: Consistent scoring during autonomous mode is what makes this team stand out Knowing its surroundings and positioning with precision is what this team is about You may be a young team, but you have learned a lot Bringing gaming controller design and function into your robot As you enter year 3, it’s obvious to us that you’ll be a team that’s hard to stop

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: In the realm of play where strategy takes flight This team used formulas and calculations to wield their might They crafted and selected each part until they were sure they got it right With steel gears that grind at 400 to 1, this robot climbs before the match is done

This team brought the competition with their Clean Green Machine. They crossed every “T” and dotted every “I”, attending to each fine detail of their excellent machine. We recognize this team for their most professional design and thorough execution.

When this team noticed friends having issues and not singing a happy tune, they quickly jumped in to make sure others got on the field. This team helped with everything from mechanisms to programming, and by loaning parts and people. They boogied down and cheered like Yankee Stadium when their friends were successful, so let’s give THEM a big cheer for their exceptionally Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Mixing engineering and artistry is key to this award, and your focus on music, women, and audio makes you stand out. Raising the voice of women makes your team impressive without a doubt. Your all girls team and your “Penguin Prince” is leading the way. Your passion for women in engineering is here to stay.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Form, function and efficiency are the rule of the day. This team's bot features an integrated design with multi-functional components. Their robust design process showcases an elite understanding of industrial design principles, as well as material selection. In-house manufacturing encourages learning and enables the creation of custom components such as their standout herringbone gears.

Looking for the note past the stage and crowd of robots, this team developed systems to marry their machine and human operators. Innovative switches, sensors and diodes combine to form a seamless feedback loop connecting islands of information. Always in control of their IRON creation, these PATRIOTS use technology to their unique advantage.

This team stood out and stood up. They impressed the judges in many areas, with their teaching and outreach, gracious professionalism, engineering organization and quality. For this team, it might be rocket science: they improve our experience, perform with proficiency, and embody our values with all-around excellence in all things FIRST.
O is for Outstanding B is for Best O is for Optimum T is for Tested Thoroughly S is for Superior What does that spell?

This team has a connector so clever it spins on its own axis because these stars Can-Can. Need some parts? This team launched a retail hub. Their innovation lets their country’s teams shop around. But where is this team? Just about everywhere! You can find them in Africa, South America, the Middle East and Europe. Most of all, this team has changed the face of FIRST in England.

In a world thirsting for change, this beacon shines brightly, empowering over 9,000 community and refugee girls with the keys to unlock the future. Their efforts extend beyond the classroom, breaking societal barriers and nurturing a generation where girls and young women see no limits to their ambitions, leading by example in the global arena of technology and innovation. Let’s applaud the relentless dedication and transformative impact of this team, who stands as champions not just in competition, but in creating a more inclusive, empowered world for females in STEM.

With the heart of FIRST is a team full of glee, inspired by RI3D and their experience with FTC. Two schools united, their spirit so keen, young but robust they embody the FIRST dream. Built through all-nighters, CAD and machining they explored. This team’s dedication leaves us wanting more. Their robot Friedlander is a tech marvel for sure. They have so much passion it’s not easy to ignore.

Throughout the rough-and-tumble of the competition, this team and their robot kept smiling. Their enthusiasm extends beyond the competition and builds a bridge to their community. You can really see with their googly eyes they cared, with their slogan “safety should be shared”.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team isn’t just cool, they school new techies and turn trash into treasure with custom, eco-smart parts. They throw open the doors with “Intro to Robotics” classes, sparking little future geniuses. Taking their FIRST love globally by traveling back to their home country to host summer presentations. So, rev up your gears for the masters of sustainable future.

Although many other teams excelled, the roar of this team was loudest. They played a perfect tune in every match, scooping up notes and scoring with precision. They deserve an Encore. Congratulations, Team 1796, The RoboTigers!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: With a limited budget, this team had the blues. Sushi was too expensive, so they rolled their own with 3D printing and kitchen chemistry. Their intake and index rollers are made of OOGOO. Congratulations, Team 6621, Artemis Robotics

This team carefully prepared for competition. Their process was: Design, CAD, Testing, Redundancy, Documentation, ... Repeat! This earned this team their gear necklaces. The Excellence in Engineering Award goes to Team 1591, Greece Gladiators.

This team promotes their programs throughout the community. They are truly gracious professionals who added the “A” to STEM. But their robot “Billy” stole the show. Thank you, Team 3044 “0xBE4”, from Ballston Spa for honoring Woodie.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team stood out, despite blending in. They blasted their trumpets in a thunderous crescendo. They rolled into the competition in style. Congrats Team 1511 Rolling Thunder for winning the Imagery award.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Photon Vision and Auto Aim enabled accurate and high scoring for both Amp and Speaker. Fluid organization and teamwork promoted broad learning among team members. This team’s full simulations were the fertilizer that enabled “Knightshade” to sprout quickly! Congratulations, Team 3173, IgKnighters!
This team set the judges straight about aspects of their engineering knowledge. Their robot can shoot and run without pausing. Oui Oui, this team is from the stars! Congratulations, Team 7605, ASTRO.

The judges were very impressed with this team’s ability to slice through problems with engineering design discipline. They created nuclear bonds with other teams locally and internationally. The Judge’s Award goes to Team 1601, Quantum Samurai

This team migrated north to compete. Their robot moves like an athlete and thinks like a machine. With a safety net and crumple zones, we know it will make it safely back to the City! Congratulations, Team 3419, Rohawks!

This team is making their mark in the community, to which we say “magnifico!” Despite obstacles, they devote their time and resources to spreading love of STEM. Like a true warrior, this team is inspiring engineering in the next generation. Congratulations, Team 1880, Warriors of East Harlem

This team blazes with innovation and purpose, hosting FIRST tournaments and orchestrating workshops in robotics, coding, and engineering. Their success leaves a trail of global STEAM partnerships that ignite imaginations, with impact that resonates far beyond their community. They leave an indelible mark on the landscape of education and innovation as they soar like a Phoenix. Congratulations Team 5993, the Istech Robotics Society.

Their country is known far and wide for its innovative designs. They built a simple modular robot proudly displaying their country colors. They even carried it to competition in suitcases and assembled it in one day. Congratulations Team 9750, E D Robotics.

Laser-cut models explain their robot’s operation. They keep it up with a double-jointed shooter and intake arm, using four belts and cam tensioners. This rookie team and robot are truly Dynamique! Felicitations, Team 9624 Dynamiques College Charles-Lemoyne.
They broke the code of Team Spirit. Their Development, Involvement, and Enthusiasm are contagious. They made us all "See Red" everywhere. We recognize Team 639, Code Red Robotics.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: O, this team has set the standard. Ushering youth programs at their school and their community created a strong foundation for their robotics program. Their district even dedicated “Robot Day” to celebrate and promote STEM programs. Congratulations to Team 4122, the Ossining O-Bots for this year’s Team Sustainability award.

In tune with this year’s theme this team made TREBLE & BASS PRO SHOTS. When it comes to making decisions, their bot isn’t STUMPED because it knows how to BARK up the right TREE. Their unique one-button control method utilized HAPTIC FEEDBACK to quickly get into range and score reliably.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Soaring high in innovations and in the arena, this team’s robot scored in all three goals. From intake to scoring, the notes SNAKED through with success. They are WELL-WIRED CIRCUITS for the Creativity Award.
This team hit all the right NOTES with their approach to design. When DAZZLED by the lights their RISK PLAN allowed them to quickly change their tune. Their documentation is not just a MYTH.

This team WARREN-ts recognition for how they PROPELLED Coopertition and Gracious Professionalism. They did everything from FLIPPING PANCAKES to TRAINING OTHER TEAMS ON SAFETY. This team always Encourages Learning in Technology and Engineering.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Watch out for this team that showcased not only functional design, but aesthetics as well. They took careful NOTE of their bot’s name and proudly donned their COATS, tightly sealing this case. We are proud to announce this team from their CONTAGIOUS enthusiasm and gorgeous design, a reminder that this team is in reality, anything but a HAZARD.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team had a well thought-out and executed design process, following core principles of simplicity and robustness. A UNIQUELY-PATTERNED gear design was light-weight and durable, and the machine was designed with maintainability in mind. This team kept cool under PRESSURE, and there’s no FIGHTING or LOCKING HORNS among this team as the designed a robot that could quickly score. They expertly NAVIGATE their way to harmonizing with their alliance team mates
When you’re out of control and your energy is spiking, this robot has a cure for you. A twist of a wrist is all it takes to reduce your spin in half. You can REACH FOR THE STARS with this team.

Using STEM, this team directly improves the lives of their local community and beyond. They are creating a sustainable multi-language 3D printing program, infused with FIRST core values. With things WELL IN HAND, we know their future is as bright as the horizon their SHIPS SAIL ON.

This team paid special attention to robustness by using solid pool noodles, recessing bearings between aluminum plates, and carrying spare parts. With this robot, even if one side breaks, the team is able to continue competing. If it falls out of the sky where EAGLES fly, its incorporated SHOCK SYSTEM will keep it alive.

This team is working tirelessly within and around their community to bring engineering skills to people of all identities and backgrounds. Their work in DISASTER ASSISTANCE and volunteering with the SPECIAL OLYMPICS is truly inspiriting. These team members PIONEER ways to bring steam to life in Nashville.

This team started off small and has expanded five-fold. Over time they have built a pathway for STEM that includes starting, funding, and mentoring several FLL and FTC teams. They also created opportunities for youth in the OHIO JUVENILE JUSTICE SYSTEM.

Collaborating with their school and other teams in the greater metropolitan area, this team celebrates all that is FIRST… Trying their best and having fun… Unphased by the late arrival of critical components, multiple iterations make a MAGNIFICENT ‘bot

In both regional and national events and competitions, this team communicated the FIRST message and worked to recruit new members while emphasizing HIGHER EDUCATION FOR ALL. Even the metal components are as light as a feather. With PANDAS on their wrists and DRAGONS on their backs, watch them fly into the Future

This team’s spirit is present within the team and in all the areas they touch. Their team culture, alumni network, engagement with sponsors, and community outreach is something to strive for. From hosting open houses, to developing a talent pipeline all the way at the elementary level, you can tell this team’s presence and SPIRIT is felt by their community. They keep their legacy alive by annually dedicating their robot to a passed mentor. Their bright minds are dedicated to helping new immigrants RISE in their new community by building toys for children with disabilities. It’s clear why this team is 45-members strong WITH a waitlist. We are proud to send you home with a Team Spirit award to talk to with the Mayor next time you are on the podcast.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team enables a sustained existence by actively engaging with their whole community to both recruit members and support student growth. Not only that, they strip down their robot to reuse components – No wasted parts And to top it off, it looks like they recycled their melted ALUMINUM to make their PANTS SO SHINY.

This award goes to a team that went above and beyond with adaptable pathing to fill alliance needs. They followed the KISS method and made the judges RAM-member them. ATLAS puts the “A” in Autonomous!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This large team from the Miami Valley is creative in both their robot design and their TIE-DYED SHIRTS. Their unique, sturdy, and well-built shooting mechanism effectively scores in both the amp and the speaker with ease. This team’s name translates to mean “FRIENDS”, which fits this successful community team very well!

This team clearly ARTICULATED their engineering process of prototyping, modeling, and manufacturing. Even though they saw RED when they redesigned their hanging mechanism, they were able to CLIP IN to their new design.

This team’s gracious professionalism screams from the MOUNTAIN TOP with everything they do. Their passion for representing the under is OUT OF THIS WORLD. These MOUNTAINEERS are expanding FIRST’s mission by building a better world, now and beyond…

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is not GREEN to the field of competition and INSPIRES many high schools to join their cause. We traced their path to success after the ORIGINAL MISPRINT stuck in the judges’ minds. Like a curtain streaming service, they play all the hits!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The judges were BLOWN away by this robot’s elegant and effective design. They SHAPED their spin and intake with clean CAD design. Their quick transfer and accurate shooting TOASTED the competition.

On the field, this team SWOOPED in to the stage with their accurate auto shooter and impressive range. Their strong autonomous was definitely in the LIMELIGHT. Just like in their neural network, our CONFIDENCE FILTER increased when we talked to this team. The controls BLEW the trap door and the judges away!

The judges selected this team for building WIRES of connection to STEM partners. They were willing to TAKE A PLUNGE teaching local scouts robot design and build techniques. Grab some COOKIES and HEAD FOR THE BORDER in the BLUE TWILIGHT…

This team has consistent performance because of their SYSTEMS ON and OFF THE FIELD. Their FIRST AID KITS and COLOR CODING has helped onboard new students. Controls enable AUTO-DRIVE ADJUSTMENT and lightning fast pickup & shooting. Their QUALITY is as strong as TITANIUM…

This team spreads the FIRST message, both locally and abroad. They create PATHWAYS into STEM by training Girl Scouts and Mentoring both FLL and FTC teams - even letting the Kids drive their robot. In translating materials for international teams, they demonstrate fluency in teamwork, not just PORTUGUESE.

records.teamName: The Giant Diencephalic BrainSTEM Robotics Team
records.script: This team’s passion for their community and the broader world, really STEMS from their love of FIRST. Their team goes above and beyond the field and CROSSES BORDERS. The scope of their involvement and outreach sets a high bar that creates new PATHWAYS for furthering STEAM in their community and beyond. These BRAINIACS leave an IMPACT with their outreach to disadvantaged communities.

This team travels FAR AND WIDE in search of technical challenges. Not only did they work hard to build a strong robot, they forged strong relationships with other teams. They have combined the spirit of FIRST with the spirit of their namesake, LUBAN.

This team has the TICKET to high DECIBELS of spirit & enthusiasm. Building a CHAIN of partnership and teamwork, throughout their community. This team had us seeing BLUE and YELLOW at their CONCERT TOUR....

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team shows an approach to team building and works together as a cohesive unit. They are SMART WITH THEIR FUNDS and RESPONSIBLE to their environment by reusing robots to build prototypes and sharing parts with other teams. They continue to GROW by attracting prospective students hosting summer camps, open houses, and visiting elementary schools. They are SPREADING the SEEDS in the community - literally - by distributing seeds to attract pollinators.

This team orchestrated a flawless performance, leading the charge with their robots pitch perfect autonomous solos. Their machine guided by vision as sharp as their mascots mountainous instincts, navigated the musical maze, hitting every bit with precision. Their autonomous performance truly RAMS the competition.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When other teams were "trapped," they were covering their tracks. They quickly flexed up to the stage with their boat hook. They are first on the creativity train!
When you go for “everything," sometimes it works out. Fortunately the robot didn’t come out “half baked," because of their ability to climb the stage and push a note. They "mashed" the competition.

If you need help on or off the field they got your back! They were front and center ready to heed the call and share tools and experience. They are in command of Gracious Professionalism! They aren’t Alpha! They aren’t Sigma! They’re OMEGA!!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has masterfully combined attractive engineering and visual elegance, leveraging cold calls and creativity to engage their community. Incorporating "retro-futuristic" technology and aesthetics, they embody the spirit of the Imagery Award. They’ve set a new standard for integrating team and machine aesthetics from the past to the future.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team paddled across the field at high velocity. Their successful robot was simple and good looking with some nice "FLY" wheel brass parts. Their design is all it is QUACKED up to be.

This team engineered a symphony of innovation, seamlessly automating the rhythm of the game with their robot’s intuitive control. They MOOOOVED the boundaries of automation, transforming complex maneuvers into simple button presses, as effortless as conducting a musical masterpiece. This team is a PRIIIIMEEEE example of innovation in control.

Throughout their region and the robotics arena, this team serves as a source of light for all to see. This team has a forte for raising the next generation of FIRST students, being involved in their community, and designing and building a robot that competes at a high level. They have used their turret to spin to the top of a number of categories and are thus awarded the Judges Award!

In the crucible of innovation, where "metal" and "mettle" fuse, more than built—it was masterfully crafted. Edge to edge, amp to floor, it roared with a resilience that resonated excellence in the competitive fray. This bot COMMANDS and withstands the toughest hits.

Their vision system was so advanced it helped them see opportunities to give thousands of people their first FIRST. Clad in turquoise they continue to inspire others every day at their workshop at a museum worth visiting. This team doesn’t play dead! They’re very much alive and well!

This team has been on a multi-year STEAM journey of Impact in their community. Not just of keeping new blood flowing into the team from year to year, but what they're doing in their community and environment. From nearly all the alumni ending up in STEM careers, outreach inside and over the team's international borders, turning old motors into small wind powered generators, turning bottle caps to cancer treatments, and saving water with smart showers, this team is making a GRANDE impact for FIRST and their community. Thank you for sharing your story with us here in Oklahoma. Viva Voltec

This IMPACTFUL rookie team reached out across the plains to inspire young and old about the future of STEM. Even in the cornfield, they stand out above their peers. Their "Tech"nical abilities "Know" no difficulties.

These rookies transform challenges into opportunities with their relentless resourcefulness, diving into dumpsters to find what others overlook. Their "golden" journey here has not only advanced respect for engineering within their community and school but has showcased the profound impact of determination and ingenuity. Their early steps in engineering have already left a lasting mark, proving that true inspiration and success come from the heart of gold and a spirit of perseverance.

Like a well-tuned Mariachi guitar this team gets you rocking from the start. From their pit, team uniforms, and robot this team has the look of a Formula One race car. They'll turn you green with Envy, Red with Live, and White with awe of their Spirit.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team values their teachers, having influenced their school board to recognize them financially. The 10-year plan will result in a robust FIRST edifice — from which all will benefit. Just like Odysseus, this team is on a 10-year epic adventure. THEY ARE TROBOTS!!!

This team is great on the field or in water. Their dynasty has an Auto mode that consistently hits two “notes” in the speaker from up close and flies more notes from mid-field. You better duck when this team is shooting!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team spent the last few years sniffing out new ideas for their custom drive train. Like a musician searching for a perfect riff, cutting their own gears like cords had the judges howling about their creativity. Elvis was wrong as this team is more than just hound dogs.

This team’s members move with intention to reach their many design goals. Their final shell and shooter are masterpieces from many iterations of modeling and tuning. They play to each other’s strengths in a prime chord.

You can see this team helping others. They are an outstanding example of going above and beyond for not only their own team, but all of the FIRST teams they interact with. They don’t hide in the shadows – when help is needed, prowling the pits to lend a hand.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s robot is a great combination of style and function. These pupils really have a googly eye for detail. You’ll never see them “dragon” behind the competition.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: You can see this team from miles away with their standout appearance and their robot to match. They brought their signature color to their smooth pivoting intake. With turret design, you can see music notes flying through the air at the speed of light.

This team’s design twists and packs a lot of sensors into a little space. They artfully combine their visual feedback systems and multiple sensors to shuttle notes from the source to the amp and speakers. Houston, we do not have a problem – we have arrived at the stage.

This team made a black and white decision on how to focus their team objectives. They consciously choose to take on a supporting role in their alliances, focusing on speed, and moving notes to where they needed to be. Reviewing teams from both day and knight, this team has a clear choice for this award.

This mountain team has elevated their quality to new heights. Their quality comes rom using both power motors for speed and pneumatics to do their heavy lifting. From the feet of the Garden of the Gods, this team has built quality and leads the region by example.

This team has taken other teams down the road to success, using their processes and resources to accelerate the reach of FIRST. They’re driven with a unique approach to funding, recruiting, and mentoring. Dressed in black and yellow, their gracious professionalism always comes in clutch.

This year's Impact Award Winner has spent their time looking for ways to drive a focus in their community and around the world by innovating with diversity, reaching the underprivileged, and uplifting women in STEM. This team built a strong foundation through hard work, determination, global vision, and a deep dedication to always reaching out and growing the FIRST brand of STEM. This team has created vassal states in foreign lands and has sent envoys to these lands to share, through technology and boots on the ground, the ideals of Gracious Professionalism and Coopertition.

This team didn’t just dip their toe into robotics – they jumped in. Using their experience as Boy and Girl Scouts, they volunteer to help younger students compete. We expect these Titans to build and expand.

This rookie team casts a shadow highlighting engineering to younger students. You can find them recruiting new team members, planning summer camps, and showing up at all club activities. This house is on fire with power.
This team’s enthusiasm runs through all their events. They multiplied their impact by training coaches. This team isn’t flightless and they don’t keep their head in the sand.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team does it all -- from hosting numerous events to creating and producing award plaques for others, they have built a foundation that will keep them moving for years to come. The work of this team can be found on golf courses, in neighborhoods, and even South Africa. This award will be another feather in their cap.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This team is developing a reputation for exploration and expansion of the FIRST mission. Specifically, they have held community outreach events, developed a website to support students in other schools, paid forward Gracious Professionalism to other teams, and inspired students to harness their STEAM potential. When thinking about this team’s future, the Judges were lovin’ it!

This team had a colossal impact on STEAM in their school and community. They have started rookie teams, run STEAM expos, developed an enormous on-line documentation store, and been interviewed by a world-class fundamental science organization. The Judges were impressed by their enthusiasm of Olympic proportions.

Every team needs to AMPLIFY the FIRST message to their community. This team’s initiatives have impacted many new and returning FLL and FRC teams and have even helped 40 teams re-start since the pandemic. They select outreach programs that are SCALEable to MAKE the LOUDEST and most SUSTAINED impact. They have SHIFTed the BAR for other teams to aspire to. They truly demonstrate that "A Small Team Can Have An Impact!"

We At FIRST Feel Leadership Enables STEM. This team has ORCHESTRATED many FIRST teams at all levels. They have started over 20 teams, launched a 6 week summer camp, and run an online robotics competition. They SING about their online HITS across multiple channels reaching over a million PLAYS. With everything they do, they never WAFFLE.

To achieve HARMONY you need many different voices with a UNITY of purpose. This team has built on their purpose of breaking barriers to bring STEM to those who otherwise would have missed out: from underserved youth, to seniors, to kids with special needs. They have planted seeds with young people to grow strong STEMs across the GTA and internationally. This is a team that's making a difference.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: While this robot might appear unassuming, just wait for it to move. With the multiple autonomous functions, the drive team watched as their robot chased down and scored countless notes. The high speed, automated performance was anything but “low-keyed”!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The winning team took a creative design to enable the robot to hit the target from multiple positions. Their robot is a swift and agile contender with a high-speed turn-able shooter capable of 120 degrees of movement in the heat of competition! In theory, just like an orchestra, every FIRST alliance needs a maestro!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This team built their bot in a flash, their double hook climbing mechanism struck the perfect balance between engineering design and fabrication. They were able to make the best use of their resources by augmenting the engineering design with data driven digital testing and simulation. You could hear the roar of the audience and the thunder clap when they entered the field!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This team worked together and marched their robot into new territories. Their comprehensive stats website amplified other team’s scouting success. They celebrate GP with their ……. Golden Wrench!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This colour-coordinated team has it all; the pits, accessories, design, and more. They have fully integrated the musical theme throughout their robot’s look and feel. Rock on, you purple guitar heroes!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Trekking along the 401, every part of their robot is practically designed, built and tuned to perform. This team stepped up to the challenge by wrapping and unwrapping carbon fiber to rise above the rest.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This team’s unique control, innovative design, precise aim, and impressive autonomous functionality, had them leading the pack. Their robot knew its territory and applied the right control strategy, even when it couldn’t see clearly. Under this innovative control, they secured the Alpha position.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: The Judges award is to recognize impact that reaches beyond this generation. This team has excelled at FIRST outreach that travels the world and is now able to travel in time to inspire the next generation. These cats have created a beautifully illustrated book written for young children that tells the story of FIRST core values, ensuring their tale will never be extinct.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This team and machine took the competition head-on, withstanding the endless battles with a robust machine right down to the clean and neat wiring. Ramming their way through the matches.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This team was started by a bright group with a passion for Engineering. In a very short time, this team has shined their light on others by sharing their field, creating a parts database tool, and spreading the word of FIRST. This group of young women and their unicorn inspires others to follow in their blazing pink trail.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This team had the energy and resilience to conquer any challenge it faced. Changing their whole design process and building their robot in days, they cranked the volume from 0 to champion. No room, no tool, NO PROBLEM!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: These green warriors really got moving on realizing their potential. Navigating through the trees they helped plant by the lake, working with local partners to recycle their metal, and guided by an environmental roadmap, this cohesive team ensures their long-term viability. Inspiring robot enthusiasts in their community they encourage these young technologists to join their merry band. The true knights of sustainability…

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This team’s 2 point scoring was so automatic the judges wondered if they were watching the NBA. Their unique and consistent Autonomous feature left the crowd Amped Up. Their sensing and positioning system allowed them to Charge to a top 8 finish!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s field success should certainly leave them flying high. Their unconventional but effective robot design can double their options for note collection. The team’s innovative achievements will really be a feather in their caps.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This well-organized horde exemplified excellent engineering practices, allowing them to attack the challenge presented by the game. Their meticulous documentation, innovative design and multidisciplinary team structure really helped them steal many victories on the field. Their high spirits and sunny bright uniforms belied their team name.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: There was no opposition or mystery about the selection of this team among the judges. We heard time and again from multiple competitors about this team's genuine gracious professionalism. When you have a problem, this team will turn your paradox down side up.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: An immaculate pit and fitting theme, this team has imagery that has never been seen. This team has a Wild imagination. Imagine a phantum of the FRC!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Like in nature, this team was able to adapt continuously and their members worked well together to overcome challenges. This team's material comparison and precise stress analysis lead to a compact and efficient robot. Their robot defends its territory and vacuums up all its prey.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This team is a giant in the field of control. Their methodical approach identified the performance of all aspects of their robot, enabling reliable navigation, aiming, and shooting. The judges were tickled pink to see this team in action.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: From Country days to City nights they are making connections for FIRST. This team has developed a unique social application engage the FIRST community. These BLOCKHEADS have used their social marketing to support the values of FIRST.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This team’s clean wiring and design kept their robot out of the flames. The meticulous workmanship and robustness ignited the judges admiration as they soared above. Leaving a blazing trail of excellence in it’s wake.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This team roared onto the field like the grand-masters of inspiration. The team showed exceptional design, flawless organization, and practiced environmental sustainability.Their forward thinking will lead them to a royal-following.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This team displayed team spirit but also focused on the core element of safety. As the judges approached the pit the flock landed with enthusiasm. Listen for the team that quacks the loudest!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team scouts for new members while following their plan. They blend their environmental and outreach activities to spread the word of FIRST to rural and urban communities. This is a sheep of a different colour!

For their autonomously managed robot operations, we present the team that hit all the high notes. They got their math right, their physics line up, and they programmed their way into winning this award.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The Judges came across a creative element that enhanced this team’s strong event ranking. Their focus on neural processing is an excellent FRAMEwork for expanding FRC’s capabilities. They say that it takes 10,000 hours to truly learn a skill, but sometimes 10,000 images will do the trick.

While this team is no stranger to their school, their presence has also resonated across the country. Their passion for robotics extends beyond FIRST in designing community-based projects, including – believe it or not – saving a one-legged chicken!

This team was exceptionally strong in areas that go far beyond their excellent performance on the field of play. The Judges were impressed with the depth and extent of their outreach efforts, openly sharing their many resources both on local and global scales. In this regard, the winning team are true titans.

This team gets amped up when they talk about their professional design. Independent mechanisms allow them reliable intake and note-dunking. Celebrating victories old and new, it’s an honour to watch this team STORM the platform.

This team was recognized by Judges and pit staff alike for their gracious professionalism. They are true ambassadors of FIRST, actively recruiting those with less-than-ideal STEM experiences to show them what inclusive collaboration is all about. You’ll need a Nimbus 2000 to catch this golden snitch!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team managed to integrate their artful natural inspirations into the visuals of their booth. This is nicely complemented with amazing outerwear and buttons. They came from afar to open our eyes to the beauty of the Earth.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Judges love the aesthetics of every robot here, yet we can’t forget about functionality. This team balances both, with every bolt, plate, and wire placed with intention. The elegance and efficiency of these systems working together had major RAMifications for the game.

This team in blue came up with a unique way to handle the challenges of the game. Their use of omni-wheels allows for optimal intake and shooting. They are able to smoothly control the notes to make them soar.

While deliberating, our Judges had EYES for this team’s innovative approach to programming and tuning. They brought their robot to life both on and off the field through their detailed renderings and simulation. Despite this team once visiting Valhalla, like bold Vikings they journeyed back from the valley.

When others were patching their bumps and bruises, this historic team’s robot stood tall. You could say that they are armoured up in quality. Their clean build of solid blue and yellow was able to withstand the test of time.

Like a precious metal, inspiration for this small team was mined from the FIRST community. They process their interest, skills, and passion, ALLOYING themselves to rise to the challenges of FIRST robotics competition.

This team puts the “A” in STEAM and in outreach with fundraising efforts in their school. They even served their bake-sale goods on minibots! These young rookie titans managed to inspire a passion for STEM in their art school.

This team’s spirit was evident through all facets of FIRST. Their enthusiasm in talking to the Judges in the pits was contagious and their mascot in the stands was on fire. They also had to merge two teams into one, which must have been a devil of a challenge!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team nurtures the Earth with their carbon calculator and book for long-term team and environmental sustainability. Flying overhead, they drizzle sweetness over the world. With their apiary and vegetable garden, they are buzzing leaders of Team Sustainability.

This team’s use of vision tracking sensors and driver feedback LEDs result in a robot that plays Crescendo with incredible proficiency. Their autonomous mode makes picking up notes look easier than picking fruit from an orchard in the summertime. Some might even call them ……. Over-Powered!!!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team imagined a creative new way to score in the trap. In the end game, this impressive lifting mechanism had had their opponents saying OH NO! It had the judges saying OH YA!

This team takes a fearless and diverse approach to outreach and collaboration in the spirit of strengthening the field of competition. They fertilized young minds through the development of multiple learning programs and they collaborated with new teams to make them more prepared for competition. With impactful programs like “Gears, Gizmos and Girls”, and their Academy, they impressed judges to the Max

This team began their “Symphony” over a decade ago and has been consistently making beautiful music ever since. They spread the message of FIRST through local and international mentorship of FLL, FTC, and FRC teams. A small team by FIRST standards, their Impact is “Amplified” through effective partnerships, outreach, and advocacy with their local school board, hospitals, and feeder schools. The final “Flourish” to embellish their Impactful performance is their co-hosted off season event, which has helped to grow FIRST in Ontario. Get ready to “Shift Octaves”, as they complete their “Crescendo of Impact”. Let’s all join this model team in their mission to promote appreciation and participation in STEM. Let’s ALL “MAKE THE SHIFT” with this year’s FIRST Impact Award winner, MakeShift Robotics!

This team had a design as clever as ACME products and an arm that had the judges on the moon. Their design process featured significant prototypes, documentation and replaceable parts. The team’s hunt for engineering perfection really deserves a loud howl from the crowd.

This team impacts their community on and off the field. They were able to reach thousands of the next generation through on-line events, as well as reaching out to an older generation off-line You can call them for a part. You can call them for help. Just don’t call them late for BREAKFAST!!!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This is a team that has united FIRST’s blue and red colours. Through their pit, outfits, and robot, they exemplify an outstanding integration of their team colours. The judges couldn't believe that even their mascot has its own colour palette. Merge your hands together in a round of applause for this winning team!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: They fly through the field with elegance and grace. Sensors help them glide and grab while LEDs give their driver ‘enhanced vision’. Smart speed controls even help reduce tipping. Judges were impressed with their sleek and simple design. This robot was truly ON FIRE

This team identified and described a unique control system for all motors that integrated into their team strategy and was reliable when put to the test. This system design enabled maximum speed and reliability while optimizing motor performance. One might go so far as to say that their motor controls were orchestrated like a BEALTOVEN masterpiece.

This is a team that has seen incredible growth in both their team size and in building global connections. With their integration of students with many different languages, and their implementation of an international youtube channel, there are no circuits that this team can’t connect. Say Hi to Mom.

This team froze out the competition with their solid robot. They designed a robust robot with an overall focus of reliability and quality that had the judges thinking “cool, cool,cool”. This amped up robot should win the chromium award in quality.

This rookie team of…………Bears??? stepped up to the mic with no signs of stage fright! Their initiative to “change the now” paves their way to environmental and future team sustainability. The judges were very impressed with their maturity and ability to so quickly embrace the ideals of FIRST.

This is a team that has so much enthusiasm that when you speak to them about FIRST, it makes you want to dance. From designing their own mascot, to community outreach and timeless outfits, this team never seems to run out of “steam”. Their green monster will power them to success!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: The judges were amazed at how the winning team integrated elements of team sustainability in an environmentally sensitive manner. This team used scrap metal and wood parts to craft toys and ornaments with younger students while introducing them to STEM. They SWATTED away waste while fueling their team’s future.
This team picks up notes that steer them in the right direction. Their robot uses a camera vision system which utilizes AI acceleration. This is a team that hit all the right notes.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s lighting system is impressive but also enhances their play. Their intake ensures the note is the “perfect pitch”, and the lights signal when the shooter arm is ready to fire. While it isn’t their name, this team is really the ‘salt of the earth’.

This sweet team impressed the judges with their commitment to environment sustainability and STEAM. They spread the message of FIRST through their environmental template, their carbon calculation, and their coding workshops across the region. These Robo Friends are sure to inspire you!

Leading with a vision to make FIRST accessible to everyone, this team continues to add to the FIRST Orchestra. Building a Crescendo of impact beyond their community and home province of Ontario, they have supported the development of FIRST teams and events in further reaches of Canada. Finding advocates in various levels of government, this team maintains that network, ensuring national advocacy of the FIRST program. Making an impact not only on all levels of FIRST - FLL, FTC, and FRC - they also have a lasting impact on their team members, being the key to open the door to many opportunities. A long standing FIRST team, they maintain their partnerships and seek out new ones expanding on their legacy. Making a home for FIRST in the ICY north, this team has not only made their world bigger, but also made the FIRST community bigger!

Don’t get it twisted, this team understands how to excel in engineering. Their direct drive shooting really put a spin on team engagement. This team’s approach will leave the competition shivering in antici…………. -pation. Let’s do the time warp again with…

This team came to the aid of other teams in need. Their long-distance mentoring and support with financing, parts, and playing field provided the resources for other teams to compete. If your team is in need this team is quick to DOC-tor you back to health.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When you see this team approaching you will feel the rhythm and blues. Their use of colour will make you purr with excitement. They are very strong in the imagery CATegory so…

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team invested capital in a design process featuring milestones and sign-offs. Their vision was to build a modular, plug-and-play robot, joining form with function. And they rocked it! Shhh!! She’s at the library!

This team redefines the teamwork required between them and their noble steed. Their vision system can identify not only their target, but also competing robots. Their innovative control system takes over at the push of a button.

This team creates harmony between art and science. Honouring the past, they illuminate their boundless spirit for continued growth. The judges were struck by their commitment to excellence, resonating through their community, and blooming into the future.

Their commitment to excellence is truly electrifying. Designed with precision manufacturing, their robot’s sturdy build ensures it can climb to new heights. They really charged-up their build quality.

This rookie team really tightened the bolts to create a robust team. They had a clear design strategy for their robot that helped them to be a strong team player. We heard from Shania Twain; this team does impress her much!
This team dug deep to create a strong team this year. The way they put science and teach learning FIRST was River-ting [riveting]. They are creating the next generation of innovators.
This team SOARS in their community and their school. Spirit flows through them, and can be felt throughout the venue. They are notoriously dressed in red, so please put your spirit hands together.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: The judges feel that this team crushed it. Their extent and breadth of community outreach and involvement is brilliant. They are quietly building sustainability and shifting perception of STEAM in the right direction.

This team's effective use of every tool and sensor made their robot so independent all they needed was a button!
